Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.

title: From Sheep to Loom: Diné Weaving Traditions
location: SRJC Multicultural Museum - Santa Rosa Campus
description: For the Diné, weaving is considered a ceremony. Creating a single blanket requires many steps, including shearing the sheep, cleaning, carding, spinning, and dyeing the wool, and then finally weaving. It can take hundreds of hours. This exhibit features rugs from the SRJC Multicultural Museum's collections, featuring award winning woven rugs such as a fine "Burntwater" style rug by the great Nellie Roan and many other examples of Navajo rugs from the 1920s through the 1970s.More information available on the SRJC Multicultural Museum website. (https://museum.santarosa.edu/)

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: SugarShuttle: Sugarloaf ↔ Hood Mountain Regional Park, Pythian Rd
location: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
description:
Shuttle also offered on Sunday, September 6.

**How it works**: Every half hour, our Shuttle will leave from either Sugarloaf Ridge State Park's Visitor Center (making a brief stop at the Goodspeed parking lot) or Hood Mountain Regional Park’s Pythian Rd parking lot (with a brief stop at the equestrian lot). Make a reservation to ride to the other end of the trail and begin your hike, or hike and ride back. We recommend riding first and hiking back to your car afterward– no worries about how long you take to finish your adventure. The hike should take 3½ to 4½ hours depending on your pace; the distance is about **7.4 miles one-way** with **approximately 2,300ft of elevation gain**. 

Bring at least 64 oz of water, sun protection (the majority of the trail is exposed), a good paper map (some of the trail signs on Hood Mtn Regional Park are still damaged from the 2020 wildfire and trails might not be well marked), and if desired, hiking poles, a friend, and a lunch.

If you are riding from Sugarloaf, the Goodspeed lot fills up quickly. If it is full, please park at the main lot and pick up the shuttle at the Visitor Center (you will have to hike a mile back to the main lot from the bottom of the canyon/Goodspeed lot). If the Hood Mt. Pythian Lot is full, please park at the Equestrian Lot, by the Hood House, in Los Guilicos.

title: Apple U-Pick at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
location: Gold Ridge Organic Farms
description:
**Our popular Apple U-Pick Experiences return for a second year!**

Experience the magic of harvest season at Gold Ridge Organic Farms, where you can hand-select the most flavorful Honeycrisp or Fuji apples straight from our certified organic orchard.

Timed entries from 8:30am. Last orchard entry at 11:30am.

Admission: $8 for adults, $3 for children. Registration required.

U-Pick apples: $4 per pound.

**Apple U-Pick FAQs** 

Do I need a reservation? 

Yes! Please reserve your time slot on our reservation site. Reservations help us ensure everyone has a wonderful experience without overcrowding.  

Can I show up without a reservation? 

We require reservations to maintain our capacity limits and ensure everyone enjoys their visit to the fullest.  

Can I cancel my reservation?  

Absolutely! You can cancel your reservation up to 48 hours before your scheduled time by calling us at 707-823-3100. Please note that cancellations made less than 48 hours in advance will result in forfeiture of the entrance fee. 

Can I bring my dog?  

Dogs are not permitted in the orchard, with the exception of service animals. This policy helps ensure the safety and comfort of all our visitors. 

Can I bring a stroller into the orchard?  

For safety reasons, strollers aren't allowed in the orchard, but you're welcome to leave yours at the check-in area where it will be safe and waiting for you!  

I require mobility accommodations. Can I still pick apples in the orchard?  

Yes. Please call us on 707-823-3110 once you’re made a reservation and we can provide suitable transportation into our orchard.

Why is there an entrance fee?  

The entrance fee helps us maintain our beautiful orchard and keep our experienced staff on hand to ensure everyone has a safe and enjoyable experience. 

How much are the apples?  

Our delicious U-pick apples are $4.00 per pound.  

What variety of apples will we be harvesting?  

You'll be picking either Honeycrisp or Fuji apples (depending on seasonal availability).  

Can I harvest heirloom apples?  

While heirloom apples aren't available for U-pick, we offer many wonderful heirloom varieties for purchase in our Farm Shop.  

Are your apples organic?  

Yes, all our apples are organically grown and certified annually by Oregon Tilth!

title: Jack London State Historic Park WILD Trail Challenge
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
On Saturdays from Sept. 5 to Oct. 3, Jack London State Historic Park’s WILD Trail Challenge returns for a third year.  This series of five hikes covers every trail in the park for a total of 39.5 miles.  The hikes increase in duration and/or difficulty each week.

Participants can sign up for individual hikes or do them all.

The price for each hike is $15.  The park entry fee of $15 per vehicle is waived for these hikes.  Those who sign up for all five hikes before Sept. 5 save 20 percent and pay only $60.

Hike \# 1 – Historic Trails

September 5, 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m.  

A great way to warm up. This hike explores the historic sites and trails of the park. Navigate both sides of the park to discover Jack London’s Beauty Ranch, London Lake, and the Wolf House ruins.

Easy – moderate hike \(approximately 4.5 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 2 – Ancient Redwood

September 12, 9 a.m.-1 p.m.   

Meander through the redwoods and sunny oak woodlands of the park’s three Bridge Trails \(Upper, Lower, and Fallen\). The journey leads to the majestic ancient redwood, fondly known as the Grandmother Tree.

Moderate hike \(approximately 6 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 3 – Historic Orchard

September 19, 9 a.m.-1:30 p.m.   

Start Location: Note that this hike does not begin at Jack London State Historic Park

Sonoma Developmental Center

Arnold Dr, Eldridge, CA 95431

Stroll along the blue shores of Fern Lake before reaching the Historic Orchard. Learn about the history of the land and the fascinating fruit-bearing crops that thrive there.

Moderate – Difficult hike \(approximately 7 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 4 – Ridge

September 26, 9 a.m-3:30 p.m.   

Details: Hikers will gain elevation and an appreciation for the diverse habitats found within the park. They’ll also traverse part of the ever-growing Bay Area Ridge Trail.

Difficult hike \(approximately 12 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 5 – Summit 

October 3, 9 a.m.-2:30 p.m.     

A trek to the park summit is the perfect way to complete the WILD Trail Challenges.  Climb Sonoma Mountain to enjoy stunning views, celebrate with fellow hikers, and become a WILD One.

Difficult hike \(approximately 10 miles roundtrip\)

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting
location: Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan. 

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: "Paddle The Petaluma: Turn to The River" Guided Kayak Tour
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
Paddle the Petaluma: Turn to The River is a relaxed, beginner-friendly guided kayak tour exploring the past, present, and future of Petaluma’s historic waterway. Launching right from downtown at The Floathouse Petaluma, you'll take part in this Sonoma County Signature Experience by spending about 90 minutes on the water in stable sit-on-top kayaks, traveling a gentle mile-and-a-half route through “Petaluma’s Longest Park.”

Along the way, you’ll raft up at docks around town, fascinating  landmarks, and riverfront gathering spaces to hear stories about how this Gold Rush-era “saltwater highway” helped shape Petaluma—and how today’s community is continuing to reinvent and reconnect with the river. This isn’t just a history tour. You’ll also learn about the people, businesses, artists, nonprofits, and river advocates helping shape the waterway’s future right now.

Everything is included in the $75 experience: kayak, gear, knowledgeable local guides, insider river stories, and post-paddle perks at nearby businesses. Finish with plenty of time for brunch, coffee, shopping, or simply hanging out downtown by the water. No experience necessary.

Note: The Floathouse Petaluma is a nonprofit project dedicated to “putting butts in boats and smiles on faces” by offering year-round easy access to the Petaluma River in and on people-powered water craft through rentals, events, classes, lessons and summer camps.

location: Sonoma Community Center
description:
Saturdays Weekly · 4 Weeks

Date & Time

10:00 AM – 1:00 PM

Location

Room 208

Printmaking

Beginning

Ages

18 and older

In this special four-week workshop, participants will explore the unique art of reduction relief printmaking. Acclaimed guest artist, Tomoko Murakami, will demonstrate how to create multi-color prints from a single linoleum block. The main idea is to gradually carve away parts of the block and print each new layer of color, with each layer building on the previous one. The course covers the entire process, from designing and planning, to carving techniques, inking, registration, and printing with both hand and printing press methods. Participants will learn to explore the possibilities of color mixing and layering, enabling students to achieve intricate designs and a wide range of visual effects. You will gain an understanding of the materials, processes, and innovations involved in this unique form of relief print printing!All levels are welcome, including continuing linocut students. Please note: This class requires hand dexterity to maneuver the carving tool. Participants should feel comfortable standing, and using tools with sharp blades and edges.

title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. \(707\) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    www.upstairsart gallery.net 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: OAEC Garden Tour
location: Occidental Arts and Ecology Center, 15290 Coleman Valley Rd, Occidental, CA, 95465, United States
description:
Join us for a guided tour of the Occidental Arts & Ecology Center’s demonstration gardens and living landscapes. Led by rotating OAEC staff, these tours offer an opportunity to explore our diverse food, medicinal, pollinator, and native plant gardens while learning about the ecological principles that guide our work. 
When: Tours start at 1pm every first and third Saturday of the month, April through October. 
Where: Tours start and end at the OAEC Nursery. 15290 Coleman Valley Rd, Occidental, CA 95465. Upper Driveway. 
Important Information:
No registration required—just show up!
Please use the second driveway and park in the upper lot near the greenhouses.
The tour route includes steep hills and unpaved dirt and gravel paths. Sturdy shoes, a brimmed hat, and weather-appropriate layers are recommended.
If you require mobility support or have other accessibility needs, please call ahead so we can accommodate you. Monday–Friday, contact the main office at (707) 874-1557 ext. 101. 
A highlight of every tour is the OAEC Nursery, a nonprofit nursery dedicated to uplifting ecologically and culturally important plants. The nursery features a wide selection of perennial food crops, medicinal and native plants, and an ever-evolving collection of annual vegetables and herbs adapted to our region.

title: South Pacific
location: 6th Street Playhouse
description:
**An unforgettable romance set against the sweeping tides of World War II.**

Against the backdrop of the Pacific War of WWII, ***South Pacific*** blends high-stakes wartime romance with a poignant exploration of social prejudice. When spirited Navy nurse, Nellie Forbush, falls in love with a sophisticated French planter, and a young Marine lieutenant finds himself captivated by an ethereal island girl, their relationships are tested by the prejudices and pressures of a world at war. What unfolds is a deeply moving story about love, courage, and the transformative power of understanding. Featuring a soaring score by **Richard Rodgers** and **Oscar Hammerstein II**, including classics like “Some Enchanted Evening” and “There Is Nothin’ Like a Dame,” *South Pacific* remains one of the most beloved musicals of all time.

Winner of the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the original Broadway production won ten Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Best Score and Best Libretto. It is the only musical production ever to have won all four Tony Awards for acting.

SOUTH PACIFIC is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of The Rodgers & Hammerstein Organization. concordtheatricals.com

Performances run Thur, Friday, Saturday evenings at 7:30pm and Saturday and Sunday matinees at 2:00pm.

title: BELONGINGS: Bringing Memories to Life
location: Petaluma Historical Library and Museum
description:
A Creative Workshop on Memory, Grief & Storytelling Facilitated by Filmmaker Danièle Wilmouth

Saturday, September 5, 3-6 pm

Petaluma Historical Library & Museum

20 4th Street \(Corner of 4th & B Street\)

Registration:  $30 per person

• Limited to 12 participants

• Light snacks will be provided.

What do we do with the things our loved ones leave behind? 

Join award-winning filmmaker Danièle Wilmouth for an intimate, three-hour workshop exploring how meaningful objects can become powerful vessels for memory, healing, and creative expression. 

Drawing from her own artistic practice, Danièle will share how she uses photographs, letters, family documents, music, treasured objects, and stop-motion animation to honor loved ones and transform personal stories into lasting works of art. 

Participants are invited to bring one to three meaningful objects that hold a special memory or story. Through film excerpts, guided conversation, and creative brainstorming, you’ll explore ways to preserve family history through storytelling, writing, journaling, archival materials, and simple stop-motion animation techniques. No filmmaking or artistic experience is necessary—just curiosity and a willingness to reflect. 

Whether you’re looking to preserve family memories, process grief, or discover new creative ways to tell your story, this workshop offers a welcoming space for reflection, connection, and inspiration. 

This workshop is presented in conjunction with Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind, on view September 4–October 4, 2026, at the Petaluma Historical Library & Museum. The exhibition explores migration, memory, and belonging through the treasured objects and personal stories that connect us across generations. 

Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind is made possible through the generous support of California Humanities through its Connecting California grant program. We are also deeply grateful to our community partners and sponsors, including the North Bay Asian American Pacific Islander Coalition, Sonoma County Japanese American Citizens League, Petaluma Arts Center, Life on Art, Zimbabwe Cultural Exchange Project of California, El Día de los Muertos Petaluma, Bolca Avia, Chelsea Antiques, Café Puente, Rustic Bakery, Quality Inn Petaluma, and all of the organizations, volunteers, artists, and community members whose collaboration has brought this exhibition to life.

title: Callie Watts
location: Fogbelt Brewing Company
description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. Over time, she’s had the honor of opening for acts such as Bootsy Collins, Elvin Bishop, Huey Lewis and The News, War, Ozomatli, Bill Champlin, Booker T, and the B52s. Callie continues to perform frequently as an acoustic solo artist, focusing on developing a core audience and a buzz for her original material. title: Mike Annuzzi
location: Konocti Harbor Resort
description: If you spent just a few minutes with Mike Annuzzi, you would become aware that his positivity towards life is contagious. Mike is always smiling. He is honest and expresses his feelings openly, probably because he is a Capricorn.  Surrounded by the inspiration from his favorite tour locations, this California native maintains a blend of laid back coastal attitude, hustle of the big city life, drive of Silicon Valley, and refinement and sophistication of wine country.  Mike started playing guitar and writing songs as a child. After the encouragement from friends throughout his high school and college days, he formed and fronted several bands. He discovered his passion in life on a stage performing original music.  He is not the typical Polytechnic University graduate who landed a tech job in Silicon Valley, rather he sewed his roots and paved a path with a musical career. Mike wrote and independently released The One \(2016\), Mike Annuzzi \(2013\), and Paradise \(2012\). In 2013, Mike was chosen West Coast Songwriters International Song Contest Singer/Songwriter of the Year for his single, “Pay No Mind.” He also received Honorable Mention for “You Make Me Fall.” Mike's first single “Paradise” was chosen as West Coast Songwriters San Francisco’s Song of the Year in 2010. His award-winning catalog has been featured on radio around California.  With over 500 shows around the US in the last 3 years headlining clubs, supporting national touring acts, and developing residency performances for venues around California, Mike established himself and his positive rhythmic sound on hometown stages and beyond. He finds himself grateful to have a career around his passion and knows it is attributed to the support of his family, friends, and fans.  Mike is always looking forward, developing his craft as a songwriter and performer, and sharing his positive energy and passion at live shows.  Some stages Mike has been humbled to perform:  BottleRock Napa Valley 2014 with headliners The Cure, Outkast, and Eric Church \(Over 80k tickets sold\) The Mountain Winery, Saratoga CA \(Historic Santa Clara Valley 2k Seat Capacity Outdoor Venue\) The Catalyst, Santa Cruz CA \(Iconic Music Venue host of acts from Neil Young to Nirvana\)  Some of the artists Mike had the opportunity to play events and share stages with include:  Los Lonely Boys \(Single:  “Heaven” Top 20 Billboard Hit\) Kenny Wayne Shepherd, \(“Blue On Black” reached \#1 on Rock Charts\). Colbie Caillat \(Universal Republic Records, Grammy Award Winning Artist\) O.A.R. \(Vangaurd Records\) Edwin McCain \(Singer/Songwriter with Billboard hits including “I'll Be” and “I Could Not Ask For More”\) Lukas Nelson \(Promise of the Real\) Jackie Greene \(Singer/Songwriter and Member of The Black Crowes\) Tyrone Wells \(Independent, iTunes top 10 album artist\)   Here is what others are saying about Mike:  “He sings honestly and expressively and the writing shows sophistication.” -Paul Freeman, Mercury News  “Mike Annuzzi was a pleasure to watch...I loved the positivity of the songs and how full of joy Mike seemed to be filled with.” -Cadet Edac:  iheartsfbands.com  “Well, listening to this wonderful artist it is clear that listeners are in for a treat. His voice is divine and the smoothness of the whole thing just makes me feel alive and gearing to go! Perfect! -Skye McAdams:  The Daily Complains  “Check out this rising star.” -Glen Starkey:  New Times SLO, San Luis Obispo  Mike Annuzzi Plays Godin Guitars Silicon Valley Based Singer/Songwriter, Positive & Rhythmic Music and Lyrics. description: England, 1605: A terrorist plot is brewing to assassinate King James 1 and blow Parliament to kingdom come! Or so the King claims. To spread his propaganda, King James 1 hires the world’s most famous playwright, William Shagspeare \(after a contemporary spelling of the Bard’s name\). As Shag investigates the King’s bizarre tale, he begins to question it, leading him and his actors to a dilemma: lie and pocket the cash, tell the truth and literally risk their necks, or perhaps equivocate–lie and tell the truth at the same time. This high-stakes thriller drops into many of the Bard’s most famous works in an alternate history that resonates today. This is a witty and poignant ensemble piece in which six actors play well over a dozen roles, some of which include snippets of Shakespeare's other plays-in-progress \(one of which becomes the famous Macbeth.\)

title: macbitches
location: The Raven Performing Arts Theater
description:
“macbitches takes Shakespearean themes and grounds them in a recognizable, modern reality — a smarter, theater-centered Mean Girls, if you will. It’s funny, sharp, and unafraid to let women be complicated.” - Jeanette Seisdedos, director

macbitches takes a darkly funny look at the toxic, high-stakes world of university theater, centering on a freshman who unexpectedly lands the role of Lady Macbeth. The play centers on freshman acting major Hailey, who unexpectedly scores the coveted role of Lady Macbeth. Her upperclassmen rivals immediately invite her over to “celebrate.” As the Fireball and Svedka flow, the young women interrogate their own ambitions as well as the power structures that have shaped their education—and when the night spirals into violent and shocking acts of betrayal, they come to learn that what’s done cannot be undone.

\*Content Advisory: Strong profanity, physical and psychological violence, heavy substance abuse and underage drinking, discussions of mental illness and sexual misconduct, and themes of betrayal and suicide. Recommended for mature audiences 16+.

Written by Sophie McIntosh

Directed by Jeanette Seisdedos

Running Time: 90 minutes with no intermission

title: TajMo - Room On The Porch Tour 2026
location: Green Music Center
description: TajMo Taj Mahal & Keb’ Mo’ Room On the Porch Tour 2026 Saturday, September 5 at 7:30 p.m. Tickets $45–$254 Weill Hall \+ Lawn TajMo - the historic collaboration between two generations of American music masters, Taj Mahal and Keb’ Mo’ – will bring their Room On The Porch Tour back on the road in 2026 with more than 15 live shows across the United States. Recorded in Nashville with Keb’ and Taj co-producing, the Grammy-nominated Room On The Porch finds the pair in peak form, playing to each other’s strengths and opening up new creative horizons more than a half-century into their storied careers. The songs are warm and inviting, rooted in the joy of human connection and the power of positivity, and the performances are as timeless as they are adventurous, incorporating the full spectrum of American roots music from blues and jazz to folk and country. Keb’ and Taj invited an all-star group of players, singers, and co-writers \(including their sons\) to join them in the studio for the sessions, but the spotlight remains firmly fixed on the legendary pair throughout the collection, their instantly recognizable voices and guitar stylings complementing and elevating each other at every turn. The result is a delightful, big-hearted work that manages to feel both classic and current all at once, an album rooted in deep tradition delivered by two icons with a boundless appetite for growth, reinvention, and discovery.  Though the two only began recording together as TajMo in 2017 the pair’s creative relationship \(and mutual admiration\) stretches back decades. Supported in part by Freeman Vineyard & Winery. Info & tickets at https://gmc.sonoma.edu/tajmo

title: Wolfpack Anniversary
location: HopMonk Tavern
description:
Immersed in the global electronic music scene, RON REESER has earned support from luminaries like Tiesto, Don Diablo, Fedde Le Grand, Kaskade, and Loud Luxury to name a few. His signature Tech House sound consistently infiltrates DJ sets across the globe.

An American DJ and producer, RON REESER, originally hailing from the vibrant backdrop of the San Francisco Bay Area, boasts an dynamic discography that spans esteemed labels such as Sony, Ultra Music, Sirup, and Pyro Records. Notably, his remix catalog features an array of renowned artists, including Billie Eilish, Dua Lipa, Coldplay, Doja Cat, Chainsmokers, Coldplay, Kaskade, Galantis, Chromeo, and more. These sonic creations have reverberated on charts, both in the United States and the United Kingdom, with a resounding presence on Beatport and iTunes.com.

Recent singles such as "Goodies" graced the airwaves and were given the prestigious spotlight on Pete Tong's BBC Radio1 mixshow, captivating an audience of over 4 million European listeners. Simultaneously, "Lights Off" illuminated Tomorrowland's One World Radio, casting its spell across the global soundscape. His earlier creations, including "Everything" featuring Myah, "Above All" featuring Sylvia Tosun, and reimagined versions of Deadmau5's "Raise Your Weapon" and Jes's "Awaken," ascended to prominence, consistently dominating the airwaves and clinching the number one spot on Sirius Radio's BPM charts, securing his position as the second most-played artist, just trailing behind the legendary Kaskade.

Fast forward to 2025, where RON REESER's momentum continues to surge. With two electrifying Top 20 Billboard Dance singles, a fresh TV mix show syndication on Music Choice reaching over 2 million viewers monthly through Xfinity Comcast, a monthly residency on iHeart Radio, and Wild 94.9's House Music Mixshow "Ghetto House Radio," syndicated across 47 stations in the United States, and "Higher," on Pyro Records \(Germany\) amassing 20 million\+ combined streams on all all platforms including Spotify.

Stay tuned and visit WWW.RONREESER.COM for more info on releases, tour dates, news, live sets, podcasts, and more.

title: SugarShuttle: Sugarloaf ↔ Hood Mountain Regional Park, Pythian Rd
location: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
description:
Shuttle also offered on Sunday, September 6.

**How it works**: Every half hour, our Shuttle will leave from either Sugarloaf Ridge State Park's Visitor Center (making a brief stop at the Goodspeed parking lot) or Hood Mountain Regional Park’s Pythian Rd parking lot (with a brief stop at the equestrian lot). Make a reservation to ride to the other end of the trail and begin your hike, or hike and ride back. We recommend riding first and hiking back to your car afterward– no worries about how long you take to finish your adventure. The hike should take 3½ to 4½ hours depending on your pace; the distance is about **7.4 miles one-way** with **approximately 2,300ft of elevation gain**. 

Bring at least 64 oz of water, sun protection (the majority of the trail is exposed), a good paper map (some of the trail signs on Hood Mtn Regional Park are still damaged from the 2020 wildfire and trails might not be well marked), and if desired, hiking poles, a friend, and a lunch.

If you are riding from Sugarloaf, the Goodspeed lot fills up quickly. If it is full, please park at the main lot and pick up the shuttle at the Visitor Center (you will have to hike a mile back to the main lot from the bottom of the canyon/Goodspeed lot). If the Hood Mt. Pythian Lot is full, please park at the Equestrian Lot, by the Hood House, in Los Guilicos.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Meeting
description:
Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.

In OA, members experience spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery by practicing the Twelve Steps and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

Overeaters Anonymous \(OA\) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person meetings at 9:30 on Sunday mornings at Church of the Nazarene, 18980 Arnold Drive, Sonoma, CA \(a small room directly off of parking lot; look for the sign posted\) and newcomers are always welcome.

You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does not endorse any specific food plan. 

Visit: https://www.northbayoa.org/

Find a meeting: https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: "Paddle The Petaluma: Turn to The River" Guided Kayak Tour
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
Paddle the Petaluma: Turn to The River is a relaxed, beginner-friendly guided kayak tour exploring the past, present, and future of Petaluma’s historic waterway. Launching right from downtown at The Floathouse Petaluma, you'll take part in this Sonoma County Signature Experience by spending about 90 minutes on the water in stable sit-on-top kayaks, traveling a gentle mile-and-a-half route through “Petaluma’s Longest Park.”

Along the way, you’ll raft up at docks around town, fascinating  landmarks, and riverfront gathering spaces to hear stories about how this Gold Rush-era “saltwater highway” helped shape Petaluma—and how today’s community is continuing to reinvent and reconnect with the river. This isn’t just a history tour. You’ll also learn about the people, businesses, artists, nonprofits, and river advocates helping shape the waterway’s future right now.

Everything is included in the $75 experience: kayak, gear, knowledgeable local guides, insider river stories, and post-paddle perks at nearby businesses. Finish with plenty of time for brunch, coffee, shopping, or simply hanging out downtown by the water. No experience necessary.

Note: The Floathouse Petaluma is a nonprofit project dedicated to “putting butts in boats and smiles on faces” by offering year-round easy access to the Petaluma River in and on people-powered water craft through rentals, events, classes, lessons and summer camps.

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: Love and Grit: Balancing Self-Compassion and Strong Determination
location: Spirit Rock Meditation Center
description:
with Cara Lai and Matthew Brensilver

On the Dharma path, no single teaching is sufficient to guide us. Awakening comes from holding the dynamic tension between two equally important, apparently contradictory teachings.

Is it possible to have great self-compassion without losing our strong determination? The Buddha relentlessly highlights the importance of persistence and resolution on the Dharma path. Progress comes through perseverance. Simultaneously, we know that this path simply cannot be walked without great love and self-compassion. Some tangles cannot be untangled through striving—they require gentleness, love, and forgiveness. How do these two forces fit together?

During this daylong, we’ll explore the two sides of this dialectic and illuminate a path that fully honors both. The day will include guided and silent sitting meditation, walking meditation, Dharma talks, and conversation between Cara and Matthew. We’ll have time for dialogue and questions as we trace out a path of effort and care.

Mike started playing guitar and writing songs as a child. After the encouragement from friends throughout his high school and college days, he formed and fronted several bands. In 2013, Mike was chosen West Coast Songwriters International Song Contest Singer/Songwriter of the Year for his single, “Pay No Mind.” He also received Honorable Mention for “You Make Me Fall.” Mike's first single “Paradise” was chosen as West Coast Songwriters San Francisco’s Song of the Year in 2010. Mike is always looking forward, developing his craft as a songwriter and performer, and sharing his positive energy and passion at live shows. title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: Nothing To See Here - Jason Perry
location: Mare Island Art Studios
description:
"Nothing To See Here" is a critical, yet playful examination of the UFO phenomenon that is hinged on the dynamic between serious scientific inquiry and fringe science.

With a mixed media approach that combines drawing, collage, and painting, Jason Perry seeks to entice the viewer into the work through familiar visual iconography, bold colors, expressive marks, and textures. Once there, the viewer is offered a deeper layer of meaning to consider. Perry calls into question the blurred narratives, misinformation, and potential truths surrounding the UFO topic.

At its core, "Nothing To See Here" invites us to look a little closer at our beliefs, our relationship to the strange, the unexplained, and our enduring fascination with what might be out there.

title: Tomales Festival
location: Tomales Community Park
description:
The Tomales Festival will be held at High Noon on Labor Day Sunday, September 6th. Join us in the Community Park \(in between the Catholic church and the William Tell House\) to celebrate with friends and neighbors. This year we're featuring music by the Blues Defenders, plus fresh oysters, beer, wine, food, and drink. Local arts and crafts, plus displays from local organizations and non-profits.

The festival is \(and always has been\) created, organized, and carried out by volunteers from the local community. This local tradition has quite a history: it was the Swiss-Italian celebration from 1888 until 1994, when it became Founder's Day and later the Tomales Festival. That's 138 years worth of parades, picnics, and parties. This event benefits the Tomales Town Hall, which is a 501\(c\)3 non-profit community center.

Special thanks to Kathryn LeMieux for once again allowing us to use her whimsical cow painting as our festive logo. And thanks to our contributors. The Hog Island Oyster Company and The Marshall Store contributed the shellfish. Morris Distributing is providing our beer supply. Recology Sonoma/Marin is providing trash containers and is donating garbage service. We are grateful to our sponsor Marin Agricultural Land Trust \(MALT\).

Sign ups for volunteers, exhibitors, vendors, and more right are currently available. Write to festival@TomalesTownHall.org or see the website: https://www.tomalestownhall.org/tomalesfest. Booth reservations end August 15th.

Participants will explore the process of collage making using magazines images on 5” x 8” canvas, usually cut from mat board or other stiff paper. title: Equivocation
location: Spreckels Center for the Performing Arts
description: England, 1605: A terrorist plot is brewing to assassinate King James 1 and blow Parliament to kingdom come! Or so the King claims. To spread his propaganda, King James 1 hires the world’s most famous playwright, William Shagspeare \(after a contemporary spelling of the Bard’s name\). As Shag investigates the King’s bizarre tale, he begins to question it, leading him and his actors to a dilemma: lie and pocket the cash, tell the truth and literally risk their necks, or perhaps equivocate–lie and tell the truth at the same time. This high-stakes thriller drops into many of the Bard’s most famous works in an alternate history that resonates today. This is a witty and poignant ensemble piece in which six actors play well over a dozen roles, some of which include snippets of Shakespeare's other plays-in-progress \(one of which becomes the famous Macbeth.\)

“macbitches takes Shakespearean themes and grounds them in a recognizable, modern reality — a smarter, theater-centered Mean Girls, if you will. It’s funny, sharp, and unafraid to let women be complicated.” - Jeanette Seisdedos, director

macbitches takes a darkly funny look at the toxic, high-stakes world of university theater, centering on a freshman who unexpectedly lands the role of Lady Macbeth. The play centers on freshman acting major Hailey, who unexpectedly scores the coveted role of Lady Macbeth. Her upperclassmen rivals immediately invite her over to “celebrate.” As the Fireball and Svedka flow, the young women interrogate their own ambitions as well as the power structures that have shaped their education—and when the night spirals into violent and shocking acts of betrayal, they come to learn that what’s done cannot be undone.

\*Content Advisory: Strong profanity, physical and psychological violence, heavy substance abuse and underage drinking, discussions of mental illness and sexual misconduct, and themes of betrayal and suicide. Recommended for mature audiences 16+.

title: South Pacific
location: 6th Street Playhouse
description:
**An unforgettable romance set against the sweeping tides of World War II.**

Against the backdrop of the Pacific War of WWII, ***South Pacific*** blends high-stakes wartime romance with a poignant exploration of social prejudice. When spirited Navy nurse, Nellie Forbush, falls in love with a sophisticated French planter, and a young Marine lieutenant finds himself captivated by an ethereal island girl, their relationships are tested by the prejudices and pressures of a world at war. What unfolds is a deeply moving story about love, courage, and the transformative power of understanding. Featuring a soaring score by **Richard Rodgers** and **Oscar Hammerstein II**, including classics like “Some Enchanted Evening” and “There Is Nothin’ Like a Dame,” *South Pacific* remains one of the most beloved musicals of all time.

Winner of the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the original Broadway production won ten Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Best Score and Best Libretto. It is the only musical production ever to have won all four Tony Awards for acting.

SOUTH PACIFIC is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of The Rodgers & Hammerstein Organization. concordtheatricals.com

Performances run Thur, Friday, Saturday evenings at 7:30pm and Saturday and Sunday matinees at 2:00pm.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting in Santa Rosa
location: Christ Church United Methodist
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: Soundscape Listening Walk California Biodiversity Day 2026
location: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
description:
As many as a quarter of California’s species exist in this compact area, a place that comprises only a tenth of 1% of California’s entire land area!

Join Jack Hines (host of the Ear to the Wild podcast on KRCB/NPR) as he sets up his high-tech audio equipment enabling participants to listen in greater detail to the summer evening soundscape as part of of California Biodiversity Day. This will be a quiet, meditative hike, where we will spend most of our time listening. We will start with a short hike (<1 mile) to a quieter location where we hope to hear owls and other summertime sounds such as the Common Poorwill. After setting up the audio equipment, we will listen quietly for ~45 minutes. Feel free to bring a portable chair in a bag. Meet at the White Barn parking area. Tickets are $15 for general audiences, $7.5 for students, youth (12-17 year olds must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian), Sugarloaf  members, Sugarloaf or RFO volunteers, and free for children 11 and under. **Tickets day-of on site are $20 and might not be available** Wear appropriate footwear for trails. Bring layers, sun protection, at least a quart of water, and if you desire, a snack. Parking fees apply.

This event is part of California Biodiversity Day 2026 along with others hosted from September 5-13. Throughout this week, individuals, communities, and organizations will host in-person and virtual events to inspire discovery of our state’s remarkable nature, while encouraging everyday actions to protect and steward it. View the power of community science in action!
source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat, Visit Santa Rosa

location: The Meritage Resort and Spa
description:
Babyface is a 13-time GRAMMY Award-winning recording artist, songwriter, producer, and one of the most celebrated creative forces in music history. He is the only producer to win the ‘Producer of the Year’ category four times, three times of which was in consecutive years \(1995-1997\); a record he holds to this day. Kenny is also co-founder of the legendary record label LaFace, which launched the careers of artists like Usher, Toni Braxton, TLC, Outkast, and P!nk.

 

From humble beginnings in Indianapolis, Kenny developed his love for music early on when he began songwriting at the age of 12. Upon graduating high school, he got signed to his first record deal after joining the band, Manchild. In the 1980s, he broke into the music world as guitarist and songwriter for the R&B band, The Deele.

 

Artistry:

Over the past five decades, he released three consecutive multi-platinum albums: Tender Lover \(1989\), featuring the \#1 “Tender Lover”; For the Cool in You \(1993\), which included “Never Keeping Secrets” and “When Can I See You”; and The Day \(1996\) featuring “Every Time I Close My Eyes.”

 

In 2014, he collaborated with Toni Braxton and released the GRAMMY Award-winning album

Love, Marriage & Divorce. Babyface has written and produced hits for artists like Bobby Brown, Boyz II Men, Eric Clapton, Madonna, Beyonce, Bruno Mars, Ariana Grande, Mary J Blige, Celine Dion, Aretha Franklin, George Michael, Michael Jackson, Justin Bieber, Phil Collins, Janet Jackson, NSYNC, Chaka Khan, Anita Baker, Faith Evans, Jay Z, Stevie Wonder, Chris Brown, John Mayer, Lionel Richie, Michael Bolton, Kenny G, Lil Wayne, Luther Vandross, Barbara Streisand, and countless others.

 

Most recently Babyface won his 13th GRAMMY Award for Best R&B Song for “Snooze” by SZA. Additionally, Babyface received nominations in two other categories: Best R&B Album \(Girls Night Out,\) Best Traditional R&B Performance \(“Simple” by Babyface & Coco Jones off his Girls Night Out album.\)

 

On July 15th, 2023, Babyface’s latest single “As a matter of fact” reached \#1 on the Billboard Adult R&B Airplay chart. The song is his first \#1 solo single in 26 years. Download / stream “As a matter of fact” HERE.

 

On October 21, 2022 Babyface released his new project, Girls Night Out, which features the legendary singer/songwriter/producer’s collaborations with some of today’s brightest female R&B stars, including Ella Mai, who is heard on the first single, “Keeps On Fallin’,” which was GRAMMY nominated for Best Traditional R&B Performance and took the \#1 spot on the Mediabase R&B chart. He also teams up with Ari Lennox; Kehlani; Queen Naija, Coco Jones; Tiana Major9; Tink; Baby Tate; Muni Long; Amaarae; Sevyn Streeter & Tkay Maidza; Doechii and Angie Martinez & Lala Anthony. Download / stream Girls Night Out HERE.

 

Currently Babyface is working on his 12th studio album.

 

Awards:

Babyface has contributed to over 800 million records sold and over a billion records streamed. He has produced and written 125 Top 10 Hits, 45 number 1 R&B hits, and 16 number 1 pop hits. In addition to winning a total of 13 GRAMMYs, he has been nominated 83 times.

 

Throughout his career, Babyface has won the BMI Pop Songwriter of the Year trophy seven times, received a total of 51 BMI Awards, as well as 4 American Music Awards, 5 Soul Train Awards, and 5 NAACP Image awards.

 

He also produced and co-wrote the Oscar winning song “When You Believe,” sung by Whitney Houston and Mariah Carey.

 

Achievements:

In 2024, he was inducted into The Apollo Walk of Fame and received the inaugural Legacy Award from The Apollo Theater. He was also honored with the BMI Icon Award at the 2024 BMI R&B/Hip-Hop Awards. 

 

In 2017, he was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame.

In 2013, he received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

In 1999, Kenny’s home state Indiana named a highway after him.

Charity:

Babyface is a passionate philanthropist, actively supporting the Carousel of Hope, which benefits the Children’s Diabetes Foundation, the Barbara Davis Center for Childhood Diabetes, Larry Ruvo’s “Keep Memory Alive,” and Stand Up for Cancer.

 

In 2023 he partnered with the non-profit organization Music Will to launch music programs in 20 schools in his hometown of Indianapolis, IN.

 

In the past, he has also lent his support to FasterCures, VH-1 Save the Music, United Negro College Fund, the David Foster Foundation, and the Mike Milken Prostate Cancer Foundation.

Fundamental practices for understanding the holistic nature, energetics and Sanskrit yoga philosophy guiding the approach of this comprehensive system. Long time yoga practitioners as well as new students will benefit. Experience the distinction of this system verses other modern yoga/vinyasa practices commonly taught & the traditional & precise use of ujjayi breath as it relates to the Sanskrit parameters, moving with the breath and the importance of the pause. Talasana is a very unique & profound krama initiating & establishing "samasthiti", the steadiness and focus of mind, balanced energy and steadiness of body - with the two feet together, moving from the center, all the major joints and muscles of the body are exercised using arm and hand movements, back bends, side bends, twists, forward bends, squats and balancing foot stretches. The fingers interlaced create a prana circuit as they come together in the repetitive movement over the head. The breath specific movements stretch the diaphragm, psoas, massage the heart and internal organs, clear the lungs, drain the lymphatic system, stimulate the vagus nerve and calm the mind. Energy is created along the spine and central nervous system, and is distributed throughout the nadis and into the entire energy body. Regular practice of Talasana flowers into to ananta samapatti and understanding "stillness in movement".
Class begins with Opening Mantras & Ding Namaskar (Devotional Salutation to the Directional Spheres with Breath & Mantra). Then moves to Tāĺāsana to Savasana then Seated Prānāyāma (Yogic Breathing) including Morning Cleansing Kriyas, Ujjayi, Nadi Shuddi, Samantraka Prānāyāma, Pratyahara, Dharana. title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

is a yogi, mother, artist, ceremonialist and lover of life. She has been practicing and teaching yoga and meditation for 30 years and offers yoga retreats and trainings that center on optimum health, self realization and self love. Her teachers are from many yoga and tantric traditions, but her primary lineages are Iyengar and Kali Ray.
Tirza is deeply devoted to community building and is honored to have created a number of community supported non profits including Mystic Family Circus and The AWAKEN Project, which serves families with children on the autism spectrum. Tirza is proud to be the mother of 3 wild teenagers, including her incredible son who is diagnosed with autism.
Tirza’s spirituality is one of many influences and teachings. Beginning with a Christian up-bringing and being raised on a Christian commune in her early childhood, she later expanded into more earth-based ways. While in her 20’s Tirza was adopted into the Native American Church, where she learned from her relatives a way of living the “Beauty Way.”
During the 1990’s and early 2000’s, Tirza lived in San Francisco, Oakland and Berkeley, directing the Mystic Family Circus, which was a performance group dedicated to cultural awareness and bridge building. She worked with Cirque du Soleil, Burning Man, Reclaiming, Contraband, CELLspace and other Bay Area art collectives and non profits to provide conscious entertainment and “prayerformances” for the betterment of humankind and the planet.
In 2012, Tirza helped to found the Buckeye Gathering, an ancestral skills gathering in Northern California which draws teachers and students of all ages to learn ancestral ways of tending the earth and survival skills.
Tirza Dawn was the founder of yoga programming and the Ayurvedic Yoga Teacher Trainings at the dhyana Center of Ayurveda in Sebastopol, California, which operated a community center of healing and education from 2010 to 2020.

title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: Lavender Labyrinth Sound Bath Experience
