description:
Join us in our most dreamy location yet, in the center of a lavender labyrinth for an exquisite sunset sound Bath Experience!

Join us in our most dreamy location yet, in the middle of lavender labyrinth at sunset!

Mondays through October 6th

We are thrilled to share this magic with you! Let the fragrance of lavender fill and sooth your senses as the sound expands your awareness.

Sound baths create the space for self-healing and transformation. The resonance of the instruments is not just an auditory experience ~ it's like receiving a full body sound massage.

There will be 8 Gongs, Crystal singing bowls, Hand pan, Mono chord, Chimes galore, Ocean drum, Native drum, Angelic Vocals & more.The vibrations will transport you on a powerful healing journey!

PLEASE NOTE: The sound bath starts at 7pm. Gates close at 6:45 PM. Please be Mindful of timing. You will need time to park, walk up and set up. You are welcome to come walk the labyrinth and visit the Farm Stand from 6 pm onward. Please check the hourly weather so you are prepaired. You will be lying on the grass, so please bring all that you will need to feel cozy and warm, "yoga mat" or camping pad, "Blanket" or sleeping bag, a pillow, eye mask, and water bottle. Wonderful Lavender Eye Masks will be available to purchase for $25 by the Bees & Blooms Farm Stand.

If we have environmental Circumstance such as rain or unhealthy air quality due to fires we will postpone to Wednesday of the same week and your tickets will roll over to that day. If these conditions are present it is your responsibility to monitor your emails\(also junk/spam\) for notifications. In these force of nature situations Tickets are not refundable but are transferable! Your understanding and cooperation is greatly appreciated.

Please be informed that there are bee hives on site and there may be bees on the lavender plants. If you are allergic to bee stings, bring your Epipen. An incident is unlikely, but best to be prepared. Also, at some point, probably mid July the Lavender will began to be harvested so there may be less lavender towards the end of the month.Full Bloom occurs mid June. The last sound bath of the Lavender season will be Oct. 6th. The labyrinth & farm will be beautiful however the Lavender will be reaching the end of its cycle around mid. July. You will walk through many rows of a varity of blooming flowers on you way from parking.

Only disability trained Registered Service dogs are permitted because of the animals on the farm and the nature of the Sound Bath. Your understanding is appreciated. Also, please no children under 10 years of age.

Labyrinths represent a metaphor for your life path and the journey you are making. While walking the path of the labyrinth, either alone or with a group, focus on your feelings and emotions to allow you to connect with yourself. You may also want to choose a meditation that you are comfortable with in order to clear and quiet your mind. The uses of a labyrinth are many; relief from stress and anxiety, healing, meditation, problem solving, enhancing intuition, expanding thought processes, communicating with the Divine, balancing mind, body and spirit, letting go of unwanted energies, obtaining goals, celebrating and remembering others, building trust in yourself or others, and coping with grief, sorrow and loss. The labyrinth is an ancient symbol that relates to wholeness. It combines the imagery of the circle and the spiral into a meandering but purposeful path. The Labyrinth represents a journey to our own center and back again out into the world. Labyrinths have long been used as meditation and prayer tools.

Looking forward to sharing this Extraordinary Experience with you! In Gratitude

title: Poetic Medicine: 09/08/2026 — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Poetic Medicine: 09/08/2026

Tuesday, September 8th, 2026; 4:00 – 5:30pm$15.00Max 20 Attendees, Pre-registration required(We are unable to offer refunds or transfers for this class. If you cannot attend, please consider it a donation. Thank you!)The practice of “poem making” offers a means to express the metaphors and meaning of the joys and suffering we experience in ourselves and bear witness to in others. Poetry can be a salve for the heart and soul. It is a way of speaking what is true in our hearts and is often difficult to access without a creative spark. You do not have to be a "poet" or even a "writer" to allow words and feelings to pour through your pen.Redwing Keyssar has been leading "poetic medicine" sessions through her work in Palliative Care at UCSF for the past 5 years. Her work has created an international community of people who, by listening to and writing poetry together, have healed wounds of grief and loss, helped "wounded healers," and provided resiliency to move forward on our life paths.Writing poetry in community is a bit like attending a meditation retreat. The instruction for most beginners when learning to meditate is to simply bring oneself back to the breath, each time the mind wanders. In poem-making, the instruction is to bring oneself back to the heart and along with a deep breath, see if one can open a little bit wider. When we witness each other in this process, in a circle of open-heartedness, something magical happens!This is an IN-PERSON gathering to establish a strong and safe creative community. We are all poets!About the Instructor: Judith Redwing Keyssar, RN has traversed an amazing 35+ year journey in the healing arts/healthcare. Redwing is an educator, end-of-life doula, author, poet, song-writer, ceremonialist, national presenter and frequent contributor to public issues about Palliative and End of Life Care. Redwing is currently the Director of Education at the MERI Center for Education in Palliative Care at UCSF/Mt. Zion. Her professional career includes being the Clinical Director at Zen Hospice Project and the Director of Palliative Care and Nursing at Jewish Family and Children’s Services from 2004-2018. She is a founder and adjunct faculty member of the California State University Shiley/Haynes Institute of Palliative Care, and has taught courses at OLLI at Sonoma State. Redwing is the author of an award-winning book, “Last Acts of Kindness; Lessons for the Living from the Bedsides of the Dying” and is the recipient of numerous awards in the field of Palliative Care. After studying with John Fox at the Institute for Poetic Medicine, her passion for using poetry as a healing modality has led to the development of a successful international program in Poetic Medicine, through her work at the UCSF MERI Center. title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: Watercolor | Building Technique II, with Nancy Ballard

description:
Building on the skills and confidence you developed in the first class, this watercolor workshop invites you to take your ideas a step further. Explore how a simple sketch, thoughtful composition, and expressive use of color can transform an idea into a finished painting.

We'll work larger and bolder while exploring watercolor techniques including:

Wet-on-wet paintingLoose interpretation and expressive mark-makingCreating shadows and depthEnhancing backgroundsWorking in black and whiteExploring the many variations and possibilities of mixing greens

Bring a favorite photograph, a live flower or small plant, or even a meaningful memory to use as inspiration. No matter where you are in your artistic journey, you'll be encouraged to experiment, have fun, and focus on the larger picture rather than striving for perfection. There are no mistakes in art—only opportunities to explore.

Please Note: There will be a $10 supply fee paid directly to the Nancy on the day of the class.

Nancy's classes sell out quickly and we only 16 spots available, so reserve your spot now!

 If you've taken Nancy's Gentle Watercolor workshop, this class will build on the skills and techniques you've already developed. If you're new to the series, you'll find a welcoming, supportive environment where you can jump right in. All experience levels are welcome, and you'll be guided along the way.

Nancy Ballard's love of art began in childhood, when she first discovered the magic of brush and paint—a sense of wonder that continues to shape her work today. After a full life as a mother, grandmother, and corporate professional, she returned to art following her retirement in 2006, studying watercolor with Mary L. Harden at Strybing Arboretum. In 2009, she was recognized as a Master Artist of Botanical Illustration by the San Francisco Botanical Garden Society. Nancy has also worked as a gallery curator and exhibiting artist throughout the Bay Area, sharing her botanical work in galleries, wineries, hospitals, and nonprofit spaces while supporting environmental awareness through art.

title: Let’s Tap! Beginner - Advanced on Tuesdays
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Welcome to the wonderful world of Tap!
These classes are for those who wish to discover tap dance and those who wish to continue exploring.
This class offering is weekly on Tuesdays in six-week sessions. Three levels are taught: Beginner from 10:15-11 AM, Intermediate from 11 AM - 12 Noon and Advanced from 12:30-1:30 PM. Summer Session starts Tuesday, September 8th and ends Tuesday, October 13. Additional classes can be taken on the same day for $5/class (pay on site).
Classes are led by
Starr Hergenrather and Gabe Copeland
. A limited supply of
tap shoes is available for use at the class.
Please contact us ahead of time to ensure we have the right size for you.
Participation fee is $120 for the series (six sessions), $90 for OCA members.
You can
email us
with any questions, or come to a class.
Register
Tap Dance provides an avenue for developing coordination, balance, musicality, rhythm, and general love for movement. We will learn the basics (if a beginner) and beyond, through warm-ups, discover the language of tap dance, learn the Shim Sham, and routines that will launch you onto your own exploration of the dance form.
Tap is an extremely fun and rewarding form of dance. Tap Dance originated in the 19th century through a fusion of African and Irish dance styles, becoming a unique American art form in the melting pot of New York City. It developed through percussive footwork, initially on plantations and in urban cellars, and later gained widespread popularity through minstrel shows, vaudeville, and Hollywood musicals. Innovators like
Bill "Bojangles" Robinson
, the
Nicholas Brothers
, Eleanor Powell, Fred Astaire, Gene Kelly to name just a few, who shaped its evolution, which continues today with new fusions in contemporary dance.
May 26
, Bojangle’s birthday, is National
Tap Dance Day.
Starr Hergenrather
has been teaching Theatre and Dance for over 54 years, dancing for 70 years, which is amazing since she is only 45 years old! She received her Theatre Arts and Teaching Credentials in 1971 from Denver, CO. Starr has taught theatre/creative dramatics/improvisation/dance to all ages and directed and produced theatre for many, many years. She and her family moved to Sebastopol in 1983. In 1987, she received her Dance credential and degree from SSU. Starr loves the theatre and dance and everything about them. She has performed on stage and in film throughout her teaching career. Before joining the staff at Analy in 2001 where she became the Theatre Arts Program Director and taught one dance class starting in 2010, when the high school lost its Dance instructor due to No Child Left Behind, she taught at Brookhaven School from 1990-2001 teaching a myriad of subjects, including Theatre and Dance, and Rincon Valley Junior High School from 1987-1997, as BJ Van Noy’s choreographer and asst. director of her Music Program. Starr’s tap mentor was a Vaudeville and later Broadway song and Dance man by the name of Jack Williams. Starr studied with Jack for almost 20 years., until his waning years.
Tap, which is a magical form of dance, btw, is Starr’s first dance love, next to swing, salsa, and partner dancing, and then just plain social, wild hippie dancing at concerts.
Starr also teaches Private Tap Lessons for any level dancer. Starr has a studio at her home.
Gabe Copeland (pictured with Mindy on flier above)
Gabe has been a dance educator for over 20 years. He has performed nationally and internationally as a featured member of the Los Angeles based touring company Rhapsody in Taps. Other credits include ABC’s Gong Show, China’s Dream television show, soloist in KIN Dance Company’s Down Around Brown Town and soloist on an international tour with Caution: Men At Work Tap! He has also performed in many Southern California Civic Light Opera productions such as Cole, Crazy For You, and Rodgers & Hart: A Celebration. Other stage credits include, appearing with the legendary Chester Whitmore in A Tribute to Jeni Le Gon, and KIN Dance Company’s James Brown tribute show, Down Around Brown Town. title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. \(707\) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    www.upstairsart gallery.net 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

Interested in learning, sharing and reading short plays? Readers Theatre is a fun opportunity to express yourself.
Readers Theatre participants read scripts adapted from literature, while the ‘audience’ pictures the action by hearing the script being read aloud. It requires no sets, costumes, props, or memorized lines. Instead of acting literature as in a play, the performer’s goal is to read a script aloud effectively, enabling the audience to visualize the action. title: S.R. Laws
location: Napa Palisades Saloon
description:
S.R. LAWS IS OUT THERE: He approaches songwriting with a passion for songs that we all grew up on. His sound rings a familiar bell in your head while still delivering ideas completely unique.  He draws inspiration from outstanding storytellers like John Hiatt, Lucinda Williams, Rodney Crowell, Steve Earle, Neil Finn, Patty Griffin, Chuck Prophet, and Ron Sexsmith. All of their music and others have carved a deep groove. 

Growing up out there in Northern California, he developed a unique connection to music early on. His father worked as a trash collector, and he would spend hours sifting through bags of discarded 45 records. Each find felt like stumbling upon hidden treasures. Some records were covered in dirt and grime, while others were pristine. The thrill of discovering new sounds was exhilarating, and he could hardly wait to drop the needle and immerse himself in the music.

He embarked on a pilgrimage to Texas with just two suitcases and $500 in his bank account. His goal was to dive into the vibrant music scene and learn from fellow songwriters. Austin, known as the "Live Music Capital of the World," offered countless opportunities for him to grow as an artist. Open mics and songwriters' nights became his training ground, where he soaked up every moment, listening to others share their stories through music.

These days, he resides in Sonoma County, California, working hard as a touring artist and singer-songwriter for his original rock band, The Heartsleeves. He invites everyone to join him on this musical journey, sharing his songs one person at a time in this vast and unpredictable world we live in.

A.M. Sessions 

Check out the latest album from S.R. Laws-  "A.M. Sessions." It's a collection of songs that I am incredibly proud of, crafted with the help of old friends and intrepid new collaborators. I can tell you more about it sometime. Come out and grab a copy at one of the shows or you can find it online. “

“ It is through forthright lyrics that are personal and earnest, that he \(Laws\) composes lyrical pictures. Taking snapshots from the most common walks of life filtered through his own joy and tribulations.”  - David Sampson - Producer Studio Secti West

“..relaxed mid-tempo Americana, capturing in each song the rhythmic pocket Laws is known for creating.” -  Coyote Music Review 2024

“...His lyrics simply tell first-person stories from his own life. Nothing fancy, he's not writing to impress--he pours himself, as is, into each phrase and melody.”- Rebecca Roudman- Dirty Cello Radio Hour KRCB Radio 104.9 FM

“A.M. Sessions is worth your while.” - Wiley Koepp- Texas Drummer

title: Artist's Way Group Next Chapter: "The Book of Alchemy"
location: Alibi Bookshop
description: Creativity is my way of making sense of the world.” — Suleika Jaouad  Are you feeling an urge to pick up a pen or paintbrush or pair of scissors and unleash your creativity, but not sure where to start? Or are you looking to find community, to motivate your creative self and make new friends? This might be just the thing for you. Two years ago, we formed an “Artist’s Way” group here at the shop, and continued it again last year. It was extraordinary. Not only did people write and paint and create, but got published and found new life paths. \(And even love!\) But best of all, a community was established, offering encouragement for creative endeavors, and friendship and support. It has been life affirming. Now, in 2026, creativity and community are more important than ever, and it’s time to gather a group again! This year, however, we will not be doing “The Artist’s Way,” and instead will be exploring “The Book of Alchemy” by Suleika Jaouad. This book focuses on journaling and looking at our life experiences to foster creativity to inspire whatever art form we choose to do.  From the publisher: “From the time she was young, Suleika Jaouad has kept a journal. She’s used it to mark life’s biggest occasions and to weather its most ferocious storms. Journaling has buoyed her through illness, heartbreak, and the deepest uncertainty. And she is not alone: for so many people, keeping a journal is an essential tool for navigating both the personal peaks and valleys and the collective challenges of modern life. More than ever, we need a space for puzzling through. In The Book of Alchemy, Suleika explores the art of journaling and shares everything she’s learned about how this life-altering practice can help us tap into that mystical trait that exists in every human: creativity. She has gathered wisdom from one hundred writers, artists, and thinkers in the form of essays and writing prompts. Their insights invite us to inhabit a more inspired life. A companion through challenging times, The Book of Alchemy is broken into themes ranging from new beginnings to love, loss, and rebuilding. Whether you’re a lifelong journaler or new to the practice, this book gives you the tools, direction, and encouragement to engage with discomfort, ask questions, peel back the layers, dream daringly, uncover your truest self—and in doing so, to learn to hold the unbearably brutal and astonishingly beautiful facts of life in the same palm.” Beginning Tuesday, March 3rd at 7pm through the end of September \(with flexibility\), we will be meeting on Tuesdays to check in and discuss the book and our progress. Each chapter has a number of prompts so we will take it slow, but also determine our pace. Every other Tuesday we will discuss the book, and then the alternate weeks will be more open — we can listen to chapters or inspiring podcasts while crafting, or just get together and talk — to give people a chance to catch up or take some time. The initial meeting on March 3rd is a welcome meeting for introductions, to pick up the book, and to set some intentions— no need to read anything yet. The cost is $40 plus the purchase of the book.  To register, come by the shop or email alibibookshop@gmail.com. Registration “closes” the end of March.  This group is truly one of the best things I have ever been a part of, and I’m looking forward to doing it again— and welcoming new folks to the fold! Hope to see you!

title: Poetry Book Club: Illuminations by Arthur Rimbaud
description: Each month, the Poetry Book Club meets online to discuss one must-read book of poems, whether a timeless classic or an award-winning contemporary. Led by Napa poet Kathleen Patterson, who has been an enthusiastic book club member since its beginning, meetings are open to all levels of poetry readers, both the curious and the committed. ABOUT THE BOOK "This may be the most beautiful book in the world, lighted from within and somehow embodying all forms of literature." — Susan Salter Reynolds, Los Angeles Times The modernist masterpiece that is Arthur Rimbaud’s Illuminations has been given new life with the publication of John Ashbery’s “dazzling” \(The Economist\) new translation, widely hailed as one of the literary events of the year. Presented with French text in parallel and a preface by its translator, Ashbery’s rendering powerfully evokes the glittering, kaleidoscopic beauty of the original ABOUT THE AUTHOR Unknown beyond the avant-garde at the time of his death in 1891, Arthur Rimbaud has become one of the most liberating influences on twentieth-century culture. Born Jean Nicolas Arthur Rimbaud in Charleville, France, in 1854, Rimbaud’s family moved to Cours d’Orléans, when he was eight, where he began studying both Latin and Greek at the Pension Rossat. While he disliked school, Rimbaud excelled in his studies and, encouraged by a private tutor, tried his hand at poetry. Shortly thereafter, Rimbaud sent his work to the renowned symbolist poet Paul Verlaine and received in response a one-way ticket to Paris. By late September 1871, at the age of sixteen, Rimbaud had ignited with Verlaine one of the most notoriously turbulent affairs in the history of literature. Their relationship reached a boiling point in the summer of 1873, when Verlaine, frustrated by an increasingly distant Rimbaud, attacked his lover with a revolver in a drunken rage. The act sent Verlaine to prison and Rimbaud back to Charleville to finish his work on A Season in Hell. The following year, Rimbaud traveled to London with the poet Germain Nouveau, to compile and publish his transcendent Illuminations. It was to be Rimbaud’s final publication. By 1880, he would give up writing altogether for a more stable life as merchant in Yemen, where he stayed until a painful condition in his knee forced him back to France for treatment. In 1891, Rimbaud was misdiagnosed with a case of tuberculosis synovitis and advised to have his leg removed. Only after the amputation did doctors determine Rimbaud was, in fact, suffering from cancer. Rimbaud died in Marseille in November of 1891, at the age of 37. He is now considered a saint to symbolists and surrealists, and his body of works, which include Le bateau ivre \(1871\), Une Saison en Enfer \(1873\), and Les Illuminations \(1873\), have been widely recognized as a major influence on artists stretching from Pablo Picasso to Bob Dylan. Pulitzer Prize–winning poet John Ashbery \(1927—2017\) translated many French writers, including Alfred Jarry, Pierre Reverdy, and Raymond Roussel. In 2011 he was awarded the National Book Foundation’s Lifetime Achievement Award.

title: Sound Bath with Laura Benson
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
Rest & Renew at our Sound Bath!
Support your nervous system, release anxiety and stress, and harmonize your body, mind and spirit on the 2nd Tuesday of every month! Laura Benson has a Masters in Intuition Medicine(R) and is a certified sound healer who will guide you through a gentle meditation before each sound bath session. Bring your own yoga mat & blanket and come ready to rest and renew! In the OCA Studio.
Sliding scale pricing $25-$35.
Register
A sound bath is a whole-body, immersive listening experience. During a sound bath, participants often sit or lie down, and are surrounded by the mostly non-melodic soundscapes created by a range of instruments played by the sound bath facilitator. Hence, they are “bathed” in sound.
Sound therapy is a non-invasive healing modality that utilizes the physical and physiological interactions of sound on our bodies and nervous systems to produce therapeutic results. In a sound healing session, specific sonic frequencies are used to soothe the central nervous system, calm the breath, and quiet the mind by encouraging the brain to move into more relaxed states, down from beta (fight-or-flight) and into theta and alpha waves. This increases present-moment awareness and reduces stress and anxiety. Sound baths have been found to be effective in improving mood, cognitive function, and overall mental, physical, and spiritual wellbeing.
Crystal bowl sound baths are particularly powerful in that each bowl is tuned to a specific frequency that corresponds with a different chakra, or energy center, of the body. Based on specific needs, a practitioner can focus on releasing tension or clearing out stuck energy in specific chakras by playing certain bowls or intervals.
While attending a sound bath, you may experience physical sensations brought out by the crystal sound bowls or gong, such as tingling in your limbs or scalp, slowing of your breathing, eye flutters, or small muscle spasms. Not to worry! These sensations often indicate the release of tension or emotional energy stored in the body’s energy systems.

title: Wonderfest: Interspecies Communication
location: HopMonk Tavern
description:
In *The Story of Doctor Dolittle* (1920), author Hugh Lofting imagines a physician who enjoys two-way communication with non-human animals. In 2026, for real, neuroscientist **Dr. Julie Elie**, earned the *Coller Dolittle Prize for Two-way Interspecies Communication*, describing a breakthrough in *genuine* animal talk. Dr. Elie and her team were able to classify zebra finch vocalizations into “core words” based on their significance. Then Dr. Elie verified that the “chatty songbirds” could distinguish — and derive meaning — from those sounds!

Our Wonderfest speaker, **Dr. Julie Elie,** is Associate Project Scientist in the neuroscience lab of Frédéric Theunissen at UC Berkeley. \[Zebra finch photo by Wolfgang Forstmeier.\]

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

description: Using AI to Lead More Effectively Across the Business Artificial intelligence is changing how businesses operate, but for many leaders the challenge is not hearing about AI. The Napa Chamber's AI Mastery for Leaders Workshop Series is designed for owners, executives, general managers, partners, and department leaders who want a practical way to guide AI adoption across the business. This is not another generic AI webinar or tool demo. It is an in-person, small-group workshop series built to help local business leaders understand where AI creates value, how to introduce it responsibly, and how to turn it into a practical advantage inside the organization. description:
Regenerative Ayurvedic Yoga with Tirza Dawn
Come, step onto your mat with an open heart and an open mind.
Invest in your self care and join us for morning yoga in the OCA studio. $20 per class, $15 for OCA members. Yoga is offered Mondays from 10-11:10 AM and also on Wednesdays from 8:30-9:40 AM. The registration below is for Mondays.
Pay at the door for a-la-carte sessions or use the links below to pay ahead for four weeks at a time.
Pay Online 4 sessions
Tirza Dawn Naramore
is a yogi, mother, artist, ceremonialist and lover of life. She has been practicing and teaching yoga and meditation for 30 years and offers yoga retreats and trainings that center on optimum health, self realization and self love. Her teachers are from many yoga and tantric traditions, but her primary lineages are Iyengar and Kali Ray.
Tirza is deeply devoted to community building and is honored to have created a number of community supported non profits including Mystic Family Circus and The AWAKEN Project, which serves families with children on the autism spectrum. Tirza is proud to be the mother of 3 wild teenagers, including her incredible son who is diagnosed with autism.
Tirza’s spirituality is one of many influences and teachings. Beginning with a Christian up-bringing and being raised on a Christian commune in her early childhood, she later expanded into more earth-based ways. While in her 20’s Tirza was adopted into the Native American Church, where she learned from her relatives a way of living the “Beauty Way.”
During the 1990’s and early 2000’s, Tirza lived in San Francisco, Oakland and Berkeley, directing the Mystic Family Circus, which was a performance group dedicated to cultural awareness and bridge building. She worked with Cirque du Soleil, Burning Man, Reclaiming, Contraband, CELLspace and other Bay Area art collectives and non profits to provide conscious entertainment and “prayerformances” for the betterment of humankind and the planet.
In 2012, Tirza helped to found the Buckeye Gathering, an ancestral skills gathering in Northern California which draws teachers and students of all ages to learn ancestral ways of tending the earth and survival skills.
Tirza Dawn was the founder of yoga programming and the Ayurvedic Yoga Teacher Trainings at the dhyana Center of Ayurveda in Sebastopol, California, which operated a community center of healing and education from 2010 to 2020.

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
location: Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: Eric Lindell & The Westside Summer League
location: Ives Park
description:
Born in San Mateo, California in 1969, Lindell spent countless hours in San Francisco, soaking up the musical sounds of the city, eventually leading him to pick up first the bass and then the guitar and harmonica. With a love of music and skateboarding, Lindell formed a few punky garage bands early on while his musical horizons expanded. He listened to the deep blues of Buddy Guy, Junior Wells, Jimmy Reed and Albert King before drifting toward the R&B sounds of The Impressions, Stevie Wonder and Donny Hathaway, soaking up the soul and learning how to craft a song. After performing at bars on the West Coast with a few short-lived bands, Eric formed his own group in 1993. He quickly gained a loyal Northern California audience thanks to countless performances and many late-night jam sessions. Established stars like Charlie Musselwhite and Tom Waits attended his shows, as did overflow crowds of music fans.

With music on his mind, Lindell headed to New Orleans in 1999, where he quickly discovered the pulsating and dynamic roots scene. He gravitated toward the West Bank dive bars of Gretna and Algiers, where he befriended many older area musicians who helped him get regular work as a performer. Some of New Orleans' finest players, including keyboardist Ivan Neville and drummers Harold Brown \(War\), Stanton Moore \(Galactic\) and Johnny Vidacovich \(Professor Longhair, Astral Project\) often joined him on stage. Galactic bassist Rob Mercurio began sitting in as well, and word of Lindell's immense talents quickly spread around the city. Stars like Branford Marsalis, The Neville Brothers and John Scofield began showing up at his gigs and embracing this fresh California kid's funky music. According to Lindell, "It's a great feeling to be recognized for your music in New Orleans." Since 2003, in addition to his own gigs, Lindell regularly joins forces with Ivan Neville, Moore and Mercurio \(when time and schedules permit\) and they perform to overflow crowds as Dragon Smoke.

2006's Change In The Weather delighted and surprised music fans hungry for a truly original artist. Lindell's deceptively simple sounding songs, laid back grooves and hook-laden melodies were fueled by guests including Brown, Neville and Moore. Critics across the country went wild, with reviews and features in Relix, OffBeat, Guitar Player, Down Beat, The New Yorker, The New York Press and many other national and regional publications. Singer And Musician magazine put Eric on the cover and many newspaper entertainment sections did the same.

2007's Low On Cash, Rich In Love and 2009's Gulf Coast Highway pushed Lindell farther into the spotlight. Appearances on Late Night With Conan O'Brien and National Public Radio's Mountain Stage solidified his stature as an artist who simply could not be ignored. Many of his songs have appeared in films and television shows, including Boston Legal and Treme. He has collaborated and shared stages with blues and rock luminaries, including John Fogerty, Luther Dickinson and Anson Funderburgh.

With Revolution In Your Heart, Lindell was more than ready to come home to Alligator. "The timing is perfect. I'm so excited to get back to focusing on what I do and have such a great team behind me," he says. Upon release of the album, Lindell and his band will tour heavily, reuniting with old friends and, as always, earning new fans at every stop. AllMusic declares Lindell a singular talent, saying, "He plays soulful, funk-drenched, tight and focused grooves. He is a quadruple threat as a solid songwriter, impressive guitarist, affecting singer and harmonica blower. This is music that's deceptively difficult to create. Lindell makes it seem not just easy, but natural."

title: Tom Chown: 46 Years Behind the Lens
location: Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery - Santa Rosa Campus
description: Santa Rosa Junior College will celebrate the 46-year career of longtime staff photographer Tom Chown with a photography exhibition featuring images from his decades at the college, from the days of film and darkrooms to the digital era.  Chown began his career at SRJC at age 24, working in the campus photography lab. Over the next 46 years, he became a familiar presence throughout the college community, documenting the people, programs and milestones that shaped generations of students and employees.  The exhibition will trace Chown's evolution as a photographer, from working with film and developing photographs in the darkroom to embracing digital photography. It also offers a visual history of SRJC, preserving moments from nearly five decades of college life.  The exhibition is free and open to the public.Location: Robert F. Yoga Vinyasa Krama is a comprehensive hatha-raja yogic system for purification, developing concentration, neuromuscular fitness and conditioning, refining & mastering the breath, awakening subtle energy and stilling the mind. Based on deep breathing & the subtle movement of prana directed into the cartilage tissue, sinuous musculature, internal organs, nerve pathways and nadis. The whole process gradually transforms the body and mind, releasing old patterns of physical and mental tension and dysfunctional patterns of movement, providing tonic, energetic and psychophysiological effects.
This system is presented from the teachings **Srivatsa Ramaswami** learned through his over 33 years of one on one study with **Sri Krishnamacharya** and teachings from a similar **Himalayan method**.
This ongoing class will explore the entire system of 12 Kramas with each class focusing on a particular krama or vinyasas from different kramas & pranayama & dharana practices.

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: S.R. Laws
location: Café Frida Gallery
description:
S.R. LAWS IS OUT THERE: He approaches songwriting with a passion for songs that we all grew up on. His sound rings a familiar bell in your head while still delivering ideas completely unique.  He draws inspiration from outstanding storytellers like John Hiatt, Lou Reed, Steve Earle, Neil Finn and Ron Sexsmith. All of their music and others have carved a deep groove. 

Growing up out there in Northern California, he developed a unique connection to music early on. His father worked as a trash collector, and he would spend hours sifting through bags of discarded 45 records. Each find felt like stumbling upon hidden treasures. Some records were covered in dirt and grime, while others were pristine. The thrill of discovering new sounds was exhilarating, and he could hardly wait to drop the needle and immerse himself in the music.

He embarked on a pilgrimage to Texas with just two suitcases and $500 in his bank account. His goal was to dive into the vibrant music scene and learn from fellow songwriters. Austin, known as the "Live Music Capital of the World," offered countless opportunities for him to grow as an artist. Open mics and songwriters' nights became his training ground, where he soaked up every moment, listening to others share their stories through music.

These days, he resides in Sonoma County, California, working hard as a touring artist and singer-songwriter for his original rock band, The Heartsleeves. He invites everyone to join him on this musical journey, sharing his songs one person at a time in this vast and unpredictable world we live in.

“Scott Ray Laws is an unique and really cool songwriter…he digs into materials, tells a story in his songs, and has a clean baritone vocality that is easy on the ears. We had a chance to meet and hang with Scott back in May ..and I HAD to have him back for a Wednesday evening.” Luigi- Owner-The Listening Room.

“..An ORIGINAL songwriter who knows how to tell a story clearly in song” -  Scotty O’Neill - Guitarist/Promoter

“ It was such a treat catching your set last night — really refreshing to hear something new and original. Thanks for pulling up a chair and hanging out with us — we really enjoyed the conversation and the stories behind your songs.”  -Tripp B. - Sonoma Songwriter

“Expect slow burning passion and vivid music …the kind of energy that turns into “let’s stay for just one more!..”  - Doug- Owner/Wine Maker- Spicy Vines

“...His lyrics simply tell first-person stories from his own life. Nothing fancy, he's not writing to impress--he pours himself, as is, into each phrase and melody.”- Rebecca Roudman- Dirty Cello Radio Hour KRCB Radio 104.9 FM

“ It is through forthright lyrics that are personal and earnest, that he composes lyrical pictures. Taking snapshots from the most common walks of life...”  - David Sampson - Producer Studio Secti West

“..relaxed mid-tempo Americana, capturing in each song the rhythmic pocket Laws is known for creating.” -  Coyote Music Review 2024

title: The Rediscovery of George "Nash" Walker: The Price of Stardom in Jim Crow America
location: Doyle Library, Room 4520 - Santa Rosa Campus
description: Join us for a lecture on George "Nash" Walker by Dr. Daniel Atkinson.  The lecture will focus on the first biography of George Walker, a uniquely Afro-American tale of innovation and triumph despite the odds; the story of an underdog with a bite!The Rediscovery of George "Nash" Walker is the first biography dedicated to the life and cultural contributions of George Walker, an actor, writer, and producer who revolutionized Black American theatre in the early twentieth century. Drawing on archival resources, newspaper accounts, memoirs, oral histories, and writings by Walker himself, Daniel E. Atkinson traces Walker's rise from a medicine show performer to a leading figure in American popular culture.  Dr. Atkinson is an independent scholar and the Assistant Director of the August Wilson estate. He earned his doctorate in ethnomusicology from the University of Washington, where he specialized in Afro-American music and culture.This lecture is funded by a grant from the Santa Rosa Junior College Foundation Randolph Newman Cultural Enrichment Endowment.For more information, visit the SRJC Multicultural Museum Website. Unlock your inner strength and find your flow. Belly dancing with Raja is an innovative fusion class that blends the rhythmic artistry of belly dance with the high-energy benefits of aerobics. • Functional Stability: Improve your balance and posture through controlled, hip-driven movements and low-impact aerobic footwork.

• Total Body Toning: Build lean muscle in your legs, glutes, and arms while maintaining a constant, heart-pumping pace.

• Mind-Body Connection: Enhance your coordination and body awareness through rhythmic, expressive choreography.

title: Author Event: Homebound by Portia Elan
description: Join us for a special event with Portia Elan, photographer of Homeland. This event is free, but we appreciate your RSVP below so we can plan for your attendance. ABOUT THE BOOK In a dazzling ode to human inventiveness and the desire for meaning, four lives are entangled across time by one unfinished story, saved to a floppy disk in the 1980s and destined to ripple across the centuries. Homebound is a big-hearted story sparkling with examples of community at its best: at our most curious, most creative, most loving, and most resilient. Here are the stories that connect us and keep us alive \(for ourselves, for each other, for the Earth\). A NATIONAL BESTSELLER A GOOD MORNING AMERICA BOOK CLUB PICK A NEW YORKER BEST BOOK OF THE YEAR “A joy...and a hauntingly beautiful exploration of what makes us human. It kept me up all night!” — MADELINE MILLER, \#1 New York Times bestselling author of The Song of Achilles "A big, bold, ecstatic world—full of heart and wonder.” — RUTH OZEKI, New York Times bestselling author of A Tale for the Time Being 1983. Becks is nineteen, blasting her Walkman, and hiding from the fact that her beloved uncle, and the only person who understood her, is dead. Luckily, he left her a half-finished video game to complete—one last collaboration to find her way out of loneliness. 2078. Dr. Portman works at the intersection of artificial intelligence and robotics, wrestling with her responsibility to Earth's precarious future. But increasingly, it seems an exceptional project may transcend everything she believed to be possible... 2586. After decades of life on the sea, Yesiko knows a scavenger's work is rife with moral compromise. Yet when a long-lost piece of technology walks aboard her ship, she is set on a path toward a sacrifice even she may be unwilling to make. Linking these women across the centuries is a chain reaction of love, longing, and creativity that reveals our deep interconnectedness. Clear-eyed and hopeful, Homebound imagines how future generations will find meaning in the things we leave behind. Perfect for fans of Gabrielle Zevin, Anthony Doerr, Ruth Ozeki, and Emily St. John Mandel, Homebound establishes Elan as a powerful new voice in fiction. She brings us a dazzling debut that explores the power of stories – how they shape us, connect us, and lead us home. This radiant novel takes us from 1980s Cincinnati to the vast ocean 600 years into the future. In it, we follow four entangled lives across time, connected by one story of survival and hope, destined to ripple across time. Portia Elan wanted to write a novel that would be a comfort, an escape, and an antidote to loneliness- much like the books she loved growing up. She says, “Homebound is for readers who have felt like an outsider and been angry about it, readers who have experienced the magic of found family, readers who believe in the power of story, and readers who see human nature too clearly to imagine a future that is either all good or all bad.” ABOUT THE AUTHOR Portia Elan studied history at Stanford University and earned an MFA from the University of Victoria, British Columbia, before returning to California, where she has worked as a teacher and public librarian. A former Lambda Literary Fellow, she lives in the San Francisco Bay Area with her wife and an abundance of cats. Homebound is her first novel.

You will learn

The Basic Step: You will master the signature quick-quick-slow rhythm that defines Samba no Pé.

Arm & Hip Styling: You will learn how to add the authentic flair, movement, and energy that makes Brazilian samba so captivating.

Technique & Posture: You will receive tips on proper body alignment to help you dance longer, faster, and more safely.

Rhythm & Musicality: You will learn how to connect your movement directly to the irresistible beat of the bateria \(the samba drum section\).

This class is perfect for anyone looking to connect with the vibrant spirit of Brazil, improve coordination, and get a fantastic workout—all while learning the foundational steps of this iconic dance. No partner or prior dance experience is required! Just bring your enthusiasm and comfortable shoes!

What is Toastmasters About?

Usually at our meetings, we will have a prepared speech, and a speech evaluation. The Grammarian and Wizard of Ah's will listen for turns of phrases and the use of filler words. We also practice impromptu speaking during the section of the meeting called Table Topics. During Table Topics, at a recent meeting, we were asked what we felt was the biggest communication problem or challenge. What would you answer in a fast moment? macbitches takes a darkly funny look at the toxic, high-stakes world of university theater, centering on a freshman who unexpectedly lands the role of Lady Macbeth. The play centers on freshman acting major Hailey, who unexpectedly scores the coveted role of Lady Macbeth. Her upperclassmen rivals immediately invite her over to “celebrate.” As the Fireball and Svedka flow, the young women interrogate their own ambitions as well as the power structures that have shaped their education—and when the night spirals into violent and shocking acts of betrayal, they come to learn that what’s done cannot be undone.

title: South Pacific
location: 6th Street Playhouse
description:
**An unforgettable romance set against the sweeping tides of World War II.**

Against the backdrop of the Pacific War of WWII, ***South Pacific*** blends high-stakes wartime romance with a poignant exploration of social prejudice. When spirited Navy nurse, Nellie Forbush, falls in love with a sophisticated French planter, and a young Marine lieutenant finds himself captivated by an ethereal island girl, their relationships are tested by the prejudices and pressures of a world at war. What unfolds is a deeply moving story about love, courage, and the transformative power of understanding. Featuring a soaring score by **Richard Rodgers** and **Oscar Hammerstein II**, including classics like “Some Enchanted Evening” and “There Is Nothin’ Like a Dame,” *South Pacific* remains one of the most beloved musicals of all time.

Winner of the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the original Broadway production won ten Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Best Score and Best Libretto. It is the only musical production ever to have won all four Tony Awards for acting.

SOUTH PACIFIC is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of The Rodgers & Hammerstein Organization. concordtheatricals.com

Performances run Thur, Friday, Saturday evenings at 7:30pm and Saturday and Sunday matinees at 2:00pm.

Chown began his career at SRJC at age 24, working in the campus photography lab. Over the next 46 years, he became a familiar presence throughout the college community, documenting the people, programs and milestones that shaped generations of students and employees.
