title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: Cheeseboard Workshop with Alli Keyser-Marti at Gold Ridge Organic Farms
location: Gold Ridge Organic Farms
description:
Join Gold Ridge Organic Farms' resident cheese expert, Alli Keyser-Marti for an intimate hands-on cheeseboard workshop! Explore how to create your own beautiful board, showcasing a wide array of flavors, textures, and colors. Learn how to incorporate a variety of edible flowers and fresh herbs, local honey, apple cider syrup, balsamic vinegar, EVOO, olives, artisan bread, crackers, and dips to accompany the best local cheeses made by artisan producers from Sonoma County and beyond.

All ingredients and materials included in ticket price. You'll get to take home your creation to share with friends and family.

Building on a culinary career starting in her teenage years, in 2014 Alli Keyser-Marti fell in love with exploring the world of milk, salt, enzymes, and microbes. Her cheese journey includes managing Cowgirl Creamery’s original Pt Reyes shop, overseeing the Oliver’s Market Stony Point cheese department, as well as being awarded an ACEF Scholarship to attend the American Cheese Society's Portland conference in 2022, where she successfully completed the Certified Cheese Professional® exam. In 2025 Alli also became an ACS Certified Cheese Sensory Evaluator® and judged cheese for the Good Food Awards. She has followed this passion from her backyard in California to small farms all over France, rural Ohio, roadside stands in Sardinia, and ferries in Croatia. Most recently you’ll find her skillfully pairing cheese with olive oil and apple tastings at Gold Ridge Organic Farms, as well as working on an apprenticeship with Applied Sensory for Olive Oil analysis and maintaining our organic certifications.

This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. title: Shut Up & Write!™ Santa Rosa REMOTE ZOOM FRIDAY
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Wine Country
**This event is hosted on the Shut Up & Write website, so please [sign up here](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2me5JeN600/id2w10OBEA00) for your writing event.**

**ABOUT THE EVENT**
Join us virtually for an hour + of writing using Zoom. Let's keep together as much as we can during these uncertain times and keep on writing. Look for the schedule online and join us.

We’ve discovered that it’s strikingly helpful to write with other writers. See if it’s true for you at 3pm on Friday afternoon. Be it a book, blog, script, essay, dissertation, resume, melody, poem or just plain work stuff, you are invited to write it with us. No one will see what you've written or give you unsolicited advice. Instead of just thinking about writing, come and get some real writing done.

JOIN US!

1. Link available on the Shut Up and Write website..

Please note:

1. If you don't have Zoom set up on your computer yet, leave 15-30 minutes ahead of time to get it set up!
2. If you have difficulty with audio (don't have a microphone set up), as long as you have a speaker, you can call in (you'll see phone numbers when you log in).
3. If you are late, you won't be able to intro with us, but you are still welcome to join in.
4. If you won't be able to make it, please cancel so that the space is available to another writer.

SCHEDULE:
3:00 - quick intros.
around 3:10 - timer starts: write for 70 mins.
4:20 - (the end) wrap up

Wherever you are, we hope to see you online! Keep on writing...
Regards,
Lorraine Segal
source: Meetup: Shut Up & Write Wine Country

title: Outdoor Movie in the Park - A Good Year
location: Veterans Memorial Park
description:
Yountville Arts Movie in the Park \(a good year-PG/13\): Friday, September 11th, Veterans Memorial Park. Starting at 6 PM, lay out your blankets, set up your lawn chairs, and order dinner from Riley's Food Truck before the movie begins at approximately 8 PM/Dusk. This is a free event, but reserving your tickets assists us with planning. 

A Good Year was directed by Ridley Scott and stars Russell Crowe and Abbie Cornish. This 2006 romantic comedy-drama follows British investment broker Max Skinner as he discovers he is the only known relative of his uncle Henry, so he inherits his Provence chateau and vineyard, where he spent many of his summers. As he spruces the estate to be sold, he rediscovers what he had loved about the place. 

Joining us at the event are Ludovic Dervin, the General Manager and Senior Winemaker at Stags' Leap Winery, a Native of Champagne, France, as well as Jim Foster, Sales Manager from Stags' Leap Winery.  Ludovic and Jim will be pouring tastings of Stags' Leap Wines before the movie and giving us an introduction right before the film rolls. This is a free event, open to everyone. 

\*Please leave pets at home. Service animals are welcome.\*

description: England, 1605: A terrorist plot is brewing to assassinate King James 1 and blow Parliament to kingdom come! Or so the King claims. To spread his propaganda, King James 1 hires the world’s most famous playwright, William Shagspeare \(after a contemporary spelling of the Bard’s name\). As Shag investigates the King’s bizarre tale, he begins to question it, leading him and his actors to a dilemma: lie and pocket the cash, tell the truth and literally risk their necks, or perhaps equivocate–lie and tell the truth at the same time. This high-stakes thriller drops into many of the Bard’s most famous works in an alternate history that resonates today. This is a witty and poignant ensemble piece in which six actors play well over a dozen roles, some of which include snippets of Shakespeare's other plays-in-progress \(one of which becomes the famous Macbeth.\)

macbitches takes a darkly funny look at the toxic, high-stakes world of university theater, centering on a freshman who unexpectedly lands the role of Lady Macbeth. The play centers on freshman acting major Hailey, who unexpectedly scores the coveted role of Lady Macbeth. Her upperclassmen rivals immediately invite her over to “celebrate.” As the Fireball and Svedka flow, the young women interrogate their own ambitions as well as the power structures that have shaped their education—and when the night spirals into violent and shocking acts of betrayal, they come to learn that what’s done cannot be undone.

title: South Pacific
location: 6th Street Playhouse
description:
**An unforgettable romance set against the sweeping tides of World War II.**

Against the backdrop of the Pacific War of WWII, ***South Pacific*** blends high-stakes wartime romance with a poignant exploration of social prejudice. When spirited Navy nurse, Nellie Forbush, falls in love with a sophisticated French planter, and a young Marine lieutenant finds himself captivated by an ethereal island girl, their relationships are tested by the prejudices and pressures of a world at war. What unfolds is a deeply moving story about love, courage, and the transformative power of understanding. Featuring a soaring score by **Richard Rodgers** and **Oscar Hammerstein II**, including classics like “Some Enchanted Evening” and “There Is Nothin’ Like a Dame,” *South Pacific* remains one of the most beloved musicals of all time.

Winner of the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the original Broadway production won ten Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Best Score and Best Libretto. It is the only musical production ever to have won all four Tony Awards for acting.

SOUTH PACIFIC is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of The Rodgers & Hammerstein Organization. concordtheatricals.com

Performances run Thur, Friday, Saturday evenings at 7:30pm and Saturday and Sunday matinees at 2:00pm.

title: Jeffrey Halford & The Healers

description:
Of the many marks of genius associated with rock n’ roll greatness, the knack for surrounding oneself with transformational talent looms especially large, with The Rolling Stones being perhaps the most notable example. Jeffrey Halford treads a poetic rootsy path on his latest release, SOUL CRUSADE, combining a bulletproof collection of songs inspired by gospel, folk, soul, and blues, with a formidable roster of musical contributors. The result is one of Halford’s most approachable and easy-grooving.

His latest album release, SOUL CRUSADE, is the follow-up to the critically acclaimed record WEST TOWARDS SOUTH. The album came out in Europe on Continental Song City, debuted in September at \#2, and then undisputedly reached \#1 in October 2022 and stayed in the chart for four months. 

JEFFREY HALFORD & THE HEALERS are gearing up for their eighth European tour in September and October 2025, bringing their signature blend of raw rock ‘n’ roll, country, and soul back to the stage. But this tour isn’t just another run—it marks the 25th anniversary of KEROSENE, the album \(release date Friday, August 29th, 2025\) that put Halford on the map as a true Americana troubadour.

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

description:
Joe Melendrez has forged a unique path to becoming one of America’s most exciting Catholic performers. At age fifteen, Joe was featured on MTV and developed a love for performing. description:
If you have previously completed Sugarloaf's Intermediate Hiking for Fitness Series, or can hike 6.5 miles with at least 1,600ft of elevation, this hike may be right for you. Completion of the Bald Mountain summit hike (in and out via Bald Mountain Trail) is recommended as a pre-requisite. 

Meet at the main parking lot at the end of Channel Dr. The group will start out on Warren Richardson Trail, continuing onto Two Quarry Trail. At the Marsh Trail junction, we'll trek northwest around Buick Meadow, connecting with South Burma Trail, returning to Warren Richardson Trail and finishing through the obsidian-peppered Steve's "S" Trail. 

**This event requires advance registration; day-of on site tickets will not be available.** There is a $10 deposit per ticket, which will be returned post-hike, unless you choose to donate it to support this and other Sonoma Ecology Center programs at Sugarloaf Ridge SP. Wear appropriate footwear for rocky/slippery trails, layers, and sun protection. Bring at least 64oz of water and if desired, a snack. Parking fees apply.

We require reservations to maintain our capacity limits and ensure everyone enjoys their visit to the fullest.  

Can I cancel my reservation?  

Absolutely! You can cancel your reservation up to 48 hours before your scheduled time by calling us at 707-823-3100. Please note that cancellations made less than 48 hours in advance will result in forfeiture of the entrance fee. 

Can I bring my dog?  

Dogs are not permitted in the orchard, with the exception of service animals. This policy helps ensure the safety and comfort of all our visitors. 

Can I bring a stroller into the orchard?  

For safety reasons, strollers aren't allowed in the orchard, but you're welcome to leave yours at the check-in area where it will be safe and waiting for you!  

I require mobility accommodations. Can I still pick apples in the orchard?  

Yes. Please call us on 707-823-3110 once you’re made a reservation and we can provide suitable transportation into our orchard.

Why is there an entrance fee?  

The entrance fee helps us maintain our beautiful orchard and keep our experienced staff on hand to ensure everyone has a safe and enjoyable experience. 

How much are the apples?  

Our delicious U-pick apples are $4.00 per pound.  

What variety of apples will we be harvesting?  

You'll be picking either Honeycrisp or Fuji apples (depending on seasonal availability).  

Can I harvest heirloom apples?  

While heirloom apples aren't available for U-pick, we offer many wonderful heirloom varieties for purchase in our Farm Shop.  

Are your apples organic?  

Yes, all our apples are organically grown and certified annually by Oregon Tilth!

title: Jack London State Historic Park WILD Trail Challenge
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
On Saturdays from Sept. 5 to Oct. 3, Jack London State Historic Park’s WILD Trail Challenge returns for a third year.  This series of five hikes covers every trail in the park for a total of 39.5 miles.  The hikes increase in duration and/or difficulty each week.

Participants can sign up for individual hikes or do them all.

The price for each hike is $15.  The park entry fee of $15 per vehicle is waived for these hikes.  Those who sign up for all five hikes before Sept. 5 save 20 percent and pay only $60.

Hike \# 1 – Historic Trails

September 5, 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m.  

A great way to warm up. This hike explores the historic sites and trails of the park. Navigate both sides of the park to discover Jack London’s Beauty Ranch, London Lake, and the Wolf House ruins.

Easy – moderate hike \(approximately 4.5 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 2 – Ancient Redwood

September 12, 9 a.m.-1 p.m.   

Meander through the redwoods and sunny oak woodlands of the park’s three Bridge Trails \(Upper, Lower, and Fallen\). The journey leads to the majestic ancient redwood, fondly known as the Grandmother Tree.

Moderate hike \(approximately 6 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 3 – Historic Orchard

September 19, 9 a.m.-1:30 p.m.   

Start Location: Note that this hike does not begin at Jack London State Historic Park

Sonoma Developmental Center

Arnold Dr, Eldridge, CA 95431

Stroll along the blue shores of Fern Lake before reaching the Historic Orchard. Learn about the history of the land and the fascinating fruit-bearing crops that thrive there.

Moderate – Difficult hike \(approximately 7 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 4 – Ridge

September 26, 9 a.m-3:30 p.m.   

Details: Hikers will gain elevation and an appreciation for the diverse habitats found within the park. They’ll also traverse part of the ever-growing Bay Area Ridge Trail.

Difficult hike \(approximately 12 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 5 – Summit 

October 3, 9 a.m.-2:30 p.m.     

A trek to the park summit is the perfect way to complete the WILD Trail Challenges.  Climb Sonoma Mountain to enjoy stunning views, celebrate with fellow hikers, and become a WILD One.

Difficult hike \(approximately 10 miles roundtrip\)

**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

In this 4 session intensive, students will create work for a soda firing while learning the history and chemistry of atmospheric Soda. Each session there will be demos and assignments that will lend to intentional and experimental decisions on the objects we make for the firing. We will make tests in clay material, slips, glazes, experiment in wadding, and placements in the kiln. During class there will be lectures on the chemistry of clay and of soda firing as well as its history, application, and experiments within the field. This class is about learning how to explore what soda can do.During the 4 weeks each student will create one cubic foot of work to be bisqued and then fired in the soda kiln. The firing will be two full days of activity, with students applying the lessons learned in class to the wadding and loading of the kiln and lighting the kiln. Students will learn how to plan a gas kiln schedule, use a kiln log, assess a kilns needs, and successfully fire off a kiln. Students will learn how to spray soda and how to maintain the kiln and her accessories in order to support Julia’s \(our beloved soda kiln\) longevity. This deep dive into soda will spark ideas and expand folx knowledge on kilns, firing, and making in clay.

title: How to be OK with an Overwhelmed Mind
location: Spirit Rock Meditation Center
description:
with Leslie Booker

Let’s first debunk the myth that our mind should be completely quiet and empty of all thoughts. This is a high bar to meet during our meditation practice, and certainly not the reality of a healthy mind. Just as the tongue tastes and the nose smells, the mind thinks… it’s its job! The goal of meditation is not about how quiet and still our mind (and body) can get, but how we respond to a mind that is overwhelmed, creative, anxious, dreamy, neurodiverse, and even a little sleepy.

And we do this by allowing the wisdom of the body to take the lead.

This day is not meant to exclude, pathologize, or diagnose anyone, but to normalize that there is a lot happening in the mind, and explore how mindfulness of the body can support us in untangling and regulating the nervous system to reduce some of that anxiety.

In this special four-week workshop, participants will explore the unique art of reduction relief printmaking. Acclaimed guest artist, Tomoko Murakami, will demonstrate how to create multi-color prints from a single linoleum block. The main idea is to gradually carve away parts of the block and print each new layer of color, with each layer building on the previous one. The course covers the entire process, from designing and planning, to carving techniques, inking, registration, and printing with both hand and printing press methods. Participants will learn to explore the possibilities of color mixing and layering, enabling students to achieve intricate designs and a wide range of visual effects. You will gain an understanding of the materials, processes, and innovations involved in this unique form of relief print printing!All levels are welcome, including continuing linocut students. Please note: This class requires hand dexterity to maneuver the carving tool. Participants should feel comfortable standing, and using tools with sharp blades and edges.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room

description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. \(707\) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    www.upstairsart gallery.net 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

location: Jarvis Conservatory
description:
**RAVEL: TWO ONE-ACT OPERAS - Monte Carlo Opera 2025** *L’Heure espagnole & L’Enfant et les Sortilèges*

*L'Heure espagnole* (The Spanish Hour) by Maurice Ravel is a witty, one act comic opera about Concepción, a clockmaker's  bored wife in 18th century Spain, who uses her husband Torquemada's absence to arrange secret liaisons, hiding her lovers (Gonzalveand Don Íñigo) inside his grandfather clocks, only to have them get stuck, leading to comedic chaos resolved by the strong, silent muleteer Ramiro, who proves more appealing than her sophisticated suitors. 

*L'Enfant et les Sortilèges* (The Child and the Spells) tells the story of a naughty young boy, confined to his room for refusing to do homework, who throws a destructive tantrum, causing household objects and pets to come alive and seek revenge,  ultimately leading him to remorse and a newfound understanding of kindness as they collectively call for his mother, who  appears at the end.

title: South Pacific
location: 6th Street Playhouse
description:
**An unforgettable romance set against the sweeping tides of World War II.**

Against the backdrop of the Pacific War of WWII, ***South Pacific*** blends high-stakes wartime romance with a poignant exploration of social prejudice. When spirited Navy nurse, Nellie Forbush, falls in love with a sophisticated French planter, and a young Marine lieutenant finds himself captivated by an ethereal island girl, their relationships are tested by the prejudices and pressures of a world at war. What unfolds is a deeply moving story about love, courage, and the transformative power of understanding. Featuring a soaring score by **Richard Rodgers** and **Oscar Hammerstein II**, including classics like “Some Enchanted Evening” and “There Is Nothin’ Like a Dame,” *South Pacific* remains one of the most beloved musicals of all time.

Winner of the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the original Broadway production won ten Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Best Score and Best Libretto. It is the only musical production ever to have won all four Tony Awards for acting.

SOUTH PACIFIC is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of The Rodgers & Hammerstein Organization. concordtheatricals.com

Performances run Thur, Friday, Saturday evenings at 7:30pm and Saturday and Sunday matinees at 2:00pm.

title: Petaluma River Upstream High Tide Paddle
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
When the tide is high, the Petaluma River opens into a quieter, greener world.

Join The Floathouse crew at their central downtown dock for a gentle, guided paddle upstream, timed to higher tides that allow access beyond the downtown channel and into a tranquil tidal slough. With extra water beneath us, we’re able to glide into calm, lush stretches of the river that are normally out of reach.

This unhurried paddle highlights the natural beauty of the Petaluma River’s brackish, tidal waterway. Watch for great egrets, blue herons, snowy egrets, turtles basking along the banks, and abundant plant life. The calm water and peaceful surroundings create a deeply grounding experience—many guests say they feel their stress melt away within minutes.

Along the way, knowledgeable guides share stories of the river’s ecology and human history, offering insight into how this upper channel has shaped—and continues to shape—Petaluma. It’s a rare opportunity to experience how close wild nature lives to the heart of downtown.

Beginner-friendly. Sit-on-top kayaks and all gear provided.

description:
**Saturday, September 12, 2026 | 4:00–6:00 PM** **Caldwell Snyder Gallery | 1328 Main Street, St. Helena, CA**

Caldwell Snyder Gallery is pleased to present **Depth of Field**, a solo exhibition of new works by acclaimed Canadian artist **Bobbie Burgers**. Join us on **Saturday, September 12, from 4–6 PM** for a Conversation with the Artist & Book Signing celebrating the exhibition.

For more than two decades, Burgers has developed a distinctive contemporary painting practice defined by vibrant color, expressive gesture, and richly layered surfaces. Blurring the line between abstraction and representation, her paintings transform florals and organic forms into immersive compositions inspired by the rhythms, growth, and fleeting beauty of the natural world.

Born in Vancouver, British Columbia, Burgers has exhibited extensively throughout Canada, the United States, Europe, and China. Caldwell Snyder Gallery has proudly represented the artist since 2002.

**Depth of Field will be on view through September 30, 2026.**

title: Nothing To See Here - Jason Perry - Opening Reception
location: Mare Island Art Studios
description:
"Nothing To See Here" is a critical, yet playful examination of the UFO phenomenon that is hinged on the dynamic between serious scientific inquiry and fringe science.

With a mixed media approach that combines drawing, collage, and painting, Jason Perry seeks to entice the viewer into the work through familiar visual iconography, bold colors, expressive marks, and textures. Once there, the viewer is offered a deeper layer of meaning to consider. Perry calls into question the blurred narratives, misinformation, and potential truths surrounding the UFO topic.

At its core, "Nothing To See Here" invites us to look a little closer at our beliefs, our relationship to the strange, the unexplained, and our enduring fascination with what might be out there.

title: Last West: An evening exploring the making of Roadsongs for Dorothea Lange
location: Western Hills Garden
description:
As dusk falls over Western Hills Garden, join poet and playwright Tess Taylor and director Ciera Eis for an intimate evening inside the making of *Last West: Roadsongs for Dorothea Lange.*

Hear readings from the play, watch an unforgettable slideshow of Dorothea Lange's California photographs, and go behind the scenes of an extraordinary production in development.

Tess and Ciera will be in conversation about the images, voices, and stories at the heart of *Last West* — Lange's road journals, her Dust Bowl migrations, her portraits of ordinary Californians navigating water, land, work, and belonging — and what her vision asks of us now.

The evening will also open into a broader conversation about the vital role spaces like Western Hills Garden play in sustaining artists and art-making in California today. Wine, snacks, and a light soup and salad supper included.

Join us for an evening of art, conversation, and California light bites including a simple soup, salad, and bread meal. Space is limited.

Artist Bios: **Tess Taylor** is a poet, playwright, and cultural critic, and the author of five poetry collections including *Last West: Roadsongs for Dorothea Lange*, *Rift Zone*, and *Work & Days* (named one of the New York Times' 10 Best Poetry Books of 2016). Her criticism appears in Harper's Magazine, The Atlantic, and The New York Times. She served as on-air poetry reviewer for NPR's All Things Considered for over a decade and was awarded an Academy of American Poets Laureate Fellowship in 2024. Her sixth collection, *Come Bite*, is forthcoming from Milkweed Editions in April 2027.

**Ciera Eis** is a bicoastal director who develops socio-political new work. Recent credits include *Last West: Roadsongs for Dorothea Lange* (Sonoma Valley Museum of Art, Oakland Museum of California, ColLABo at Carnegie Mellon University), *Hadestown* (American Conservatory Theatre YC), and *Love U: A New Musical* (Z Below). For five years she was a producer on Berkeley Repertory's New Works Summer Program, The Ground Floor. She is a founding member of the Bay Area Directors Collective and a 2024 Directors Lab West Recipient.

title: 2nd Annual BEE in Kenya Dinner and Art Auction

description:
Healdsburg, CA — \[Sept. 12\] — Following the incredible success of its first sold-out and waitlisted Bee-Inspired Benefit Dinner at Preston Farm and Winery and first BEE in Kenya dinner at Acorn, Sonoma County Bee Company is thrilled to announce their third dinner experience and Second Annual BEE in Kenya Benefit Dinner—an unforgettable evening celebrating community, conservation, and global connection.

On \[Sept 12\], guests are invited to gather at Dragonfly Floral in Healdsburg for a community-driven fundraising dinner benefiting Bee in Kenya, the nonprofit co-founded by beekeeper and Sonoma County Bee Company owner Candice Koseba.

This year's event will also feature an all-art auction, with original works generously donated by an inspiring collection of local and international artists. Local artists Jake Messing, Jessica Martin, and Sebastian Pochan to name a few. Each piece has been donated to help raise critical funds for BEE in Kenya's mission, making art an integral part of an evening dedicated to creating meaningful impact.

BEE in Kenya 501\(c\)\(3\)—short for Beekeepers and Educators Engaged in Kenya—works to empower rural Kenyan communities through ecological education and sustainable beekeeping. The organization partners with schools and community organizations throughout Kenya to foster a deeper understanding of natural ecosystems, the essential role of bees, and regenerative beekeeping practices that support environmental stewardship and long-term economic resilience.

Every ticket purchased, every auction bid, and every donation made directly supports BEE in Kenya's programs, helping provide beekeeping equipment, training, educational resources, and opportunities that strengthen both communities and the landscapes they depend on.

As Sonoma Magazine noted in its coverage of previous events: 🔗 “An Upcoming Winery Dinner in Healdsburg Is Creating a Lot of Buzz”

All proceeds from the dinner will directly support BEE in Kenya’s initiatives, including equipment grants for rural beekeepers, curriculum development for schools, and training workshops in sustainable apiculture.

Tickets are limited — and if history is any indication, they’ll sell fast. Be part of the buzz and help bring the transformative power of bees across continents.

description: England, 1605: A terrorist plot is brewing to assassinate King James 1 and blow Parliament to kingdom come! Or so the King claims. To spread his propaganda, King James 1 hires the world’s most famous playwright, William Shagspeare \(after a contemporary spelling of the Bard’s name\). As Shag investigates the King’s bizarre tale, he begins to question it, leading him and his actors to a dilemma: lie and pocket the cash, tell the truth and literally risk their necks, or perhaps equivocate–lie and tell the truth at the same time. This high-stakes thriller drops into many of the Bard’s most famous works in an alternate history that resonates today. This is a witty and poignant ensemble piece in which six actors play well over a dozen roles, some of which include snippets of Shakespeare's other plays-in-progress \(one of which becomes the famous Macbeth.\)

macbitches takes a darkly funny look at the toxic, high-stakes world of university theater, centering on a freshman who unexpectedly lands the role of Lady Macbeth. The play centers on freshman acting major Hailey, who unexpectedly scores the coveted role of Lady Macbeth. Her upperclassmen rivals immediately invite her over to “celebrate.” As the Fireball and Svedka flow, the young women interrogate their own ambitions as well as the power structures that have shaped their education—and when the night spirals into violent and shocking acts of betrayal, they come to learn that what’s done cannot be undone.

title: Safari West Presents! Shark Stewards
location: Safari West
description: Conservation Dinner Series: David McGuire of  Shark Stewards joins us in the elephant room after dinner to give a talk about sharks. The conservation dinner series is complimentary to all dinner guests. If you want to attend this presentation, please call our reservations team at \(707\) 566-3667 or \(800\) 616-2695 and they can book it for you. Dinner starts at 7:00 PM.    About the Speaker: David McGuire is the founder and director of the Ocean Health and Shark Conservation non-profit Shark Stewards. As a Research Associate of the Department of Aquatic Biology at the California Academy of Sciences, David is conducting a shark research program that includes population studies, movements and fisheries impacts. A Captain, Dive Master and filmmaker, David explores the world ocean on numerous sailing voyages producing media with an emphasis on ocean awareness. Educated in Marine Biology, he holds a master's degree in Environmental Health, has worked in education and public health at the University of California at Berkeley and is an adjunct professor at the University of San Francisco in the Department of Environmental Science. His advocacy catalyzed the coalition leading to the passage of the California Shark Conservation Act \(Fong, Huffman\) in the State of California, the Shark Conservation Act, AB 376. Since then Shark Stewards has worked in shark fin regulations in 10 US states and currently is supporting a US law to eliminate the trade of shark fins in the United States. As a documentarian and diver, he has conducted expeditions with California Academy researchers communicating the wonders of the natural world and ocean life and the need to protect them, including a two-month expedition to the Philippines where he collected and filmed for the Academy. Shark Stewards has catalyzed an alliance in Malaysian Borneo to reduce shark fishing and the shark fin trade and create marine protected areas in the Coral Triangle and develop ocean media to educate and advocate marine protection. Active in the California Marine Protected Areas and local National Marine Sanctuaries, he co-chairs the Golden Gate MPA Collaborative effort communicating the science and regulations of MPAs and facilitating compliance. David is the writer, producer and underwater cinematographer of several award-winning documentaries focusing on sharks. He has also published numerous articles on the state of the ocean and sharks and writes a National Geographic blog called Ocean Views on sharks and ocean health that is published on several online outlets. David is also an author of numerous articles and fiction and non-fiction books including Surviving the Shark. He sits on several boards of non-profits including The San Francisco Ocean Film Festival, the Green Film Festival and the Cordell Bank Marine Sanctuary Association. He has received numerous awards for his work including an award for Journalism with KQED for the investigative story Sea Horse Sleuth, the 2011 Hero of Marin Environmental Stewardship Award, and an Emmy award for his work on the documentary Reefs to Rainforests. David has been recognized by Congressman Jared Huffman for his work introducing the successful California Shark Fin Trade Ban and was awarded the Hero of Marin Award for that work. He has also been recognized as a Hero of the Environment by the Town of Pacifica for his educational and ocean conservation work. An ocean adventurer and athlete, David is an open water marathon swimmer, swimming for sharks. His current work includes an online film series called Borneo From Below and a book Surfing with Sharks.

Joe Pethoud \(drums\) and Marc Heathfield \(vocals\) quickly filled out the lineup. Marc left in 1986 and Greg Foot joined, adding another guitar and vocals. Joe left in 1987 and was replaced by George Fenley. The band self-released a cassette in 1985, and was signed to Rough Trade records in 1987. They released two LPs , Self- Entitled and Matt Dillion, and then disbanded in 1990. The band reunited 3 times with all original members -2008 for a celebration of the Chatterbox bar,  2009 for a bike messenger reunion, and in 2012 for Carmela’s wedding. Sadly, George passed away April 10th, 2013. He is greatly missed. Short Dogs have always remained friends and are currenlty writing and recording new material and playing gigs with legendary SF drummer Chewy Marzolo on drums.

In this 4 session intensive, students will create work for a soda firing while learning the history and chemistry of atmospheric Soda. Each session there will be demos and assignments that will lend to intentional and experimental decisions on the objects we make for the firing. We will make tests in clay material, slips, glazes, experiment in wadding, and placements in the kiln. During class there will be lectures on the chemistry of clay and of soda firing as well as its history, application, and experiments within the field. This class is about learning how to explore what soda can do.During the 4 weeks each student will create one cubic foot of work to be bisqued and then fired in the soda kiln. The firing will be two full days of activity, with students applying the lessons learned in class to the wadding and loading of the kiln and lighting the kiln. Students will learn how to plan a gas kiln schedule, use a kiln log, assess a kilns needs, and successfully fire off a kiln. Students will learn how to spray soda and how to maintain the kiln and her accessories in order to support Julia’s \(our beloved soda kiln\) longevity. This deep dive into soda will spark ideas and expand folx knowledge on kilns, firing, and making in clay.

Start your Sunday with a peaceful introduction to meditation in the tranquil setting of our olive orchard. We'll begin with a peaceful stroll to the orchard from our Farm Shop. Feel free to bring your own mat, though we'll also provide one if needed. Then we'll move into gentle standing stretches and mindful breathing—essential practices that prepare the body to become limber, relaxed, and comfortable for stillness. As you settle into a 20-minute meditation, Joy will hold space for your practice, opening and closing the session with the soothing sound of a singing bowl.

We'll conclude the experience back at the farm shop with fresh apple cider and sliced heirloom apples.

Joy brings firsthand experience from training in Hatha and Vinyasa yoga in Goa, India, and from completing a three-week silent meditation retreat in Thailand. Her welcoming, supportive approach creates an ideal environment for both experienced practitioners and those new to meditation. You'll also find her warmth at Gold Ridge Organic Farms, where she manages the Farm Shop and is a familiar, friendly face to our community.

title: Meditative Birding California Biodiversity Day 2026
location: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
description:
We will start off by sitting quietly for 10 minutes with Merlin app recording in 3 different locations, followed by about 10 minutes of discussion of the birds we heard, using Cornell to confirm their calls and songs before moving onto the next sitting spot. We will also saunter (while looking for birds) between the locations for a total distance of ~1.3 mile & ~250’ ascent. Birding by ear lends itself to meditation because it works best when you sit silently and listening closely (i.e., if Merlin *hears* something you did not, it reminds you that your mind has wandered).

Meet at the White Barn parking lot. Tickets are $10 for general audiences, $5 for students, youth (12-17 year olds; must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian), Sugarlof members, Sugarloaf or RFO volunteers, and free for children under 12. **Tickets day-of on site are $15 and might not be available**. 

Ensure you install the Merlin app on your device along with the bird pack for US: West Coast before you arrive for the hike, as there is no cell service is non-existent in the areas we'll be meandering. Wear layers (it's likely to be cold in the early morning) and sturdy shoes. Bring binoculars, at least a quart of water, sun protection, a bird-identification guide (if you have one), and if desired, a snack. If you are willing to carry a portable chair for about 1.3 miles, you are welcome to bring it, but there will be benches at all of our stops. Parking fees apply.

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: Nothing To See Here - Jason Perry
location: Mare Island Art Studios
description:
"Nothing To See Here" is a critical, yet playful examination of the UFO phenomenon that is hinged on the dynamic between serious scientific inquiry and fringe science.

With a mixed media approach that combines drawing, collage, and painting, Jason Perry seeks to entice the viewer into the work through familiar visual iconography, bold colors, expressive marks, and textures. Once there, the viewer is offered a deeper layer of meaning to consider. Perry calls into question the blurred narratives, misinformation, and potential truths surrounding the UFO topic.

At its core, "Nothing To See Here" invites us to look a little closer at our beliefs, our relationship to the strange, the unexplained, and our enduring fascination with what might be out there.

Expect to hear groovy covers from legendary artists like The Meters, Booker T & the M.G.'s, Herbie Hancock, Donnie Hathaway, Cannonball Adderley, and even the Beastie Boys. Whether you're a jazz head or just love good vibes, P-Butta delivers the perfect soundtrack for a Sunday afternoon in wine country.

**What's No Cell Sundays?**

It's simple: disconnect from your devices, reconnect with great wine, live music, and the people around you. *Check your phone with us at the door and receive a complimentary tasting.* Bring a blanket, grab a glass, and spend your Sunday the way it was meant to be spent.

title: FIESTA DE INDEPENDENCIA
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description:
Celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month with a taste of Latin America in Sonoma County! Enjoy authentic food, music, games, and activities for the entire family. Organized by the Center’s Latino Advisory Council, this free, family-friendly, campus-wide festival honors Latin American countries that recognize their independence during this month.

LBC also will present its annual Community Leadership Awards in partnership with Los Cien Sonoma County to an individual and an organization that have demonstrated an outstanding commitment to the Latino Community through volunteerism, education, mentorship, or other personal or professional efforts.

Fiesta de Independencia began at the Center in 2010 to commemorate Mexican Independence Day \(September 16\) and has since evolved to celebrate the rich history of the diverse Latino cultures and people who are an integral part of the North Bay community. Drawing more than 5,000 community members each year, the event has become a Sonoma County tradition. The Fiesta is a community-wide celebration of cultures, people, and traditions that also increases awareness about Hispanic history and tradition, service organizations that support our community, and the many Latinx businesses in Sonoma County.

¡Celebre el mes de la herencia hispana con una muestra de América Latina en el condado de Sonoma! Disfrute de auténtica comida, música, juegos y actividades para toda la familia.  Organizado por el Consejo Asesor Latino del Centro, este festival gratuito, familiar y que se llevará a cabo en todo el campus honra a los países latinoamericanos que reconocen su independencia durante este mes.

LBC también presentará sus Premios Anuales  de Liderazgo Comunitario en conjunto con Los Cien del Condado de Sonoma a un individuo y a una organización que hayan demostrado un compromiso sobresaliente con la comunidad latina a través del voluntariado, la educación, la tutoría u otros esfuerzos personales o profesionales.

La Fiesta de Independencia comenzó en el Centro en 2010 para conmemorar el Día de la Independencia de México \(16 de septiembre\) y desde entonces ha evolucionado para celebrar la rica historia de las diversas culturas y latinoamericanos que son parte integral de la comunidad del Norte de la Bahía. Atrayendo a más de 5,000 miembros de la comunidad cada año, el evento se ha convertido en una tradición del Condado de Sonoma. La Fiesta es una celebración comunitaria de culturas, personas y tradiciones que también aumenta la conciencia sobre la historia y la tradición hispanas, las organizaciones de servicio que apoyan a nuestra comunidad y las muchas empresas latinas en el condado de Sonoma.

description: England, 1605: A terrorist plot is brewing to assassinate King James 1 and blow Parliament to kingdom come! Or so the King claims. As Shag investigates the King’s bizarre tale, he begins to question it, leading him and his actors to a dilemma: lie and pocket the cash, tell the truth and literally risk their necks, or perhaps equivocate–lie and tell the truth at the same time. This high-stakes thriller drops into many of the Bard’s most famous works in an alternate history that resonates today. macbitches takes a darkly funny look at the toxic, high-stakes world of university theater, centering on a freshman who unexpectedly lands the role of Lady Macbeth. The play centers on freshman acting major Hailey, who unexpectedly scores the coveted role of Lady Macbeth. title: South Pacific
location: 6th Street Playhouse
description:
**An unforgettable romance set against the sweeping tides of World War II.**

Against the backdrop of the Pacific War of WWII, ***South Pacific*** blends high-stakes wartime romance with a poignant exploration of social prejudice. When spirited Navy nurse, Nellie Forbush, falls in love with a sophisticated French planter, and a young Marine lieutenant finds himself captivated by an ethereal island girl, their relationships are tested by the prejudices and pressures of a world at war. What unfolds is a deeply moving story about love, courage, and the transformative power of understanding. Featuring a soaring score by **Richard Rodgers** and **Oscar Hammerstein II**, including classics like “Some Enchanted Evening” and “There Is Nothin’ Like a Dame,” *South Pacific* remains one of the most beloved musicals of all time.

Winner of the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the original Broadway production won ten Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Best Score and Best Libretto. It is the only musical production ever to have won all four Tony Awards for acting.

SOUTH PACIFIC is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of The Rodgers & Hammerstein Organization. concordtheatricals.com

Performances run Thur, Friday, Saturday evenings at 7:30pm and Saturday and Sunday matinees at 2:00pm.

title: Myth & Archetype as seen through Poetry & Astrology
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
We invite all to a fascinating afternoon with Diana and Brian who will explore through the respective lenses of astrology and poetry, valuable insights offered by both myth and archetype, for better clarity and resilience in today’s tumultuous world.
This event features Author and Astrologer Diana Badger discussing her book "
Dance of the Archetypes: How Astrology Informs our Lives and Connects Us to the Earth",
and Author/Poet/Storyteller Brian R. Martens with his book,
"Merlin’s Wing", Mythic Poems.
This event is free, all donations gratefully invited. Selected readings from each presenter, a storytelling with Brian, then Q&A, book sales & signing
.
Refreshments for sale. OCA’s facilities are accessible to people with disabilities.
Dance of the Archetypes
by Diana Badger
Whether you’re new to astrology or already immersed in its symbolism,
Dance of the Archetypes
illuminates the zodiac in a refreshingly accessible way. With grounded wisdom, Diana connects planetary cycles to the Earth we depend on, our emotional lives, and our healing. This is a beautifully integrative guide for readers seeking relevance, connection, and purpose in rapidly changing times, brought to life by the author’s own striking photographs.
For the past 20 years, Diana Badger has woven together parallel careers as a counseling astrologer and a writer/editor, while pursuing an ongoing commitment to inner work and spiritual practice. Rooted in a reverence for the natural world and informed by multiple wisdom traditions, Diana’s work reflects a lifelong inquiry into the relationship between psyche, cosmos, and Earth. She currently devotes her time to her
Earth Sky Journal
podcast/writing, her astrology practice, tending of her garden, and adventures in local community.
Merlin’s Wing
by Brian Martens
This collection of poems is concerned with the “Human Condition” : Awareness, Transformation, and Deep Intuition. His poetry resonates with yearning, humor and intelligence in which he expresses his love and admiration for the first people, the ancestors, animal, human and plant. He asks these voices to speak through him in symbols, rhythms and revelations to reveal the deep beauty, tragedy, and unknowable mystery that surrounds him.
Brian R. Martens is an abstract Artist, Poet, Author, Creativity Facilitator, International Speaker, Myth Maker, CA Poets in the Schools Instructor, Podcaster, and Storyteller. Brian weaves poetry, myth, and reflection into all his storytelling. His first book,
Three Raven Gate
, is a collection of haiku, the form he learned from his work with Angeles Arrien Ph.D., a cross-cultural anthropologist, over the course of seven years. Brian seeks to inspire and motivate people, with articles, podcasts, creativity workshops, and poetry to recognize their own deep creative spirit and to express that to the world.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .
