location: Mystic Theatre & Music Hall
description:
**Vieux Farka Touré** 

Often referred to as “The Hendrix of the Sahara”, Vieux Farka Touré was born in Niafunké, Mali in 1981. He is the son of legendary Malian guitar player Ali Farka Touré, who died in 2006. Ali Farka Touré came from a historical tribe of soldiers, and defied his parents in becoming a musician. When Vieux was in his teens, he declared that he also wanted to be a musician. His father disapproved due to the pressures he had experienced being a musician. Rather, he wanted Vieux to become a soldier. But with help from family friend the kora maestro Toumani Diabaté, Vieux eventually convinced his father to give him his blessing to become a musician shortly before Ali passed.

Vieux was initially a drummer / calabash player at Mali’s Institut National des Arts, but secretly began playing guitar in 2001. Ali Farka Touré was weakened with cancer when Vieux announced that he was going to record an album. Ali recorded a couple of tracks with him, and these recordings, which can be heard on Vieux’s debut CD, were amongst his final ones. It has been said that the senior Touré played rough mixes of these songs when people visited him in his final days, at peace with, and proud of, his son’s talent as a musician.

In 2005, Eric Herman (still Vieux’s manager today) of Modiba Productions expressed an interest in producing an album for Vieux; this led to Vieux’s self-titled debut album, released by World Village in 2007. Ali Farka Touré’s work to tackle the problem of malaria is continued as 10% of proceeds are donated to Modiba’s “Fight Malaria” campaign in Niafunké through which over 3000 mosquito nets have been delivered to children and pregnant women in the Timbuktu region of Mali. On this first album, Vieux pays homage to his father and follows Ali’s musical tradition, giving new versions of the West African music that is echoed in the American blues. The album features Toumani Diabaté, as well as his late father.

On his second record, Fondo on Six Degrees (2009), Vieux branched out and presented his own sound: while remaining true to the roots of his father’s music he uses elements of rock, Latin music, and other African influences. The album received a great deal of critical acclaim from across the globe, and Vieux was clearly moving out of his father’s shadow.

By June 2010, Vieux was performing at the opening concert for the FIFA World Cup in South Africa. That month Vieux also released his first live album, LIVE. His live performances are highly energized and Vieux is known for dazzling crowds with his speed and dexterity on the guitar, as well as his palpable charisma and luminous smile, both of which captivate audiences from all audiences in spite of any language barriers (though Vieux does speak 8 languages).

In 2011 Vieux released his 3rd studio album, The Secret, so named because the listener will hear the secret of the blues with a blend of generations from father to son. It was produced by guitarist Eric Krasno (of the Soulive trio) and features South African-born vocalist Dave Matthews, Derek Trucks on electric slide guitar and jazz guitarist John Scofield. The title track is the last collaboration between Vieux and his late father. With the heralded release of The Secret, Vieux Farka Touré has clearly established himself as one of the world’s rare musical talents and guitar virtuosos with a distinct style that always pays homage to the past while looking towards the future.

Vieux released The Tel Aviv Session (Cumbancha) in April 2012, a collaborative project with Israeli superstar Idan Raichel dubbed ‘The Touré-Raichel Collective’ that has been hailed by fans and critics alike as a masterpiece and one of the best collaborative albums in the history of international music, drawing comparisons to Ali Farka Touré and Ry Cooder’s legendary Talking Timbuktu album.

In 2013, Vieux Farka Touré’s beautiful and critically acclaimed album Mon Pays was released as an homage to his homeland. Being that his native Mali had recently been splintered by territorial fighting between Tuareg and Islamic rebels since January 2012, Mon Pays was devoted to reminding the world about the beauty and culture of his native Mali. Translated as ‘My Country,’ this predominantly acoustic undertaking transformed into an artifact of cultural preservation. Two songs on the project - ‘Future’ and ‘Peace’ feature Sidiki Diabate’s kora leading an emotional charge complemented by Touré’s spectacular guitar work. Both tracks represent an important generational “passing of the torch” as Sidiki’s father, Toumani is considered one of the greatest living kora masters and was a close friend of Vieux’s father Ali. Mon Pays has been widely hailed as the most mature and lovely record yet from one of this generation’s most exciting artists to come out of Mali and one of world music’s true rising stars.

Vieux reunited with Idan Raichel in Paris to record, release and subsequently tour their 2nd collaborative album as The Touré-Raichel Collective in 2014. The result was yet another musical and critical triumph, titled 'The Paris Session' (Cumbancha) revered by many as not just a musical gem for the ages, but a powerful testimonial to the power of art and fraternity to transcend vast cultural and political divides. In 2015, Vieux released another unexpected, genre-bending collaborative album, this time with New York-based singer Julia Easterlin, aptly titled 'Touristes'. The album shot to the top of the iTunes World chart and earned critical acclaim, including that of John Schaefer (NPR) who called it "brilliant." On April 7, 2017, Vieux released his next album 'Samba', recorded live in front of a small audience at Applehead Studio in Woodstock, NY.

When the COVID pandemic hit in 2020 and all touring ground to a halt, Vieux stayed focussed on his craft at home. He worked tirelessly in the studio he built at his family's compound (which he named 'Studio Ali Farka Toure' in honor of his late father) to record his debut album for World Circuit Records/BMG, the prestigious UK-based record label with whom his father recorded and released most of his own work. The resulting album, 'Les Racines' (released June 2022), sees Vieux masterfully return to the deep roots of the Desert Blues music that his father introduced to the world and Vieux spent most of his career to date exploring, experimenting with, and expanding. 2022 also saw the release of a long-awaited collaborative album between Vieux and Houston-based psych-rock superstars Khruangbin called ‘Ali’ - an album on which the artists join forces to pay homage to Ali Farka Toure by reimagining eight of his songs together. The album was an instant hit around the globe, immediately getting millions of streams, enormous critical acclaim and even earning the praise of Sir Elton John who called it "one of the albums of the year - absolutely wonderful music." With each new project Vieux broadens his horizons, embraces new challenges and further entrenches his reputation as one of the world’s most talented and innovative musicians.

As a passionate champion for the people of Mali and The Sahel, Vieux founded the charity Amahrec Sahel in 2012. As part of Amahrec Sahel’s mission to support humanitarian reconstruction and culture, the charity has provided school supplies for children, supported an orphanage in Bamako and provided musical instruments for young musicians in Mali. Vieux is also the director of The Ali Farka Touré Foundation, an international organization dedicated to the preservation of Ali’s legacy and the cultural growth of Mali.

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

**ABOUT THE EVENT**
Join us virtually for an hour + of writing using Zoom. Let's keep together as much as we can during these uncertain times and keep on writing. Look for the schedule online and join us.

We’ve discovered that it’s strikingly helpful to write with other writers. See if it’s true for you at 3pm on Friday afternoon. 2. If you have difficulty with audio (don't have a microphone set up), as long as you have a speaker, you can call in (you'll see phone numbers when you log in).

3:00 - quick intros.
around 3:10 - timer starts: write for 70 mins.

description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: SQFF & International Day of Peace Festival present : Healing Through Hula
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center's International Day of Peace Festival weekend begins with a special screening of the documentary feature Healing Through Hula, presented by the San Quentin Film Festival. The film sets the tone for a weekend dedicated to exploring the many pathways to peace.

Directed by Louis Sále, Healing Through Hula tells the powerful story of Asian American and Pacific Islander men in prison who reconnect with their cultural heritage through the practice of hula. Drawing from his own lived experience, Sále chronicles a journey of healing and redemption that culminates in a moving Makahiki ceremonial ritual. The original 10-minute version of the film was first screened at the inaugural San Quentin Film Festival \(SQFF\) in 2024, where it received the award for Best Documentary Short. The evening program will include two additional short films: Processing, a SQFF25 Short Film Finalist, directed by formerly incarcerated filmmaker, artist and musician Antwan Banks Williamsand Exonerated, directed by incarcerated filmmaker Ernest “Ben Shua”Woods II. 

Following the film, attendees are invited to stay for a panel discussion featuring director Antwan Williams and Demora Henderson, the subject of Exonerated, who was released in June and continues the struggle to overturn his wrongful conviction. The conversation will be moderated by the Community Center's own Alexa Davidson.

Prior to the screening, at 5:30pm guests are invited to enjoy a reception where the Lagunitas Middle School eighth-grade class will offer refreshments as a fundraiser for their Spring 2027 Civil Rights Field Trip.

Healing Through Hula begins at 6:30pm sharp!

Slow down and float into a quieter rhythm with SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River at The Floathouse Petaluma. Launching from downtown Petaluma, this peaceful on-the-water yoga experience feels worlds away from the bustle—set in the calm, protected turning basin where the river naturally invites you to relax.

This all-levels, 90-minute session welcomes everyone, from first-time paddle boarders and yoga newcomers to experienced practitioners. We begin with a short, gentle paddle from the docks to get comfortable on your board \(knees are always welcome\), then anchor together so tidal movement won’t interrupt your flow. Once settled, you’re free to move, stretch, rest, or simply be—guided by expert instruction and supported by the shared energy of the group. Evening sessions and morning sessions allow YOU to choose the vibe that suits you best.

All equipment is provided, including extra-stable paddleboards that are wider and longer than a yoga mat, designed to help you feel grounded and secure on the water.

Perfect for locals and Bay Area visitors alike, SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River offers a rare chance to experience downtown Petaluma from the water—peaceful, playful, and deeply restorative.

It’s YOUR river. Come out and play.

title: Henry Kramer - Solo Piano
description: Henry Kramer, pianist, has been praised by The Cleveland Classical Review for his "astonishingly confident technique" and by The New York Times for "thrilling and triumphant" performances. Known for his sensitivity, stylish programming, and insightful interpretations, he gained international recognition with Second Prize at the 2016 Queen Elisabeth Competition and received a 2019 Avery Fisher Career Grant. A native of Cape Elizabeth, Maine, Kramer began piano at age 11, quickly advancing from self-taught beginnings to studying Chopin and Mozart. He went on to win major competitions including the National Chopin \(2010\), Montreal International \(2011\), and Shanghai International \(2012\), later earning top honors at the Honens Competition and joining Astral Artists. Kramer has performed widely as a soloist and recitalist, with notable debuts at Alice Tully Hall and Amsterdam's Concertgebouw. He has appeared with orchestras such as the Belgian National, Shanghai Philharmonic, and Indianapolis Symphony, collaborating with leading conductors including Marin Alsop and Stéphane Denève. His active recital schedule includes major venues and festivals across North America and beyond, with highlights in the 2025-26 season including performances with the Baton Rouge Symphony, Chamber Orchestra of Philadelphia, and appearances in New York, Montreal, Seattle, and Washington, D.C. An accomplished chamber musician, Kramer has performed with the Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center and collaborated with artists including Emmanuel Pahud and the Calidore Quartet. His recordings have received critical acclaim from BBC Music Magazine and Gramophone. Kramer is also a dedicated educator, joining the Université de Montréal faculty in 2022 after previous positions at Columbus State University, Smith College, and the University of Missouri-Kansas City. He holds degrees from Juilliard and Yale, where he studied with Julian Martin, Robert McDonald, and Boris Berman. A Steinway Artist, his pedagogical lineage traces back to Beethoven, Chopin, and Busoni.

About the musicians:
Jose Neto and Netoband
World-class guitarist
José Neto
and his band,
the Netoband
, have been performing together for over 25 years. For the last 18 years, Neto has also been touring internationally as Steve Winwood’s guitarist, collaborating on numerous songs and projects together. Neto’s life and diverse musical journey from Brazil to the United States and England was the subject of the award-winning documentary,
The Man Behind the White Guitar
, which was released to international film festivals in 2019.
The Netoband features Frank Martin – piano, Celso Alberti – drums, José Neto – guitar, Gary Brown – bass.
Glass Brick Boulevard
Created in 1991,
Greg Johnson
and
Glass Brick Boulevard
rose to acclaim in the Bay Area in the late ‘90s. Now reunited after a hiatus, they’re making soul-soothing music once again and inspiring audiences the world over. Led by their composer-pianist Johnson, the band draws on a diverse array of influences, including gospel, Beethoven, The Who, and Motown, to name just a few. Says Johnson, “If Beethoven came back as Seal, we'd be his band.” Glass Brick Boulevard is
Greg Johnson on Piano, Paul Hanson on Bassoon, Rob Fordyce on Bass and Celso Alberti on Drums.
Ken Cook Trio
Ken Cook
- Pianist, educator, composer
Californian native Ken Cook spent close to twenty-five years on the east coast free lancing, touring, recording and teaching. He has performed in Europe, Latin and South America and much of the Eastern United states with various groups including the great New Orleans singer Johnny Adams. Currently based in the SF Bay Area, he performs often with his Jazz trio and can be found backing many other west coast musicians. His music is a blend of Modern Jazz, Soul, Blues, Latin and Brazilian music. He has performed with Brazilian guitarist Ricardo Peixoto, Blues singer Terrie Odabi, cellist Mark Summer (Turtle Island String Quartet). He holds a Masters degree in Jazz Performance from the New England Conservatory in Boston and is an alum of The Berklee College of Music in Boston. He is an active clinician and educator and currently holds the Jazz piano chair in the Jazz Studies Department at Sonoma State University in Rohnert Park, CA.
The Ken Cook Trio includes
Michael Pinkham
on bass and
Kendrick Freeman
on drums.
Jaycie Grady 4Tet
The Jaycie Grady 4Tet
is a San Francisco-based jazz ensemble led by drummer J
aycie (JC) Grady
. Primarily playing contemporary jazz, their style is rooted in traditional jazz fundamentals but incorporates modern elements and diverse instrumentation, such as the violin. JC was featured recently in the San Francisco
Women in Jazz
event.
Hanson, Manring & Amendola
Bass virtuoso Michael Manring is joined by fellow master Scott Amendola and Paul Hanson on electric bassoon. Get ready for an ensemble like you've never heard before!
Paul Hanson
has recorded and/or performed with Grammy winners Bela Fleck and the Flecktones, Jon Batiste, Wayne Shorter and Taylor Eigsti. He has also recorded/ toured with Billy Cobham’s Crosswinds Ensemble, Peter Erskine, Billy Childs, Harmonica virtuoso Gregorie Maret, Billy Higgins, David Binney, Ray Charles, Charlie Hunter, Patrice Rushen, Alex Acuna, Dennis Chambers, Abraham Laboriel, Medeski Martin & Wood, Bob Weir’s RATDOG, T. Lavitz from Dixie Dregs, Jeff Coffin, Jeff Sipe, Jonas Hellborg, Afro/Cuban pianist Omar Sosa, Bob Moses, Kai Eckhardt, Peter Apfelbaum and the Hieroglyphics Ensemble, 60string bassist Ariane Cap in the group OoN, The Paul Dresher Ensemble, DAVKA, St. Joseph Ballet Company, The Klezmorim, as jazz soloist with the Oakland Eastbay Symphony Orchestra, as classical soloist with the Napa Symphony Orchestra (non-improvising) and many more.
Michael Manring
is an acclaimed American fretless bass virtuoso renowned for revolutionizing solo bass playing through innovative techniques, alternate tunings, and his signature Zon Hyperbass. A protégé of Jaco Pastorius, Manring has released multiple solo albums, including
Soliloquy
and
Small Moments
, and was named 1994 Bassist of the Year by Bass Player Magazine.
For
Scott Amendola
, the drum kit isn’t so much an instrument as a musical portal. As an ambitious composer, savvy bandleader, electronics explorer, first-call accompanist and capaciously creative foil for some of the world’s most inventive musicians, Amendola applies his wide-ranging rhythmic virtuosity to a vast array of settings. His closest musical associates include guitarists Charlie Hunter, Nels Cline, and Jeff Parker, Hammond B-3 organist Wil Blades, violinist Jenny Scheinman, saxophonist Phillip Greenlief, clarinetist Ben Goldberg, bassists Trevor Dunn, and Todd Sickafoose, players who have each forged a singular path within and beyond the realm of jazz.
While rooted in the San Francisco Bay Area scene, Amendola has woven a dense and far-reaching web of bandstand relationships that tie him to influential artists in jazz, blues, rock and new music. A potent creative catalyst, the Berkeley-based drummer is the nexus for a disparate community of musicians stretching from Los Angeles and Seattle to Chicago and New York. Whatever the context, Amendola possesses a gift for twisting musical genres in unexpected directions.
Over a career spanning more than three decades, Amendola has forged deep ties across the country, and throughout the world. As an ambitious composer, savvy bandleader, electronics explorer, first-call accompanist, and capaciously creative foil for some of the world’s most inventive musicians, Amendola applies his wide-ranging rhythmic virtuosity to a vast array of settings.
Junior Jazz All-Stars
The Junior Jazz All Starts are an extraordinary group of young music enthusiasts. This amazing ensemble is assembled and directed by Greg Johnson of Glass Brick Boulevard, and mentored by Music Directors Casey Jones - Analy High School, Bennett Friedman - Santa Rosa Junior College, and Gary Jones - Marin School of the Arts. Coming from a variety of musical backgrounds, they forage a cool, contemporary jazz sound. For the inaugural Jazz Festival they’re putting their own stamp on a few familiar Glass Brick Boulevard compositions.
The Junior Jazz All Stars are Julian Nelson on guitar, Julia Busci on drums, Robbie Paterson on Keyboards, James Paterson on Bass, Choegyal Hergenrather on Soprano and Alto Sax, and Songsten Hergenrather on Tenor Sax.

"Mostly Jokes" : Growing up with a bipolar father and a schizophrenic older brother left Aaron Foster with a combination of survivor’s guilt, depression and anxiety that has invalidated his every accomplishment, destroyed his every relationship and invaded his every waking thought. A comedy! 

First performed at the Hollywood Fringe Festival to reviews such as: "Some shows claim to be dark humor, but this was the absolute epitome of it." "You will fall in love with a man who would rather you not." "A laugh every 20 seconds." 

Foster is the former host of HGTV’s FreeStyle and has performed in theaters and comedy clubs around the country. A few of his main influences are Mike Birbiglia, Maria Bamford, Gary Gulman, Marc Maron, Taylor Tomlinson and Neal Brennan. Do with that information what you will.

title: South Pacific
location: 6th Street Playhouse
description:
**An unforgettable romance set against the sweeping tides of World War II.**

Against the backdrop of the Pacific War of WWII, ***South Pacific*** blends high-stakes wartime romance with a poignant exploration of social prejudice. When spirited Navy nurse, Nellie Forbush, falls in love with a sophisticated French planter, and a young Marine lieutenant finds himself captivated by an ethereal island girl, their relationships are tested by the prejudices and pressures of a world at war. What unfolds is a deeply moving story about love, courage, and the transformative power of understanding. Featuring a soaring score by **Richard Rodgers** and **Oscar Hammerstein II**, including classics like “Some Enchanted Evening” and “There Is Nothin’ Like a Dame,” *South Pacific* remains one of the most beloved musicals of all time.

Winner of the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the original Broadway production won ten Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Best Score and Best Libretto. It is the only musical production ever to have won all four Tony Awards for acting.

SOUTH PACIFIC is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of The Rodgers & Hammerstein Organization. concordtheatricals.com

title: Jack London State Historic Park WILD Trail Challenge
location: Jack London State Historic Park
description:
On Saturdays from Sept. 5 to Oct. 3, Jack London State Historic Park’s WILD Trail Challenge returns for a third year.  This series of five hikes covers every trail in the park for a total of 39.5 miles.  The hikes increase in duration and/or difficulty each week.

Participants can sign up for individual hikes or do them all.

The price for each hike is $15.  The park entry fee of $15 per vehicle is waived for these hikes.  Those who sign up for all five hikes before Sept. 5 save 20 percent and pay only $60.

Hike \# 1 – Historic Trails

September 5, 9 a.m.-12:30 p.m.  

A great way to warm up. This hike explores the historic sites and trails of the park. Navigate both sides of the park to discover Jack London’s Beauty Ranch, London Lake, and the Wolf House ruins.

Easy – moderate hike \(approximately 4.5 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 2 – Ancient Redwood

September 12, 9 a.m.-1 p.m.   

Meander through the redwoods and sunny oak woodlands of the park’s three Bridge Trails \(Upper, Lower, and Fallen\). The journey leads to the majestic ancient redwood, fondly known as the Grandmother Tree.

Moderate hike \(approximately 6 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 3 – Historic Orchard

September 19, 9 a.m.-1:30 p.m.   

Start Location: Note that this hike does not begin at Jack London State Historic Park

Sonoma Developmental Center

Arnold Dr, Eldridge, CA 95431

Stroll along the blue shores of Fern Lake before reaching the Historic Orchard. Learn about the history of the land and the fascinating fruit-bearing crops that thrive there.

Moderate – Difficult hike \(approximately 7 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 4 – Ridge

September 26, 9 a.m-3:30 p.m.   

Details: Hikers will gain elevation and an appreciation for the diverse habitats found within the park. They’ll also traverse part of the ever-growing Bay Area Ridge Trail.

Difficult hike \(approximately 12 miles roundtrip\)

Hike \# 5 – Summit 

October 3, 9 a.m.-2:30 p.m.     

A trek to the park summit is the perfect way to complete the WILD Trail Challenges.  Climb Sonoma Mountain to enjoy stunning views, celebrate with fellow hikers, and become a WILD One.

Difficult hike \(approximately 10 miles roundtrip\)

title: "Paddle The Petaluma: Turn to The River" Guided Kayak Tour
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
Paddle the Petaluma: Turn to The River is a relaxed, beginner-friendly guided kayak tour exploring the past, present, and future of Petaluma’s historic waterway. Launching right from downtown at The Floathouse Petaluma, you'll take part in this Sonoma County Signature Experience by spending about 90 minutes on the water in stable sit-on-top kayaks, traveling a gentle mile-and-a-half route through “Petaluma’s Longest Park.”

Along the way, you’ll raft up at docks around town, fascinating  landmarks, and riverfront gathering spaces to hear stories about how this Gold Rush-era “saltwater highway” helped shape Petaluma—and how today’s community is continuing to reinvent and reconnect with the river. This isn’t just a history tour. You’ll also learn about the people, businesses, artists, nonprofits, and river advocates helping shape the waterway’s future right now.

Everything is included in the $75 experience: kayak, gear, knowledgeable local guides, insider river stories, and post-paddle perks at nearby businesses. Finish with plenty of time for brunch, coffee, shopping, or simply hanging out downtown by the water. No experience necessary.

Note: The Floathouse Petaluma is a nonprofit project dedicated to “putting butts in boats and smiles on faces” by offering year-round easy access to the Petaluma River in and on people-powered water craft through rentals, events, classes, lessons and summer camps.

location: Sonoma Community Center
description:

In this special four-week workshop, participants will explore the unique art of reduction relief printmaking. Acclaimed guest artist, Tomoko Murakami, will demonstrate how to create multi-color prints from a single linoleum block. The main idea is to gradually carve away parts of the block and print each new layer of color, with each layer building on the previous one. The course covers the entire process, from designing and planning, to carving techniques, inking, registration, and printing with both hand and printing press methods. Participants will learn to explore the possibilities of color mixing and layering, enabling students to achieve intricate designs and a wide range of visual effects. You will gain an understanding of the materials, processes, and innovations involved in this unique form of relief print printing!All levels are welcome, including continuing linocut students. Please note: This class requires hand dexterity to maneuver the carving tool. Participants should feel comfortable standing, and using tools with sharp blades and edges.

title: You are Invited to North Bay Speech Masters Toastmasters Club Meeting
location: Cogir of the North Bay
description:
Whether it's improving our health, focusing on professional advancement, learning a new skill, it is often helpful to obtain someone to help learn new skills like speaking without preparation. The group at Toastmasters can help.

We call speaking without preparation, impromptu speaking. If you want to learn new Impromptu speaking skills, Toastmasters can help. During the meeting, we will practice our impromptu speaking skills during our session we call Table Topics. During the Table Topics, the speaker is given a question, and they are asked to speak for 60 seconds to 2 minutes about the question.

Outside Toastmasters, impromptu speaking happens constantly. You might recognize it in moments such as:

--Being asked for your opinion in a meeting

--Responding to a follow-up question during a presentation

--Introducing yourself or someone else unexpectedly

--Handling a difficult or unplanned question

You can learn tips and tricks about speaking off the cuff at our meeting. Won't you join us and learn

what Toastmasters can do to help you on your professional journey.

Feel free to contact us for the zoon link at our website under the "Contact Us" button. The website is https://3038.toastmastersclubs.org

We hold meetings online and in-person. If joining us in-person, there is limited parking in the front lot. Once in the front door, please sign in at the computer to obtain a visitors' badge. \(IUsually, there is a sheet by the computer telling you how to log in for Toastmasters.\) If the sheet isn't there, the clerk at the desk can help. Then take the elevator down to the second floor, and take a left out of the elevator and a left at the hall and come down to the meeting room.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room

description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: Redwood Writers General Meeting Genre Panel
location: Finley
description:
Want to learn inside tips about writing and meet local authors?

You're invited to

Redwood Writers General Meeting, networking, and potluck \(Please bring a dish to share of you like.\)

Join us for an engaging panel conversation with three fiction writers, each a master of their own genre — Crime/Thriller, Speculative Fiction, and Romance. From the thrill of the unexpected to the pull of unforgettable characters, our panelists will pull back the curtain on what it really takes to craft a novel readers can’t put down.

Whether you’re a lifelong bookworm, an aspiring writer, or simply curious about what goes on behind the page, this is your chance to hear firsthand how great stories are made, and why genre matters more than you might think. This meeting is for all storytellers, no matter what genre you write in!

Panelists:

Ellen Kirschman Crime/Thriller

Please welcome Ellen Kirschman, author of the five-book Dot Meyerhoff mystery series. A retired police psychologist herself, Ellen brings real insider knowledge to her fictional counterpart Dot — a police psychologist who takes orders from no one and keeps solving crimes she should be leaving to the cops. Ellen lives in Santa Rosa and is a member of Mystery Writers of America, Sisters in Crime, and the Public Safety Writers Association. https://ellenkirschman.com/

Mara Lynn Johnstone Science Fiction & Fantasy

Please welcome Mara Lynn Johnstone, author of multiple books exploring other worlds — aliens, robots, shapeshifters, magicians, and the occasional precisely-timed witty banter. Known for memorable characters and a knack for turning genre tropes on their head, Mara Lynn is also President of Redwood Writers. You can find her up a tree, in a bookstore, or lost in thought… https://www.maralynnjohnstone.com/

Crissi Langwell Small-Town Romance & Women’s Fiction

Please welcome Crissi Langwell, a multi-genre author whose work spans romance, women’s fiction, and speculative storytelling — all centered on deeply human characters and heartfelt emotional journeys. From her award-winning Sunset Bay series to her newest small-town Lahoma Springs romances, her novels blend heartache, hope, and humor into stories that feel both intimate and real. Crissi lives in Northern California with her writerly husband, their Maine Coon cat Cleo, and a chair of laundry that really needs to get its act together. https://crissilangwell.com/

Educational displays will showcase mosquito and tick surveillance methods used to identify and prevent emerging threats to public health, non-toxic rodent control strategies, and simple tips for reducing mosquito sources around the home.

Guests can learn how mosquito traps work, meet the vector control technicians who respond to service requests, and leave with practical, easy-to-use information to help protect their families and neighborhoods.

Whether you are stopping by to learn, ask questions, or enjoy a day of discovery, the District’s Open House offers a welcoming opportunity to connect with the people dedicated to keeping Marin and Sonoma counties safe from mosquitoes and vector-borne diseases.

title: Public Garden Tour
location: Occidental Arts and Ecology Center
description:
Join us for a guided tour of the Occidental Arts & Ecology Center's demonstration gardens and living landscapes. Led by rotating OAEC staff, these tours offer an opportunity to explore our diverse food, medicinal, pollinator, and native plant gardens while learning about the ecological principles that guide our work. 

When: Tours start at 1 pm every first and third Saturday of the month, April through October. 

Where: Tours start and end at the OAEC Nursery. 15290 Coleman Valley Rd, Occidental, CA 95465. Upper Driveway. 

Important Information:

No registration required—just show up!

Please use the second driveway and park in the upper lot near the greenhouses.

The tour route includes steep hills and unpaved dirt and gravel paths. Sturdy shoes, a brimmed hat, and weather-appropriate layers are recommended.

If you require mobility support or have other accessibility needs, please call ahead so we can accommodate you. Monday–Friday, contact the main office at \(707\) 874-1557 ext. 101.

A highlight of every tour is the OAEC Nursery, a nonprofit nursery dedicated to uplifting ecologically and culturally important plants. The nursery features a wide selection of perennial food crops, medicinal and native plants, and an ever-evolving collection of annual vegetables and herbs adapted to our region.

title: The Things We Never Say by Elizabeth Strout [OPTION 1]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
Publisher's description: Artie Dam is living a double life. He spends his days teaching history to eleventh graders, expanding their young minds, correcting their casual cruelties, and lending a kind word to those who need it most. He goes to holiday parties with his wife of three decades, makes small talk with neighbors, and, on weekends, takes his sailboat out on the beautiful Massachusetts Bay. He is, by all appearances, present and alive. But inside, Artie is plagued by feelings of isolation. He looks out at a world gone mad—at himself and the people around him—and turns a question over and over in his mind: How is it that we know so little about one another, even those closest to us?

And then, one day, Artie learns that life has been keeping a secret from him, one that threatens to upend his entire world. Once he learns it, he is forced to chart a new course, to reconsider the relationships he holds most dear—and to make peace with the mysteries at the heart of our existence.

Elizabeth Strout, as we have come to expect, delivers a moving exploration of the human condition—one that brims with compassion for each and every one of her indelible characters. With exquisite prose and profound insight, *The Things We Never Say* takes one man’s fears and loneliness and makes them universal. And in the same breath, captures the abiding love that sustains and holds us all.

"I haven't enjoyed a Strout book this much in years. Strout takes you inside Artie, gradually revealing pieces of his past and his relationships. Despite the premise, much of the book is upbeat, and when it isn't, we're rooting for Artie." - Joan

"More wonderful characters and interesting narrative from Strout. Highly recommend." - Dave

"I too, am a fan of *The Things We Never Say.* I was immediately drawn into this novel. Can't wait!"

description:
**An unforgettable romance set against the sweeping tides of World War II.**

Against the backdrop of the Pacific War of WWII, ***South Pacific*** blends high-stakes wartime romance with a poignant exploration of social prejudice. When spirited Navy nurse, Nellie Forbush, falls in love with a sophisticated French planter, and a young Marine lieutenant finds himself captivated by an ethereal island girl, their relationships are tested by the prejudices and pressures of a world at war. What unfolds is a deeply moving story about love, courage, and the transformative power of understanding. Featuring a soaring score by **Richard Rodgers** and **Oscar Hammerstein II**, including classics like “Some Enchanted Evening” and “There Is Nothin’ Like a Dame,” *South Pacific* remains one of the most beloved musicals of all time.

Winner of the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the original Broadway production won ten Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Best Score and Best Libretto. It is the only musical production ever to have won all four Tony Awards for acting.

SOUTH PACIFIC is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of The Rodgers & Hammerstein Organization. concordtheatricals.com

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
location: Buena Vista Historical Winery
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: macbitches

description:
“macbitches takes Shakespearean themes and grounds them in a recognizable, modern reality — a smarter, theater-centered Mean Girls, if you will. It’s funny, sharp, and unafraid to let women be complicated.” - Jeanette Seisdedos, director

macbitches takes a darkly funny look at the toxic, high-stakes world of university theater, centering on a freshman who unexpectedly lands the role of Lady Macbeth. The play centers on freshman acting major Hailey, who unexpectedly scores the coveted role of Lady Macbeth. Her upperclassmen rivals immediately invite her over to “celebrate.” As the Fireball and Svedka flow, the young women interrogate their own ambitions as well as the power structures that have shaped their education—and when the night spirals into violent and shocking acts of betrayal, they come to learn that what’s done cannot be undone.

title: Safari West Presents! National Wildlife Federation
location: Safari West
description: ConservationDinner Series: Beth Pratt of  National Wildlife Federation joins us in the elephant room after dinner to give a talk about the Mountain Lions. The conservation dinner series is complimentary to all dinner guests. If you want to attend this presentation, please call our reservations team at \(707\) 566-3667 or \(800\) 616-2695 and they can book it for you. Dinner starts at 7:00 PM. Being Good Neighbors for Wildlife: Did you know that a family of foxes thrives on the Facebook campus in Silicon Valley? Or that a mountain lion lives in the middle of Los Angeles? Beth Pratt-Bergstrom, California Director for the National Wildlife Federation and author of the book,  When Mountain Lions are Neighbors: Wildlife in Today's California , will tell some remarkable stories of how-sometimes in the most unlikely of places-people are being good neighbors for wildlife in the Golden State, and why coexistence with wild animals is vital for their survival. Biography A lifelong advocate for wildlife, Beth Pratt has worked in environmental leadership roles for over thirty years, and in two of the country's largest national parks: Yosemite and Yellowstone. As the California Regional Executive Director for the National Wildlife Federation, Pratt leads the \#SaveLACougars campaign to build the Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing, which broke ground on Earth Day in 2022. The largest wildlife crossing of its kind in the world, it will help save a population of mountain lions from extinction. Her innovative conservation work has been featured by The New Yorker, The Wall Street Journal, Washington Post, BBC World Service, CNN, CBS This Morning, the Los Angeles Times, Men's Journal, The Guardian, NPR, AP News, and more. Her books include When Mountain Lions are Neighbors, published by Heyday in 2024, and I Heart Wildlife: A Guided Activity Journal for Connecting With the Wild World, by Di Angelo Publications in 2020. Her new book, Yosemite Wildlife: The Wonder of Animal Life in California's Sierra Nevada, will be published by the Yosemite Conservancy in 2025. Beth has also given a TEDx talk about coexisting with wildlife called, "How a Lonely Cougar in Los Angeles Inspired the World," is featured in the documentary, "The Cat that Changed America," on CNN's Heroes in Conservation series, and the new reboot of Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom. Beth obtained a BS/BA from the University of Massachusetts, an MBA from Regis University, earned the LEED AP credential, and trained with Vice President Al Gore as part of his Climate Reality Leadership Corps. In 2007, she traveled to Japan as part of a month-long Rotary International Professional Exchange to study business and national park operations. Beth also served as a founding board member and the board chair for the nonprofit Outdoor Afro for eight years. The Western Section of the Wildlife Society named her "Conservationist of the Year" in 2023, and in 2024, she received the Alan Rabinowitz Conservation award from the Explorers Club. Beth spends much of her time in Los Angeles, but makes her home outside of Yosemite, "my north star," with her six dogs, two cats, and the mountain lions, bears, foxes, frogs, and other wildlife that frequent her backyard. More information at  www.bethpratt.com or  www.101wildlifecrossing.org

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: Petaluma River History Paddle
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
Enjoy a uniquely Petaluma experience on the water. This two-hour, gentle guided kayak tour launches from The Floathouse Petaluma and explores the river that once served as the region's "saltwater highway." Long before roads and railways, the Petaluma River powered San Francisco, the Gold Rush miners, and even global markets with the produce from local farms and industries, supplying everything from eggs to overalls.

Designed and led by a Petaluman, actor and former history teacher this entertaining and enlightening tour brings history to life through storytelling enhanced by costumed actors on shore. You'll hear fascinating stories from the perspectives of long-ago Petalumans—young workers, entrepreneurs, and colorful characters whose daily lives revolved around the river.

Paddle in stable sit-on-top kayaks through and beyond Petaluma's charming downtown, while gaining a deeper appreciation for how this tidal waterway shaped the city and the region. Visitors are often surprised by how much they learn—and many come back with friends.

$75 per person, all-inclusive. No paddling experience necessary. All equipment provided.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: Ceramic Carving - Mini Ofrenda Bowls
location: Art Escape
description:
Join Kelly from No Peach Ceramics for this special ceramic carving class. 

Hand carve a set of mini ofrenda bowls for your home altar! Each participant will receive 4–6 handmade bowls to personalize using simple carving techniques and colorful glazes.

Sgraffito is an ancient technique of surface decoration that involves scratching or carving through a layer to reveal a contrasting color beneath. During the course of this 3-hour workshop, we will cover the fundamentals of which tools and techniques to best apply \(and then remove\) slips and underglazes to a pre-prepared clay "canvas". Demonstrations of when and how to carve successfully will be supplemented with in-depth advice on each aspect of the sgraffito process. 

 All experience levels are welcome! You will be provided with materials, tools, and forms to practice sgraffito and make your own unique platter. Bringing inspiration photos and design ideas is welcomed and encouraged! We will be providing one pre-prepared raw clay platter per student to use during the course. After the class, we will fire your finished piece, and it will be ready for pickup within 2-3 weeks.

title: Nothing To See Here - Jason Perry
location: Mare Island Art Studios
description:
"Nothing To See Here" is a critical, yet playful examination of the UFO phenomenon that is hinged on the dynamic between serious scientific inquiry and fringe science.

With a mixed media approach that combines drawing, collage, and painting, Jason Perry seeks to entice the viewer into the work through familiar visual iconography, bold colors, expressive marks, and textures. Once there, the viewer is offered a deeper layer of meaning to consider. Perry calls into question the blurred narratives, misinformation, and potential truths surrounding the UFO topic.

At its core, "Nothing To See Here" invites us to look a little closer at our beliefs, our relationship to the strange, the unexplained, and our enduring fascination with what might be out there.

title: No Cell Sundays: Callie Watts & Kris Dilbeck
location: Hook & Ladder Winery
description:
**Callie Watts: Where Classic Sounds Meet Modern Soul**

Join us for No Cell Sundays with Callie Watts, a Northern California pop singer-songwriter whose sound is steeped in the golden era of songwriting.

Raised on classical music, The Beatles, and The Beach Boys, Callie discovered her calling through the great writers of the '60s and '70s—Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, and Carole King. These legendary artists shaped her melodic writing style and continue to influence every note she plays.

A versatile musician, Callie has spent her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, arranger, and lead/backing vocalist—performing solo and with local and Bay Area bands across multiple genres. Expect an afternoon of soulful melodies, timeless classics, and songs that transport you back to when music was everything.

**What's No Cell Sundays?**

It's simple: disconnect from your devices, reconnect with great wine, live music, and the people around you. *Check your phone with us at the door and receive a complimentary tasting.* Bring a blanket, grab a glass, and spend your Sunday the way it was meant to be spent.

title: Contemplating Climate Change, with Trevor Houser
location: St. Columba's Inverness
description:
Contemplating Climate Change, with Trevor Houser

Sunday, September 20, 1:00 pm 

In this Iona Lecture, climate change researcher and former diplomat Trevor Houser will provide an overview of the current state of global efforts to address climate change and constructive steps individuals and communities can take to advance those efforts. He will also reflect on how faith can provide both a refuge from environmental anxiety and a guide to personal engagement. 

Join us for this important afternoon of conversation with lecture at 1 pm and wine and cheese reception to follow.  Free and Open to the Public. 

Trevor Houser is a partner at Rhodium Group, an independent research provider. He leads the company's Energy & Climate practice, which analyzes the effects of policy and market developments on greenhouse gas emissions and energy systems. Trevor also co-directs the Climate Impact Lab, a consortium of leading research institutions quantifying the impact of climate change on communities around the world.

Trevor previously served as a climate change negotiator for the U.S. Department of State and as a Visiting Fellow at the Peterson Institution for International Economics. He has written three books on energy policy and global climate change, including The Economic Risks of Climate Change: An American Perspective.

title: Melba's Kitchen Big Band - Jazz Super Sunday
location: Vino Godfather Winery
description: MELBA’S KITCHEN Big Band - the “crackling 14\+ piece all-woman unit…” \(Downbeat magazine\) - presents a concert and dance to celebrate the music of Black women musical geniuses Melba Liston, Mary Lou Williams, and their friends. 2026 is Melba Liston’s Centennial, and the band is raring to return to Vallejo and bring the party! Over nearly ten years of performing at venues including YOSHI’S Oakland, SFJAZZ Miner Auditorium, Berkeley’s Freight and Salvage, the Healdsburg Jazz Festival, SF’s de Young Museum, the band has excited audiences and earned rave reviews. “They’re so astonishing…They’re so swinging!”- Dee Spencer, jazz professor. “A marvelous night with good vibes all around!” - Rebecca Mauleon, SFJAZZ. “A talent-packed ensemble…” - Andy Gilbert, jazz journalist. Sunday afternoon’s lawn party is your chance to tear up the outdoor dance floor AND soak in the strains of authentic blues-drenched jazz compositions from the thirties through today - tunes as new as tomorrow morning. MELBA’S KITCHEN will be playing Quincy Jones, Stevie Wonder, Sly Stone, Basie, Abbey Lincoln, and more, including sophisticated and swinging Liston, Mary Lou Williams, and band originals. Just the ticket for a hip and relaxing step into Bay Area Autumn! A little background about Melba and Mary Lou: The jazz great MELBA LISTON made formidable contributions to jazz. Liston toured with and wrote for Dizzy Gillespie, Quincy Jones, Gerald Wilson, and collaborated for decades - in the Ellington/ Strayhorn mode - with piano titan Randy Weston. Liston had a great big beautiful sound on the trombone, and was a pioneer as a woman in jazz. She arranged for many, including Abbey Lincoln, Betty Carter, Marvin Gaye, Clark Terry, and Ruth Brown. MARY LOU WILLIAMS, an activist for jazz, was a virtuosic and inspired pianist, composer, and arranger. Although Williams attained a level of visibility and recording success, her work has remained in relative shadow. MELBA’S KITCHEN intends to bring Liston’s and Williams’ names into your musical household. Melba Liston has earned her spot in the jazz firmament with other 2026 jazz centennial greats, like Coltrane, Miles and Randy Weston. Come dance and celebrate the music with us! “macbitches takes Shakespearean themes and grounds them in a recognizable, modern reality — a smarter, theater-centered Mean Girls, if you will. It’s funny, sharp, and unafraid to let women be complicated.” - Jeanette Seisdedos, director

macbitches takes a darkly funny look at the toxic, high-stakes world of university theater, centering on a freshman who unexpectedly lands the role of Lady Macbeth. The play centers on freshman acting major Hailey, who unexpectedly scores the coveted role of Lady Macbeth. Her upperclassmen rivals immediately invite her over to “celebrate.” As the Fireball and Svedka flow, the young women interrogate their own ambitions as well as the power structures that have shaped their education—and when the night spirals into violent and shocking acts of betrayal, they come to learn that what’s done cannot be undone.

title: San Geronimo Valley Community Center's Peace Fest : Art and Music Festival
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The Sunday afternoon of Peace Fest celebrates creativity, community, and the ways music and art can inspire peace and human connection.

The festivities begin at 2 p.m. with a ceremonial blessing by Henry Frank, whose wisdom and presence have become a treasured Peace Fest tradition. Visitors can also experience Henry Frank: A Human Experience in the West Room, while the Valley Room will feature artwork from the William James Association's Prison Arts Project.

Outside, students from Lagunitas School will exhibit peace-inspired artwork created following Ashanti Branch's Taking Off the Mask workshop. Through interactive activities and thoughtful conversation, students explore identity, empathy, and authentic connection, expressing both their inner and outer selves through art. Also, outside near the Courtyard the GreenStitch Climate Action interns will once again create one of their vibrant community chalk murals, illustrating the connection between climate protection and world peace.

Following the blessing, we are excited to present all the way from Paraquay, Orquestra de Reciclados de Cateura, an internationally acclaimed youth ensemble from Paraguay whose musicians perform on instruments handcrafted from recycled materials recovered from a landfill. The instruments played by the orchestra members mimic violins, violas, cellos, double basses, guitars, flutes, saxophones, trumpets, trombones, and percussion instruments, yet they are constructed from refuse. Their repertoire includes classical, folk, Paraguayan, and Latin American music, as well as songs by the Beatles and Frank Sinatra, among others. Their inspiring story of resilience, creativity, and hope beautifully reflects the spirit of Peace Fest.

Peace Fest will then welcome Enriching Lives Through Music \(ELM\) for the first time. The youth music education program provides young people with immersive musical experiences, mentorship, and the resources to pursue their artistic dreams. Their talented young performers promise to bring energy, enthusiasm, and inspiration to the afternoon.

Closing this year's festival is featured headliner AgapéSoul, led by bassist, songwriter, and producer Darryl Anders.Blending soul, funk, jazz, and R&B, AgapéSoul delivers uplifting performances centered on hope, healing, and connection. Anders has performed with the legendary Tower of Power and toured and recorded with Meters drummer Zigaboo Modeliste, bringing decades of musical experience to the Peace Fest stage.

As Anders describes it, "The name AgapéSoul comes from the Greek word Agape—meaning God's unconditional love—and Soul, the place within us where music comes from. It also reflects the style of music I feel connected to. As an artist, I feel it's important to speak on issues that are crucial to the healing of our society."

title: South Pacific
location: 6th Street Playhouse
description:
**An unforgettable romance set against the sweeping tides of World War II.**

Against the backdrop of the Pacific War of WWII, ***South Pacific*** blends high-stakes wartime romance with a poignant exploration of social prejudice. When spirited Navy nurse, Nellie Forbush, falls in love with a sophisticated French planter, and a young Marine lieutenant finds himself captivated by an ethereal island girl, their relationships are tested by the prejudices and pressures of a world at war. What unfolds is a deeply moving story about love, courage, and the transformative power of understanding. Featuring a soaring score by **Richard Rodgers** and **Oscar Hammerstein II**, including classics like “Some Enchanted Evening” and “There Is Nothin’ Like a Dame,” *South Pacific* remains one of the most beloved musicals of all time.

Winner of the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the original Broadway production won ten Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Best Score and Best Libretto. It is the only musical production ever to have won all four Tony Awards for acting.

SOUTH PACIFIC is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of The Rodgers & Hammerstein Organization. concordtheatricals.com

Performances run Thur, Friday, Saturday evenings at 7:30pm and Saturday and Sunday matinees at 2:00pm.

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
location: Buena Vista Historical Winery
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: Ravi Coltrave Quartet: Centennial Celebration
location: The Raven Performing Arts Theater
description:
Just days before John Coltrane would have turned 100, his son, saxophonist Ravi Coltrane, presents a blazing young band to mark the milestone. Ravi, 60, spent the first quarter-century of his career acquiring a diverse array of experience and honing his own lustrous, harmonically slippery compositions. But in recent years he’s taken up the family mantle with a variety of projects and initiatives on and off the bandstand, championing the legacy of both his parents, John and Alice Coltrane. 

For this celebration, he’s joined by the brilliant trumpeter Jonathan Finlayson, a longtime collaborator who graduated from Berkeley High. Israeli pianist/keyboardist Gadi Lehavi made his Village Vanguard debut with Ravi at 15. Now 30, he’s more than lived up to his enormous potential. Powering the quartet is Bay Area-reared drum sensation Elé Howell, 28, a supremely musical accompanist who gained national attention when Coltrane started hiring him in 2021 for various projects, including Cosmic Music: Revisiting the Music of John and Alice Coltrane.

John Coltrane's presence continues to illuminate new directions for exploration. Join us for this special Centennial Celebration with Ravi Coltrane and his band.

Chown began his career at SRJC at age 24, working in the campus photography lab. Experience the distinction of this system verses other modern yoga/vinyasa practices commonly taught & the traditional & precise use of ujjayi breath as it relates to the Sanskrit parameters, moving with the breath and the importance of the pause. Talasana is a very unique & profound krama initiating & establishing "samasthiti", the steadiness and focus of mind, balanced energy and steadiness of body - with the two feet together, moving from the center, all the major joints and muscles of the body are exercised using arm and hand movements, back bends, side bends, twists, forward bends, squats and balancing foot stretches. The fingers interlaced create a prana circuit as they come together in the repetitive movement over the head. The breath specific movements stretch the diaphragm, psoas, massage the heart and internal organs, clear the lungs, drain the lymphatic system, stimulate the vagus nerve and calm the mind. Energy is created along the spine and central nervous system, and is distributed throughout the nadis and into the entire energy body. Regular practice of Talasana flowers into to ananta samapatti and understanding "stillness in movement".
Class begins with Opening Mantras & Ding Namaskar (Devotional Salutation to the Directional Spheres with Breath & Mantra). Then moves to Tāĺāsana to Savasana then Seated Prānāyāma (Yogic Breathing) including Morning Cleansing Kriyas, Ujjayi, Nadi Shuddi, Samantraka Prānāyāma, Pratyahara, Dharana. May include Specific Mudra (Energetic Bodily Gestures).
