title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Come, step onto your mat with an open heart and an open mind.

Pay Online 4 sessions
Tirza Dawn Naramore
is a yogi, mother, artist, ceremonialist and lover of life. She has been practicing and teaching yoga and meditation for 30 years and offers yoga retreats and trainings that center on optimum health, self realization and self love. Her teachers are from many yoga and tantric traditions, but her primary lineages are Iyengar and Kali Ray.
Tirza is deeply devoted to community building and is honored to have created a number of community supported non profits including Mystic Family Circus and The AWAKEN Project, which serves families with children on the autism spectrum. Tirza is proud to be the mother of 3 wild teenagers, including her incredible son who is diagnosed with autism.
Tirza’s spirituality is one of many influences and teachings. Beginning with a Christian up-bringing and being raised on a Christian commune in her early childhood, she later expanded into more earth-based ways. While in her 20’s Tirza was adopted into the Native American Church, where she learned from her relatives a way of living the “Beauty Way.”
During the 1990’s and early 2000’s, Tirza lived in San Francisco, Oakland and Berkeley, directing the Mystic Family Circus, which was a performance group dedicated to cultural awareness and bridge building. She worked with Cirque du Soleil, Burning Man, Reclaiming, Contraband, CELLspace and other Bay Area art collectives and non profits to provide conscious entertainment and “prayerformances” for the betterment of humankind and the planet.
In 2012, Tirza helped to found the Buckeye Gathering, an ancestral skills gathering in Northern California which draws teachers and students of all ages to learn ancestral ways of tending the earth and survival skills.
Tirza Dawn was the founder of yoga programming and the Ayurvedic Yoga Teacher Trainings at the dhyana Center of Ayurveda in Sebastopol, California, which operated a community center of healing and education from 2010 to 2020.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

The event will be presented in partnership with local civic, faith, and wellness leaders. Musicians will include Sukhawat Ali Khan Band, Vox Populi, Sophia Sanchez, and René Jenkins.

As part of the opening ceremony, there will be a minute of silence at 12 PM to coincide with the UN International Day of Peace moment of silence around the world. Guided meditations and an afternoon talk will be provided by Sonoma Ashram Founder Baba Harihar Ramji, affectionately known as “Babaji." Babaji has inspired people in the Sonoma Valley for over 35 years. His teachings emphasize living simply, inner freedom, and selfless service.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: Keith Hansen: "For the Love of Birds and the Joy of Birding"
location: First United Methodist Church
description:
Join Keith Hansen for a lively dive into what inspired him to take up illustrating birds and eventually to become a bird book author. He has recently finished his 13th and 14th books entitled Hansen’s Field Guide to the Birds of the Sierra Nevada and The Birds of Point Reyes.

Talk begins at 7pm, following 6:30pm Madrone Audubon monthly general meeting.

Keith, who comes from an artistic family, has been looking at birds from the age of 10 and illustrating them since the 12th grade. Growing up, he and his older brother Rob birded every spare moment they could, first in the woods of Maryland, before moving to Fresno, California in 1970. He did work at Point Reyes Bird Observatory’s Palomarin Field Station and then spent 9 years on the SE Farallon Island, where he banded, photographed and studied hundreds of birds up close. He has traveled extensively through the New World Tropics including Mexico, Guatemala, Costa Rica, Panama, Ecuador, Colombia, Trinidad and Tobago, Guyana, the Amazon, and the Galapagos, where he filmed 100s of species for his artwork. His current project is illustrating all the birds of N. America for an app called FLOCK.

Come and join us!

title: Lavender Labyrinth Sound Bath Experience
location: Bees n blooms
description:
Join us in our most dreamy location yet, in the center of a lavender labyrinth for an exquisite sunset sound Bath Experience!

Join us in our most dreamy location yet, in the middle of lavender labyrinth at sunset!

Mondays through October 6th

We are thrilled to share this magic with you! Let the fragrance of lavender fill and sooth your senses as the sound expands your awareness.

Sound baths create the space for self-healing and transformation. The resonance of the instruments is not just an auditory experience ~ it's like receiving a full body sound massage.

There will be 8 Gongs, Crystal singing bowls, Hand pan, Mono chord, Chimes galore, Ocean drum, Native drum, Angelic Vocals & more.The vibrations will transport you on a powerful healing journey!

PLEASE NOTE: The sound bath starts at 7pm. Gates close at 6:45 PM. Please be Mindful of timing. You will need time to park, walk up and set up. You are welcome to come walk the labyrinth and visit the Farm Stand from 6 pm onward. Please check the hourly weather so you are prepaired. You will be lying on the grass, so please bring all that you will need to feel cozy and warm, "yoga mat" or camping pad, "Blanket" or sleeping bag, a pillow, eye mask, and water bottle. Wonderful Lavender Eye Masks will be available to purchase for $25 by the Bees & Blooms Farm Stand.

If we have environmental Circumstance such as rain or unhealthy air quality due to fires we will postpone to Wednesday of the same week and your tickets will roll over to that day. If these conditions are present it is your responsibility to monitor your emails\(also junk/spam\) for notifications. In these force of nature situations Tickets are not refundable but are transferable! Your understanding and cooperation is greatly appreciated.

Please be informed that there are bee hives on site and there may be bees on the lavender plants. If you are allergic to bee stings, bring your Epipen. An incident is unlikely, but best to be prepared. Also, at some point, probably mid July the Lavender will began to be harvested so there may be less lavender towards the end of the month.Full Bloom occurs mid June. The last sound bath of the Lavender season will be Oct. 6th. The labyrinth & farm will be beautiful however the Lavender will be reaching the end of its cycle around mid. July. You will walk through many rows of a varity of blooming flowers on you way from parking.

Only disability trained Registered Service dogs are permitted because of the animals on the farm and the nature of the Sound Bath. Your understanding is appreciated. Also, please no children under 10 years of age.

Labyrinths represent a metaphor for your life path and the journey you are making. While walking the path of the labyrinth, either alone or with a group, focus on your feelings and emotions to allow you to connect with yourself. You may also want to choose a meditation that you are comfortable with in order to clear and quiet your mind. The uses of a labyrinth are many; relief from stress and anxiety, healing, meditation, problem solving, enhancing intuition, expanding thought processes, communicating with the Divine, balancing mind, body and spirit, letting go of unwanted energies, obtaining goals, celebrating and remembering others, building trust in yourself or others, and coping with grief, sorrow and loss. The labyrinth is an ancient symbol that relates to wholeness. It combines the imagery of the circle and the spiral into a meandering but purposeful path. The Labyrinth represents a journey to our own center and back again out into the world. Labyrinths have long been used as meditation and prayer tools.

Looking forward to sharing this Extraordinary Experience with you! In Gratitude

location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

This class is designed for dancers who have a solid grasp of the basics and are eager to expand their repertoire with more complex and fluid movements.

Salsa Class Beginners

Each week, we’ll break down a new move, focusing on the technique and connection that will make you a more confident and stylish dancer. We’ll go beyond the foundational steps to cover a wide range of essential intermediate patterns and styling, including:

Turns and Spins:

Master your inside and outside turns, double spins, and the elegant 360 and Hand Toss moves.

Intricate Patterns:

Learn to execute the 360, wrap, as well as various Cross Body Lead variations like the U-Turn and Spiral.

Footwork and Styling:

Enhance your rhythm and flair with advanced footwork like the Suzy Q, Front Tap, and Mambo Step. We’ll also work on styling with a wrap and improving your posture and upper body movement.

This class is your chance to refine your technique, improve your lead-follow connection, and add a variety of fun and dynamic moves to your salsa vocabulary. Join us and elevate your dance!

title: Artist's Way Group Next Chapter: "The Book of Alchemy"
location: Alibi Bookshop
description: Creativity is my way of making sense of the world.” — Suleika Jaouad  Are you feeling an urge to pick up a pen or paintbrush or pair of scissors and unleash your creativity, but not sure where to start? Or are you looking to find community, to motivate your creative self and make new friends? This might be just the thing for you. Two years ago, we formed an “Artist’s Way” group here at the shop, and continued it again last year. It was extraordinary. Not only did people write and paint and create, but got published and found new life paths. \(And even love!\) But best of all, a community was established, offering encouragement for creative endeavors, and friendship and support. It has been life affirming. Now, in 2026, creativity and community are more important than ever, and it’s time to gather a group again! This year, however, we will not be doing “The Artist’s Way,” and instead will be exploring “The Book of Alchemy” by Suleika Jaouad. This book focuses on journaling and looking at our life experiences to foster creativity to inspire whatever art form we choose to do.  From the publisher: “From the time she was young, Suleika Jaouad has kept a journal. She’s used it to mark life’s biggest occasions and to weather its most ferocious storms. Journaling has buoyed her through illness, heartbreak, and the deepest uncertainty. And she is not alone: for so many people, keeping a journal is an essential tool for navigating both the personal peaks and valleys and the collective challenges of modern life. More than ever, we need a space for puzzling through. In The Book of Alchemy, Suleika explores the art of journaling and shares everything she’s learned about how this life-altering practice can help us tap into that mystical trait that exists in every human: creativity. She has gathered wisdom from one hundred writers, artists, and thinkers in the form of essays and writing prompts. Their insights invite us to inhabit a more inspired life. A companion through challenging times, The Book of Alchemy is broken into themes ranging from new beginnings to love, loss, and rebuilding. Whether you’re a lifelong journaler or new to the practice, this book gives you the tools, direction, and encouragement to engage with discomfort, ask questions, peel back the layers, dream daringly, uncover your truest self—and in doing so, to learn to hold the unbearably brutal and astonishingly beautiful facts of life in the same palm.” Beginning Tuesday, March 3rd at 7pm through the end of September \(with flexibility\), we will be meeting on Tuesdays to check in and discuss the book and our progress. Each chapter has a number of prompts so we will take it slow, but also determine our pace. Every other Tuesday we will discuss the book, and then the alternate weeks will be more open — we can listen to chapters or inspiring podcasts while crafting, or just get together and talk — to give people a chance to catch up or take some time. The initial meeting on March 3rd is a welcome meeting for introductions, to pick up the book, and to set some intentions— no need to read anything yet. The cost is $40 plus the purchase of the book.  To register, come by the shop or email alibibookshop@gmail.com. Registration “closes” the end of March.  This group is truly one of the best things I have ever been a part of, and I’m looking forward to doing it again— and welcoming new folks to the fold! Hope to see you!

title: Cola
location: HopMonk Tavern
description: \(\(\(folkYEAH!\)\)\) Presents COLA \+ Artificial Go HopMonk Sebastopol - The Abbey MOSTLY STANDING | 21\+ ONLY ABOUT:  C.O.L.A. is sort of a self-titled album. It’s an acronym for Cost of Living Adjustment, a fitting conceptual framework for the band’s third record. Why? Because C.O.L.A. considers, among other things, socialism vs. hell. It considers: rolling the dice of life. The eerie and sweet pangs that nostalgia can provoke. This is not new territory for band members Tim Darcy, Evan Cartwright, and Ben Stidworthy. It is, in Cartwright’s words “a deepening of what we’ve been doing.” C.O.L.A. is an intricate, beautiful, and sometimes strange record. It is the band’s most refined offering. A perfection of carefully honed aesthetic impulses.  Cola, as a band, says Darcy is defined by its “tasteful minimalism.” A deep appreciation for making music that is romantic, subtle, and deceptively intense. C.O.L.A., however, is the band’s most maximalist work to date. This is a little tongue and cheek \(“We were so worried,” says Cartwright, “About all the songs on this record being too different”\). In practice, this maximalism means that a song like “Hedgesitting,” has both live drums and a sample drum loop. “Hedgesitting,” is a gorgeous, lush song. It’s like a deconstructed, chopped & screwed b-side from the Cure’s Disintegration. It’s also a little indebted to Sarah Records. “When you were young,” Darcy sings at the song’s start, “you came to make it.”  C.O.L.A., like everything written by the band, is inherently collaborative. The band writes everything separately, then comes together and works in the studio. Look again to “Hedgesetting,” to see this in action, which started out with chords that Darcy had sent, then the band expanded it together, with Stidworthy remixing it right before heading to the studio. This division of labor works intuitively. It is a part of the band’s DNA to say, take an arrangement Stidworthy wrote, and then have Darcy and Cartwright build upon it. Take “Favoured Over the Ride,” as an example. “I wanted to create a dusky, melancholy palette for Tim to write lyrics for,” says Stidworthy. The song starts with a lonely, dreamy guitar riff. Then there’s a crisp line of bass and it all comes into focus: “What’s on the ceiling that’s caught your gaze?” sings Darcy. It’s a moment of clarity on a record that is interested abstraction. C.O.L.A. is full of these clarifying moments: where a whole swirl of feelings become so clear that it almost hurts a little bit.  One of the goals with C.O.L.A. was to have the melody guide the lyrics. This is a distinct shift from the sprechgesang that has been an anchor for many of Darcy’s earlier records. Here, the vocal melodies are on the same level as all of the other melodies on the record. But the lyrics are no less poetic, no less precise than anything Darcy has written before \(“It’s not,” he jokes, “like we’re making a Cocteau Twins song.”\) The result is a record that is ruthlessly aware of all of its parts, and treats them all as equally important. C.O.L.A. is a record that speaks to itself: where all of its parts are in direct conversation with each other. Sounds do not blur, even when they are expansive. It is abstract, oblique, sometimes strange, whatever you want to call it. But it is also beautiful, in the classic sense. Beautiful like a painting can be beautiful. Really, really gorgeous. Almost chiseled in the way it plays so deliberately with experimentation. On “Skywriter’s Sigh,” for example, things sizzle and flicker. It touches on the sublime. It is Cola, the band, at their very best. Cola - Cost of Living Adjustment - Bio C.O.L.A. is sort of a self-titled album. title: Carsie Blanton with The Burning Hell
location: Mystic Theatre & Music Hall
description:
**CARSIE BLANTON**

with support from The Burning Hell

**BIOS:**

Carsie Blanton:

Carsie Blanton is a songwriter with hooks, chutzpah, and revolutionary optimism. A

radical folk artist in the tradition of Woody Guthrie, her infectious melodies and lyrical

wit keep listeners rapt while she conjures spirits of vaudeville, campfire singalongs, and

punk rock. Blanton and her road-tested band deploy humor, camaraderie, and

considerable musical muscle to enroll each audience in a rare vision of hope and

solidarity.

In addition to writing and performing music, Carsie works as a political organizer and

activist. In fall of 2025, she participated in the Global Sumud Flotilla, a direct action to

bring humanitarian aid to Gaza by sailboat. In early October, after a month at sea, she

was imprisoned in Israel for five days along with hundreds of her comrades.

Soon after, Blanton released The Little Flame, a song of solidarity covered widely on

social media during her detention. The Little Flame features background vocals from

Irish band Ye Vagabonds and Carsie’s Palestinian/New Zealander prison-mate Rana

Hamida, and appears on her latest album, The Red Album Vol II.

After two decades spent on the road, Blanton has amassed a dedicated fan base and a small menagerie of viral hits, and regularly sells out mid-size venues across the U.S. and Europe. 2026 will find her touring heavily with her own band and in collaboration with Canadian folk-punk rabblerousers The Burning Hell, as well as continuing her organizing work with Artists Against Apartheid and the Party for Socialism and Liberation.

The Burning Hell:

The Burning Hell is the musical project of songwriter Mathias Kom and multi-instrumentalist Ariel Sharratt. Their narrative-driven songs are packed with literary, historical, and pop-cultural subjects, incorporating a frequent fixation on apocalypse and ruin into work that celebrates participation in a surprising, wry, and even occasionally beautiful world. Based in the woods of Prince Edward Island, Canada, The Burning Hell emphasizes connection and commitment to the political power of sharing music.

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: Tom Chown: 46 Years Behind the Lens
location: Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery - Santa Rosa Campus
description: Santa Rosa Junior College will celebrate the 46-year career of longtime staff photographer Tom Chown with a photography exhibition featuring images from his decades at the college, from the days of film and darkrooms to the digital era.  Chown began his career at SRJC at age 24, working in the campus photography lab. Over the next 46 years, he became a familiar presence throughout the college community, documenting the people, programs and milestones that shaped generations of students and employees. Tirza Dawn Naramore
is a yogi, mother, artist, ceremonialist and lover of life. She has been practicing and teaching yoga and meditation for 30 years and offers yoga retreats and trainings that center on optimum health, self realization and self love. Her teachers are from many yoga and tantric traditions, but her primary lineages are Iyengar and Kali Ray.
Tirza is deeply devoted to community building and is honored to have created a number of community supported non profits including Mystic Family Circus and The AWAKEN Project, which serves families with children on the autism spectrum. Tirza is proud to be the mother of 3 wild teenagers, including her incredible son who is diagnosed with autism.
Tirza’s spirituality is one of many influences and teachings. Beginning with a Christian up-bringing and being raised on a Christian commune in her early childhood, she later expanded into more earth-based ways. While in her 20’s Tirza was adopted into the Native American Church, where she learned from her relatives a way of living the “Beauty Way.”
During the 1990’s and early 2000’s, Tirza lived in San Francisco, Oakland and Berkeley, directing the Mystic Family Circus, which was a performance group dedicated to cultural awareness and bridge building. She worked with Cirque du Soleil, Burning Man, Reclaiming, Contraband, CELLspace and other Bay Area art collectives and non profits to provide conscious entertainment and “prayerformances” for the betterment of humankind and the planet.
In 2012, Tirza helped to found the Buckeye Gathering, an ancestral skills gathering in Northern California which draws teachers and students of all ages to learn ancestral ways of tending the earth and survival skills.
Tirza Dawn was the founder of yoga programming and the Ayurvedic Yoga Teacher Trainings at the dhyana Center of Ayurveda in Sebastopol, California, which operated a community center of healing and education from 2010 to 2020.

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. title: Author Event: Grief Grit Glory by Pamela Jessup Runner
description: Join us for a special event with Pamela Jessup Runner, author of Grief Grit Glory. This event is free, but we appreciate your RSVP below so we can plan for your attendance. ABOUT THE BOOK In this deeply moving memoir, Napa Valley author Pamela Jessup Runner shares her family’s extraordinary journey after the birth of her profoundly disabled son, Jonny. Through heartbreak, advocacy, faith, perseverance, and unconditional love, Pamela invites readers into a story that explores what it means to continue choosing hope through life’s most difficult seasons. From the vineyards of Napa Valley to the realities of disability caregiving and family devotion, Grief Grit Glory is a powerful story of motherhood, purpose, and the enduring strength of family. Praised by early readers as “deeply moving,” “heartfelt,” and “impossible to put down,” this memoir offers encouragement and understanding for anyone navigating grief, caregiving, uncertainty, or personal transformation. For additional information and media, you may also visit: Website: https://griefgritglory.com/ Book trailer, podcast https://www.youtube.com/@PamelaJessupRunner ABOUT THE AUTHOR Pamela Jessup Runner writes from the heart in her memoir about motherhood, faith, and the strength it takes to hold a family together. Her storytelling is shaped by a life journey that has included advocacy for families of children with disabilities, entrepreneurship in Napa Valley’s wine community, and the enduring lessons of love and perseverance. Now residing in Sacramento with her husband George, Pam finds inspiration in family life, time at their Tahoe retreat, and traveling the world while continuing to write. Her debut memoir, Grief Grit Glory, shares these experiences, with more stories from her life in Napa Valley yet to come.

title: The Lostines
location: Little Saint
description:
Although recorded in the band's hometown of New Orleans, Meet The Lostines — the full-length debut from songwriters Casey Jane Reece-Kaigler and Camille Wind Weatherford — is an album that charts its own geography. This is where the swampland meets the sock hop. Where golden-age rock & roll crosses paths with old-school country. Where timeless American roots music drops its anchor and climbs skyward, finding some balance between the earthy and the otherworldly. 

At the center of that sound are the entwined voices of Casey Jane and Camille, two longtime friends whose songs explore the uncharted territory between genres. There's rarely a melody on Meet The Lostines that the two don't sing together, stacking their lush harmonies against a backdrop of baritone guitar, spring reverb, orchestral strings, Cajun fiddle, upright piano, and Theremin. It's an immersive sound that bridges the gaps between genres, created by two songwriters \(along with a revolving door of collaborators, co-conspirators, and fellow Big Easy residents\) who're happy to build their own world.

In this eight-session class new weavers will start at the beginning and experience the full process from designing to finishing. title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: S.R. Laws
location: Café Frida Gallery
description:
S.R. LAWS IS OUT THERE: He approaches songwriting with a passion for songs that we all grew up on. His sound rings a familiar bell in your head while still delivering ideas completely unique.  He draws inspiration from outstanding storytellers like John Hiatt, Lou Reed, Steve Earle, Neil Finn and Ron Sexsmith. All of their music and others have carved a deep groove. 

Growing up out there in Northern California, he developed a unique connection to music early on. His father worked as a trash collector, and he would spend hours sifting through bags of discarded 45 records. Each find felt like stumbling upon hidden treasures. Some records were covered in dirt and grime, while others were pristine. The thrill of discovering new sounds was exhilarating, and he could hardly wait to drop the needle and immerse himself in the music.

He embarked on a pilgrimage to Texas with just two suitcases and $500 in his bank account. His goal was to dive into the vibrant music scene and learn from fellow songwriters. Austin, known as the "Live Music Capital of the World," offered countless opportunities for him to grow as an artist. Open mics and songwriters' nights became his training ground, where he soaked up every moment, listening to others share their stories through music.

These days, he resides in Sonoma County, California, working hard as a touring artist and singer-songwriter for his original rock band, The Heartsleeves. He invites everyone to join him on this musical journey, sharing his songs one person at a time in this vast and unpredictable world we live in.

“Scott Ray Laws is an unique and really cool songwriter…he digs into materials, tells a story in his songs, and has a clean baritone vocality that is easy on the ears. We had a chance to meet and hang with Scott back in May ..and I HAD to have him back for a Wednesday evening.” Luigi- Owner-The Listening Room.

“..An ORIGINAL songwriter who knows how to tell a story clearly in song” -  Scotty O’Neill - Guitarist/Promoter

“ It was such a treat catching your set last night — really refreshing to hear something new and original. Thanks for pulling up a chair and hanging out with us — we really enjoyed the conversation and the stories behind your songs.”  -Tripp B. - Sonoma Songwriter

“Expect slow burning passion and vivid music …the kind of energy that turns into “let’s stay for just one more!..”  - Doug- Owner/Wine Maker- Spicy Vines

“...His lyrics simply tell first-person stories from his own life. Nothing fancy, he's not writing to impress--he pours himself, as is, into each phrase and melody.”- Rebecca Roudman- Dirty Cello Radio Hour KRCB Radio 104.9 FM

“ It is through forthright lyrics that are personal and earnest, that he composes lyrical pictures. Taking snapshots from the most common walks of life...”  - David Sampson - Producer Studio Secti West

“..relaxed mid-tempo Americana, capturing in each song the rhythmic pocket Laws is known for creating.” -  Coyote Music Review 2024

title: Book Mark Story Awards Celebration
location: Yountville Community Center
description:
The challenge is complete, and now it's time to jubilate! Join Yountville Arts for the Bookmark Story Celebration on Thursday, Sept. 24, from 5:30 to 7 p.m. in the Heritage Room of the Community Center, 6516 Washington Street.

Each writer was a resident, worker or student in Napa County. Writers submitted one or two unpublished stories in either prose or poetry format, with a limit of 60 words per story. A winning story connected all elements together, showing creativity and originality!

Submissions were accepted in English from adults or youth age 18 or younger, or in Spanish from youth age 18 or younger.

Yountville Arts, Napa County Libraries and Friends of the Yountville Library sponsor this event. Guests will join the people who support the contest and who will talk about why this technique of writing can be useful. Jurors, who read 39 entries from writers of all ages, will share suggestions for writing a strong story. And the exciting highlight of the evening is this: You'll hear the winning and honorable-mention stories read by the authors, along with their insights into creating micro-compositions. Copies of the bookmarks with the winning stories will also be available.

“The Bookmark Stories contest is one of those rare projects that brings every generation together through creativity and storytelling. It's inspiring to see how 60 words can hold such imagination. We are proud to bring our community's big voices to appear on small bookmarks,” project chair Geoffrey Leigh said.

Join us for an inspiring and fun evening while you also get the scoop about next year's contest. The celebration is open to the public, and there is no admission charge. We do encourage you to get a free ticket to make sure everyone has a seat. Light bites and refreshments will be served. Arrive early to get a great spot. We look forward to seeing you! 

Bookmark Stories Contest Thursday, Sept. 24, 5:30 to 7 p.m. Yountville Community Center

For further information, contact Katelyn Huss at khuss@yville.com or 707.944.8712

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting March 2025, we ask that every attending member pay a $1 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

description:
Get ready to feel the rhythm and energy of Rio de Janeiro! Samba no Pé \(Samba in the Foot\) is the captivating solo style of samba danced in the streets and at Carnival, known for its rapid, intricate footwork and infectious hip movements.

You will learn

The Basic Step: You will master the signature quick-quick-slow rhythm that defines Samba no Pé.

Arm & Hip Styling: You will learn how to add the authentic flair, movement, and energy that makes Brazilian samba so captivating.

Technique & Posture: You will receive tips on proper body alignment to help you dance longer, faster, and more safely.

Rhythm & Musicality: You will learn how to connect your movement directly to the irresistible beat of the bateria \(the samba drum section\).

This class is perfect for anyone looking to connect with the vibrant spirit of Brazil, improve coordination, and get a fantastic workout—all while learning the foundational steps of this iconic dance. No partner or prior dance experience is required! Just bring your enthusiasm and comfortable shoes!

description:
We meet in-person only on the 1st and 2nd Thursdays of the month. However, you can catch us online every Thursday unless the meeting date falls on a holiday.

Please register at https://signup.com/go/WiniixA

What is Toastmasters About?

Usually at our meetings, we will have a prepared speech, and a speech evaluation. The Grammarian and Wizard of Ah's will listen for turns of phrases and the use of filler words. We also practice impromptu speaking during the section of the meeting called Table Topics. During Table Topics, at a recent meeting, we were asked what we felt was the biggest communication problem or challenge. What would you answer in a fast moment? Table topics will challenge you to think quickly and give an answer without preparation.

You will also hear tips on public speaking skills at our upcoming meeting. Whether you're a seasoned traveler or just looking for some adventure from the comfort of your home, this event is perfect for you.

Toastmasters International is all about communication excellence, and for 100 years and counting, Toastmasters have been expressing themselves better, practicing, and evaluating in a fun club environment, shining all around the world.

To find out more--Msg us on our webpage \(under Contact Us\) button at

https://mareisland.toastmastersclubs.org/

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

Long-time friends and fellow plantsmen, Sean and Jim will reflect on horticulture, legacy gardens, plant exploration, and the enduring relationships between people and place.

Expect an evening of stories, insights, and thoughtful conversation for gardeners, horticulturalists, and anyone who loves the natural world.

This talk is part of *Western Hills Garden’s Horticultural Exchange Series*, bringing together leading voices in horticulture for thoughtful public conversations.

Speaker Bios:

Sean Hogan: Sean is an acclaimed horticulturist, garden consultant, speaker, and international plant collector. Convinced to become California’s first certified arborist by Western Hills Garden founder Marshall Olbrich, Sean has had a storied career as a Curator at the University of California Botanical Garden at Berkeley, and in 1996 he and his partner Parker founded Cistus Design Nursery on Sauvie Island in Oregon. Sean is a Founding Board Member of the new Portland Botanical Garden and a member of the WHG Horticultural Advisory Committee.

Jim Salyards: Jim has worked at Filoli for 30 years, moving into his current role as Associate Director of Garden Experience in early 2025. Jim oversees a wide range of programs that support Filoli’s external relations, learning and engagement, development, retail, and interpretive strategies, with a particular emphasis on community engagement. He also oversees Filoli’s plant collections work and is responsible for building and nurturing relationships within the fields of public gardens, horticultural science, gardening, retail product production, and the culinary arts.

description:
Acorn MusEcology Project is proud to present the Northern California premiere of Alex Berko's
Sacred Place
, an immersive exploration of ecological spirituality set to the words of Wendell Berry, John Muir, William Stafford, and Rabindranath Tagore. Acorn's 27-voice ensemble will be joined by violin, cello, and piano to offer up this song cycle of reverential texts within a richly-layered soundscape. Additional original music by co-directors Sarah Dupre and Robin Eschner includes a new setting of poetry by the late Steve Fowler, co-founder of the Sebastopol Peace Garden, soil ecologist, and community builder. Acorn composer Chris Smith will usher listeners into the alchemical mysteries of human composting. Joni Mitchell, Moira Smiley, and other master songsmiths round out the program. With Acorn's signature approach to melding rich vocal harmony with the values of deep ecology, this concert will invite reflection on our place and purpose on the Earth, and on the wild intelligence speaking to us from beneath our feet.
"The earth says have a place; be what that place requires; hear the sound the birds imply and see as deep as ridges go behind each other...Listening, I think that’s what the earth says."
– William Stafford.

title: Greg Sarris - The Last Human Bear
description: In conversation with Jane Ciabattari, he will share back stories about the area from an Indigenous perspective in this unforgettable tale inspired by the Native women elders who shaped Greg in his youth. The novel's main character Mary Hatcher lives with a curse-or is it a power that could make her life whole? A Native Pomo woman who comes of age in 1930s California, Mary keeps trying to make sense of her enigmatic family. Strange rumors spread about her. Her stepmother may have taught her how to become a Human Bear, a shapeshifter who can menace and poison enemies. Two men may love her-or love who they think she is. A mystery even to herself, Mary learns to pass between Native and white societies, tenaciously carving her own path as an independent woman. But as she explores love and desire, family inherited and chosen, and the secrets of the natural world, one question gnaws at her: Is she fated to do harm? Wry and richly lyrical, The Last Human Bear follows Mary from the Great Depression to the twenty-first century, when she commits a haunting final act.

description: Grizfolk burst onto the scene with their 2014 debut EP, From the Spark, followed by 2016’s full-length Waking Up The Giants, from wheir catchy blend of electronic-tinged folk-rock and pop styles caught the ears of fans around the globe. They returned in 2019 with Rarest Of Birds, delivering a nostalgic, summertime feel with their embracing more organic instrumentation in lieu of previous synth-heavy sounds.  In 2021 they shared their 3rd full-length album, the self-titled Grizfolk. It succeeds as a mix of both worlds that their previous albums created, while also achieving the sound the band has been chasing all along, which Billboard called “a little country, a little rock and a lot catchy,” Half of the new songs were produced by Rich Costey \(Muse, The Killers, Barns Courtney\) in early 2020 after the band returned from an inspiring retreat in Joshua Tree. These include long-time fan favorite “The Ripple,” which has been a staple of their live set thanks to its Americana twang and irresistible singalong appeal but had never been captured in the studio, along with the harmonica-led “Money,” the relentless hip-shaker and head-nodder “Queen of the Desert,” and the sunny, confident “California High.” The new album is available now and tour tickets are on sale now!

description:
HABITAAT \(Tomas Wischerath\) is a San Francisco based DJ, composer, and producer who is pushing the boundaries between organic bass and high-energy dance music, creating a sound he describes as “electronic music inspired by nature”. Born in Brazil and raised in the Bay Area, HABITAAT’s sound is deeply influenced by hip-hop beats, cinematic movie scores, and underground dance music—crafting immersive sonic landscapes that transport listeners to a world where rhythm meets the raw beauty of the earth. Blending infectious dance beats and ethereal melodic sounds, HABITAAT’s soundscapes mirror the beauty of our own natural world in danceable and psychedelic ways. 

A rising force in indie electronic music, HABITAAT has graced legendary stages, including opening for CloZee at Red Rocks in 2022, and sharing lineups with artists like Bonobo and Duke Dumont. HABITAAT has become a staple in both ecstatic dance and electronic festival circuits. With a growing catalog of music, including two album releases in 2024 \(Grow, Fall In Deep\), his work continues to explore what connects us to nature through sound. 

HABITAAT’s music resonates with both deep-listening organic bass DJs and feel-good partygoers, offering an experience that is as meditative as it is high-energy. Whether played in the depths of a forest, the pulse of a nightclub, or under the stars at a festival, HABITAAT’s music creates a space where movement, connection, and nature unite.
