title: Artist's Way Group Next Chapter: "The Book of Alchemy"
location: Alibi Bookshop
description: Creativity is my way of making sense of the world.” — Suleika Jaouad  Are you feeling an urge to pick up a pen or paintbrush or pair of scissors and unleash your creativity, but not sure where to start? Or are you looking to find community, to motivate your creative self and make new friends? This might be just the thing for you. Two years ago, we formed an “Artist’s Way” group here at the shop, and continued it again last year. It was extraordinary. Not only did people write and paint and create, but got published and found new life paths. \(And even love!\) But best of all, a community was established, offering encouragement for creative endeavors, and friendship and support. It has been life affirming. Now, in 2026, creativity and community are more important than ever, and it’s time to gather a group again! This year, however, we will not be doing “The Artist’s Way,” and instead will be exploring “The Book of Alchemy” by Suleika Jaouad. This book focuses on journaling and looking at our life experiences to foster creativity to inspire whatever art form we choose to do.  From the publisher: “From the time she was young, Suleika Jaouad has kept a journal. She’s used it to mark life’s biggest occasions and to weather its most ferocious storms. Journaling has buoyed her through illness, heartbreak, and the deepest uncertainty. And she is not alone: for so many people, keeping a journal is an essential tool for navigating both the personal peaks and valleys and the collective challenges of modern life. More than ever, we need a space for puzzling through. In The Book of Alchemy, Suleika explores the art of journaling and shares everything she’s learned about how this life-altering practice can help us tap into that mystical trait that exists in every human: creativity. She has gathered wisdom from one hundred writers, artists, and thinkers in the form of essays and writing prompts. Their insights invite us to inhabit a more inspired life. A companion through challenging times, The Book of Alchemy is broken into themes ranging from new beginnings to love, loss, and rebuilding. Whether you’re a lifelong journaler or new to the practice, this book gives you the tools, direction, and encouragement to engage with discomfort, ask questions, peel back the layers, dream daringly, uncover your truest self—and in doing so, to learn to hold the unbearably brutal and astonishingly beautiful facts of life in the same palm.” Beginning Tuesday, March 3rd at 7pm through the end of September \(with flexibility\), we will be meeting on Tuesdays to check in and discuss the book and our progress. Each chapter has a number of prompts so we will take it slow, but also determine our pace. Every other Tuesday we will discuss the book, and then the alternate weeks will be more open — we can listen to chapters or inspiring podcasts while crafting, or just get together and talk — to give people a chance to catch up or take some time. The initial meeting on March 3rd is a welcome meeting for introductions, to pick up the book, and to set some intentions— no need to read anything yet. The cost is $40 plus the purchase of the book.  To register, come by the shop or email alibibookshop@gmail.com. Registration “closes” the end of March.  This group is truly one of the best things I have ever been a part of, and I’m looking forward to doing it again— and welcoming new folks to the fold! Hope to see you!

title: Tom Chown: 46 Years Behind the Lens
location: Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery - Santa Rosa Campus
description: Santa Rosa Junior College will celebrate the 46-year career of longtime staff photographer Tom Chown with a photography exhibition featuring images from his decades at the college, from the days of film and darkrooms to the digital era.  Chown began his career at SRJC at age 24, working in the campus photography lab. Over the next 46 years, he became a familiar presence throughout the college community, documenting the people, programs and milestones that shaped generations of students and employees.  The exhibition will trace Chown's evolution as a photographer, from working with film and developing photographs in the darkroom to embracing digital photography. It also offers a visual history of SRJC, preserving moments from nearly five decades of college life.  The exhibition is free and open to the public.Location: Robert F. title: Morning Yoga
location: Occidental Center for the Arts Studio, 3820 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental CA 95465
description:
Regenerative Ayurvedic Yoga with Tirza Dawn
Come, step onto your mat with an open heart and an open mind.
Invest in your self care and join us for morning yoga in the OCA studio. $20 per class, $15 for OCA members. Yoga is offered Mondays from 10-11:10 AM and also on Wednesdays from 8:30-9:40 AM. The registration below is for Mondays.
Pay at the door for a-la-carte sessions or use the links below to pay ahead for four weeks at a time.
Pay Online 4 sessions
Tirza Dawn Naramore
is a yogi, mother, artist, ceremonialist and lover of life. She has been practicing and teaching yoga and meditation for 30 years and offers yoga retreats and trainings that center on optimum health, self realization and self love. Her teachers are from many yoga and tantric traditions, but her primary lineages are Iyengar and Kali Ray.
Tirza is deeply devoted to community building and is honored to have created a number of community supported non profits including Mystic Family Circus and The AWAKEN Project, which serves families with children on the autism spectrum. Tirza is proud to be the mother of 3 wild teenagers, including her incredible son who is diagnosed with autism.
Tirza’s spirituality is one of many influences and teachings. Beginning with a Christian up-bringing and being raised on a Christian commune in her early childhood, she later expanded into more earth-based ways. While in her 20’s Tirza was adopted into the Native American Church, where she learned from her relatives a way of living the “Beauty Way.”
During the 1990’s and early 2000’s, Tirza lived in San Francisco, Oakland and Berkeley, directing the Mystic Family Circus, which was a performance group dedicated to cultural awareness and bridge building. She worked with Cirque du Soleil, Burning Man, Reclaiming, Contraband, CELLspace and other Bay Area art collectives and non profits to provide conscious entertainment and “prayerformances” for the betterment of humankind and the planet.
In 2012, Tirza helped to found the Buckeye Gathering, an ancestral skills gathering in Northern California which draws teachers and students of all ages to learn ancestral ways of tending the earth and survival skills.
Tirza Dawn was the founder of yoga programming and the Ayurvedic Yoga Teacher Trainings at the dhyana Center of Ayurveda in Sebastopol, California, which operated a community center of healing and education from 2010 to 2020.

title: From Sheep to Loom: Diné Weaving Traditions

description: For the Diné, weaving is considered a ceremony. title: Tom Chown: 46 Years Behind the Lens
location: Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery - Santa Rosa Campus
description: Santa Rosa Junior College will celebrate the 46-year career of longtime staff photographer Tom Chown with a photography exhibition featuring images from his decades at the college, from the days of film and darkrooms to the digital era.  Chown began his career at SRJC at age 24, working in the campus photography lab. Over the next 46 years, he became a familiar presence throughout the college community, documenting the people, programs and milestones that shaped generations of students and employees.  The exhibition will trace Chown's evolution as a photographer, from working with film and developing photographs in the darkroom to embracing digital photography. It also offers a visual history of SRJC, preserving moments from nearly five decades of college life.  The exhibition is free and open to the public.Location: Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery, Doyle Library 1st floor - Santa Rosa CampusFor more information, visit SRJC's Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery website. title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process

  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings

Dates: Fridays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series, meeting 6 consecutive Fridays. You can start your series anytime.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with instructor for details.



This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcomed.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.

title: From Sheep to Loom: Diné Weaving Traditions
location: SRJC Multicultural Museum - Santa Rosa Campus
description: For the Diné, weaving is considered a ceremony. Creating a single blanket requires many steps, including shearing the sheep, cleaning, carding, spinning, and dyeing the wool, and then finally weaving. It can take hundreds of hours. This exhibit features rugs from the SRJC Multicultural Museum's collections, featuring award winning woven rugs such as a fine "Burntwater" style rug by the great Nellie Roan and many other examples of Navajo rugs from the 1920s through the 1970s.More information available on the SRJC Multicultural Museum website. (https://museum.santarosa.edu/)

title: Gravenstein Mandolin Ensemble
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Experience the bright, shimmering sound of strings in harmony as the
Gravenstein Mandolin Ensemble
takes the stage at Occidental Center for the Arts. This talented local ensemble brings together mandolins, mandolas, mandocello, and guitar for a lively musical journey spanning folk traditions, classical favorites, contemporary arrangements, and melodies from around the world.
With the mandolin family’s distinctive blend of warmth, sparkle, and rhythmic energy, the ensemble creates a sound that is both intimate and wonderfully full. Join us for an afternoon of beautiful music, community, and the irresistible charm of many mandolins making music together!
Get Tickets
The Gravenstein Mandolin Ensemble
was formed in 2006 in Sebastopol, California, a town famous for its Gravenstein apples. With humble beginnings, the six original members grew to its present size of fifteen, including the entire mandolin family: mandolins, mandolas, mandocellos, with additional support from guitar and bass. The repertoire includes music from the Classical Era to the most contemporary works for modern mandolins; the geographical range includes music from Italy, Spain, Germany, Eastern Europe as well as Latin America. Smaller groups, or “breakout” ensembles, often perform a variety of music, including Bluegrass, Celtic, Choro, and more. The GME has performed at the Green Center at Sonoma State University, the San Francisco Mandolin Festival and numerous venues through the North Bay Area. In 2018, the GME co-hosted the national convention of the Classical Mandolin Association of America, held in Santa Rosa.

title: Senderos & RFO: Observación de Estrellas
description: ¡Ven a conocer más acerca de nuestro universo!  Milo Buitrago-Casas, físico investigador en el Laboratorio de Ciencias Espaciales de la Universidad de California, Berkeley, nos guiarán en una charla en español acerca de nuestro lugar en el cosmos, mientras que los docentes del Observatorio Robert Ferguson (ubicado dentro de Sugarloaf Ridge State Park) nos guiarán en el uso de telescopios para que tu y tu familia puedan observar el cosmos. El evento comenzará a las 7:00 pm en el aula del Observatorio con una presentación. Milo Buitrago-Casas nos pregunta, ¿qué pasaría si mañana una civilización de otro planeta nos contactara y nos pidiera nuestra ubicación en el Universo para venir a visitarnos? ¿Qué le responderíamos? La respuesta nos lleva en un viaje que empieza donde estamos parados y termina en los límites del universo conocido, qué tan pequeños somos frente a todo lo demás, y por qué esa pequeñez, lejos de asustarnos, es una de las ideas más hermosas que nos ha dado la ciencia.EntradasLa admisión es $10 para adultos, $5 para jóvenes entre 12 y 18 años (deben ser acompañados por un padre de familia o guardián legal), y gratis para menores de 12 años. Obtén tus boletos en rfo.simpletix.com Si posees una tarjeta de EBT, el dueño y tres familiares pueden registrarse por gratis a través del programa Museums for All. Regístrate por adelantado ya que el espacio es limitado y se llenará pronto. Recomendamos vestirse en capas, traer agua, una linterna pequeña de mano (sólamente para aluzar el camino; no puede ser usada cerca del Observatorio a menos que tenga un filtro rojo)  y si la tienes, una guía a las estrellas. Nos reuniremos en el estacionamiento del Granero Blanco. El estacionamiento, usualmente $10, es gratis para este evento.  Para más información, manda un correo electrónico a Alma en senderos@sonomaecologycenter.org o llama al 707-247-5767, martes a sábado entre 9:00 am-5:00 pm. Condiciones lluviosas cancelan el evento pero continuará en condiciones nubladas .Facilidad de acceso: el Observatorio Robert Ferguson se ubica dentro de Sugarloaf Ridge State Park. El área de estacionarse cuenta con un espacio designado para camionetas que necesitan acceso y aunque no oficialmente, hay mucho estacionamiento que puede ser accesible en esa misma área y en el estacionamiento del granero blanco. Hay una rampa que oficialmente cumple con los requerimientos de la Ley para Estadounidenses con Discapacidades (ADA) para ingresar al observatorio. El área de asentamiento en el aula principal del observatorio está compuesto de sillas que fácilmente pueden moverse. Hay baños disponibles dentro del edificio, incluyendo uno accesible. El telescopio de la sala oeste tiene una rampa portátil para alcanzar el ocular, y el telescopio de la sala este es una pantalla grande instalada en la pared.  Encuentra más oportunidades recreacionales a través del programa Senderos Naturales en ésta página.Para aprender más acerca de RFO, visita rfo.org. Para más eventos en Sugarloaf, visita sugarloafpark.org/events

title: Poetic Medicine: 10/06/2026 — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Poetic Medicine: 10/06/2026

  
    
      
        
          $15.00
        
      
    
  

PLEASE NOTE: October Poetic Medicine will meet on the first Tuesday of October. Tuesday, October 6th, 2026; 4:00 – 5:30pm$15.00Max 20 Attendees, Pre-registration required(We are unable to offer refunds or transfers for this class. If you cannot attend, please consider it a donation. Thank you!)The practice of “poem making” offers a means to express the metaphors and meaning of the joys and suffering we experience in ourselves and bear witness to in others. Poetry can be a salve for the heart and soul. It is a way of speaking what is true in our hearts and is often difficult to access without a creative spark. You do not have to be a "poet" or even a "writer" to allow words and feelings to pour through your pen.Redwing Keyssar has been leading "poetic medicine" sessions through her work in Palliative Care at UCSF for the past 5 years. Her work has created an international community of people who, by listening to and writing poetry together, have healed wounds of grief and loss, helped "wounded healers," and provided resiliency to move forward on our life paths.Writing poetry in community is a bit like attending a meditation retreat. The instruction for most beginners when learning to meditate is to simply bring oneself back to the breath, each time the mind wanders. In poem-making, the instruction is to bring oneself back to the heart and along with a deep breath, see if one can open a little bit wider. When we witness each other in this process, in a circle of open-heartedness, something magical happens!This is an IN-PERSON gathering to establish a strong and safe creative community. We are all poets!About the Instructor: Judith Redwing Keyssar, RN has traversed an amazing 35+ year journey in the healing arts/healthcare. Redwing is an educator, end-of-life doula, author, poet, song-writer, ceremonialist, national presenter and frequent contributor to public issues about Palliative and End of Life Care. Redwing is currently the Director of Education at the MERI Center for Education in Palliative Care at UCSF/Mt. Zion. Her professional career includes being the Clinical Director at Zen Hospice Project and the Director of Palliative Care and Nursing at Jewish Family and Children’s Services from 2004-2018. She is a founder and adjunct faculty member of the California State University Shiley/Haynes Institute of Palliative Care, and has taught courses at OLLI at Sonoma State. Redwing is the author of an award-winning book, “Last Acts of Kindness; Lessons for the Living from the Bedsides of the Dying” and is the recipient of numerous awards in the field of Palliative Care. After studying with John Fox at the Institute for Poetic Medicine, her passion for using poetry as a healing modality has led to the development of a successful international program in Poetic Medicine, through her work at the UCSF MERI Center. Learn more about her here: https://redwingkeyssar.com/

Watercolor Fundamentals - Part 1

This class focuses on the simple delight of mixing color with water, brushing it on paper, and watching what happens as it moves and dries. You will learn easy ways to create paintings that are all about color and the sometimes unpredictable nature of water.

No drawing skills are needed.

In this class we will explore the basic principles of watercolor painting. Learn or refresh your understanding of brush handling, brush care and setting up, the benefits of “good paper”, watercolor lights and darks, flat and graded washes, wet-on-wet techniques such as charging, wet-on-dry techniques such as glazing, color wheel, color theory, color mixing, and more. Simple applications of these techniques invite you to experiment and play.

We will create more complex landscape paintings, skies and seascapes; wet-into-wet and wet-into-dry nature studies in a few different ways, and we will venture further into painting from our imaginations. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Fridays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series, meeting 6 consecutive Fridays. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 2:30pm - 4:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with instructor for details.



This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcomed.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: "Sip, Sparkle & Shine" - For National You Go Girl Day
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
Join us in celebrating national "You Go Girl' Day with a fun wine tasting at Foppiano Vineyards here in Healdsburg for us girls!

The tasting will be focused on wines from the Russian River Valley. You are welcome to bring snacks to share if you wish. The hostesses will likely bring a something to share as well.

Optional dress code: Everyone wear something that sparkles- Sequins, Glitter, Metallics, Rhinestones, Pink, Sparkly shoes, etc.

The story of Foppiano Vineyards is a family epic full of tradition, perseverance and contributions to the history of Sonoma County and the wine country. Founded in 1896 by Giovanni Foppiano, Foppiano Vineyards is one of Sonoma County’s oldest continually-operated, family-owned wineries. They offer a variety of different wines and a lovely space to enjoy ourselves in.

The tasting fee and gratuity will be $38 per person, with $1 for added for our 'Slush' fund, to pay for incidentals with the club. Spots must be reserved by prepaying, using Paypal through the Meetup website. Paypal does charge a nominal fee for payment processing. We can refund you the price of your tasting fee if you need to cancel and let us know 5 days in advance.

Thanks and we look forward to sharing our favorite wines with you!!

Rachael and Kris

title: John Prine Tribute with David Luning, Ben Dubin and Victoria George
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
David Luning returns to OCA for a special tribute celebrating John Prine's birthday. David will be joined by musical colleagues Ben Dubin and Victoria George.
Tickets are $35, $30 for OCA members.
Get Tickets
Please note: this show is scheduled to take place in our Amphitheater. Weather and other factors could cause us to move the event indoors. Please check back here the week of the event for an update on location.
David Luning knew at a young age the path his life should take. Throughout generations, troubadours and singers have harnessed the cultural landscape and passed it along, with the likes of John Prine and Townes Van Zandt paving the way with the telling of their stories. Following in those footsteps, the 29-year-old Sonoma County singer/songwriter's new record is the product of a massive turn in his life and taps into that cultural archive. Listening to ‘Souvenirs’ by John Prine, was a cornerstone moment, compelling Luning to leave Berklee College and follow in the tradition of these iconic troubadours.

description:
Instructor: Anne Millett

Date: This is a 6-class series, meeting 6 Tuesdays September 15th, 22nd, 29th, October 6th, 13th & 20th.

Time: 10:30AM-1:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$270.00

There will be a materials fee of $20 plus tax for the series.

*optional 7th and 8th classes priced separately, October 27th & November 3rd.


Watercolor Fundamentals - Part 1

This class focuses on the simple delight of mixing color with water, brushing it on paper, and watching what happens as it moves and dries. You will learn easy ways to create paintings that are all about color and the sometimes unpredictable nature of water.

No drawing skills are needed.

In this class we will explore the basic principles of watercolor painting. Learn or refresh your understanding of brush handling, brush care and setting up, the benefits of “good paper”, watercolor lights and darks, flat and graded washes, wet-on-wet techniques such as charging, wet-on-dry techniques such as glazing, color wheel, color theory, color mixing, and more. Simple applications of these techniques invite you to experiment and play.

This class is designed for adults 18+ (exceptions made for very motivated teens, please email to discuss)

class sizes are limited to 8 people, please register early

$270 for 6 classes, 2.5 hours each class

There will be a materials fee of $20 plus tax for the series.

description:

Date: This is a 6-class series, meeting 6 Tuesdays September 15th, 22nd, 29th, October 6th, 13th & 20th.

Watercolor Fundamentals - Part 2

This next series will build on what we learned in Part 1, quickly refreshing some techniques and then applying them in our paintings. We will create more complex landscape paintings, skies and seascapes; wet-into-wet and wet-into-dry nature studies in a few different ways, and we will venture further into painting from our imaginations. We will explore abstraction and non-representational styles, where we don't look at something and try to paint it, but instead work intuitively with colors and shapes and let the paintings emerge and evolve from there. You don't have to know where you're going, enjoy the journey and see where it takes you!

This class is designed for adults 18+

title: Readers' Theatre
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
2nd & 4th Tuesdays, 2-4 pm in the OCA Lobby
Interested in learning, sharing and reading short plays? Readers Theatre is a fun opportunity to express yourself.
Readers Theatre participants read scripts adapted from literature, while the ‘audience’ pictures the action by hearing the script being read aloud. It requires no sets, costumes, props, or memorized lines. Instead of acting literature as in a play, the performer’s goal is to read a script aloud effectively, enabling the audience to visualize the action. Performers bring the text alive by using voice, facial expressions, and some gestures. $15 participation fee, $10 for OCA members.
Alternating READER’S CHOICE nights: Can be play, poetry, story, essay, your own writing, OR ??????
For more information, email
Joan Ambrosini,
coordinator .

title: Sound Bath with Laura Benson
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
Rest & Renew at our Sound Bath!
Support your nervous system, release anxiety and stress, and harmonize your body, mind and spirit on the 2nd Tuesday of every month! Laura Benson has a Masters in Intuition Medicine(R) and is a certified sound healer who will guide you through a gentle meditation before each sound bath session. Bring your own yoga mat & blanket and come ready to rest and renew! In the OCA Studio.
Sliding scale pricing $25-$35.
Register
A sound bath is a whole-body, immersive listening experience. During a sound bath, participants often sit or lie down, and are surrounded by the mostly non-melodic soundscapes created by a range of instruments played by the sound bath facilitator. Hence, they are “bathed” in sound.
Sound therapy is a non-invasive healing modality that utilizes the physical and physiological interactions of sound on our bodies and nervous systems to produce therapeutic results. In a sound healing session, specific sonic frequencies are used to soothe the central nervous system, calm the breath, and quiet the mind by encouraging the brain to move into more relaxed states, down from beta (fight-or-flight) and into theta and alpha waves. This increases present-moment awareness and reduces stress and anxiety. Sound baths have been found to be effective in improving mood, cognitive function, and overall mental, physical, and spiritual wellbeing.
Crystal bowl sound baths are particularly powerful in that each bowl is tuned to a specific frequency that corresponds with a different chakra, or energy center, of the body. Based on specific needs, a practitioner can focus on releasing tension or clearing out stuck energy in specific chakras by playing certain bowls or intervals.
While attending a sound bath, you may experience physical sensations brought out by the crystal sound bowls or gong, such as tingling in your limbs or scalp, slowing of your breathing, eye flutters, or small muscle spasms. Not to worry! These sensations often indicate the release of tension or emotional energy stored in the body’s energy systems.

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: From Sheep to Loom: Diné Weaving Traditions
location: SRJC Multicultural Museum - Santa Rosa Campus
description: For the Diné, weaving is considered a ceremony. Creating a single blanket requires many steps, including shearing the sheep, cleaning, carding, spinning, and dyeing the wool, and then finally weaving. It can take hundreds of hours. This exhibit features rugs from the SRJC Multicultural Museum's collections, featuring award winning woven rugs such as a fine "Burntwater" style rug by the great Nellie Roan and many other examples of Navajo rugs from the 1920s through the 1970s.More information available on the SRJC Multicultural Museum website. (https://museum.santarosa.edu/)

description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Fridays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series, meeting 6 consecutive Fridays. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 2:30pm - 4:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with instructor for details.



This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcomed.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: Afternoon of East Asian Calligraphy with Christine Renden Haggarty
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Christine Renden Haggarty
Date: Saturday, October 17th
Time: 12:00-3:30PM
Fee: $60.00
Location: Santa Rosa Store

The invention of the brush in 300 B.C. revolutionized civilization at the time. Up until then, people were carving in stone or bone or writing with sticks in the earth. Because these methods were so slow and unwieldy necessity, the mother of invention, the brush was created.

Please join Christine for this afternoon of brushwork. You will experience three different types of script – formal, semi-cursive and cursive and learn to write five different characters in those styles. At the end of the class you can take your favorite character and write it on a shikishi board.

Christine has studied with several different calligraphy masters over 20 years. She has participated in exhibitions around the world; most recently in San Francisco and Healdsburg. She is the Associate Editor of Heart of the Brush, a collaborative work with Kazuaki Tanahashi, published in 2016. For more information about Christine go to zenbrush.net http://www.zenbrush.net/


Cost for the afternoon is $60 per class with all materials included. To enroll contact Christine at zenbrush@yahoo.com mailto:zenbrush@yahoo.com

title: Tribute to Dr. Ralph Stanley with Nathan Stanley Band and Mission Blue
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
Nathan Stanley Band and Mission Blue honor the King of Mountain Soul
Join us for a musical tribute to the one and only Dr. Ralph Stanley!
Local bluegrass favorites
Mission Blue
open for the touring
Nathan Stanley Band
.
Yes- Nathan is Ralph Stanley's grandson!
Don't miss this incredible evening of unforgettable harmonies and picking from the legendary musical catalog of Ralph Stanley.
Tickets are $30 GA, $25 for OCA members. Online sales end at 6PM day of show or when sold out. This event will be held indoors. ADA seating available, please email info@occidentalcenterforthearts.org to arrange. Beer, wine, refreshments available. Art gallery open during intermission.
Get Tickets
Legendary American bluegrass artist,
Dr. Ralph Edmund Stanley
, was internationally known for his unique, innovative style of singing and banjo playing. In 1976, he was awarded an honorary Doctorate of Music from Lincoln Memorial University, spawning the popular title “Dr. Ralph Stanley.” He was inducted into the International Music Hall of Honor in 1992, and the Grand Ole Opry in 2000, the same year in which his work was featured in the film
O Brother, Where Art Thou?
- for which he won a 2002 Grammy Award for Best Male Country Vocal Performance.
After considering retirement and even scheduling a farewell tour in 2014, Ralph Stanley later announced a welcome decision to continue gracing the country with his beloved, signature style of music.
On June 23, 2016, Dr. Ralph Stanley passed away while battling complications from skin cancer. He will forever be remembered in the hearts and minds of his family and fans, and his legend lives on through his music, which will inspire generations of artists to come.
Read more about Dr. Ralph Stanley here
.
Nathan Stanley is the grandson of Bluegrass Music Icon Dr. Ralph Stanley
and is no exception to the family tradition. Having garnered several charting singles in Inspirational Country Music and Southern Gospel Music, Nathan has come front and center as a music Evangelist.
Through decades of performing—spanning the U.S. and international tours—Nathan has achieved numerous milestones. In 2006, he performed for the Queen of England, and in 2011, his single “White Dove” (featuring Vince Gill) reached #1 on the Inspirational country music charts. That same year, his album “My Kind of Country” was named Classic Country Album of the Year by the National Traditional Country Music Association.
Read more about Nathan Stanley.
Mission Blue has quickly become one of Sonoma County's most beloved bluegrass bands,
delivering their special brand of rhythm, instrumental craft, and harmony singing. A deep well of tradition informs Mission Blue’s sets – one can expect songs from the The Stanley Brothers, Larry Sparks, Bill Monroe, Flatt & Scruggs, Mac Martin and Red Allen, as well as bluegrass innovators such as J.D. Crowe and The New South, Hot Rize, Southern Blend and The Johnson Mountain Boys. They also salt each set with reinterpretations of country hits, folk songs and ballads. Based in Sonoma County, their traditional 5-piece format features Dana Frankel on fiddle, AJ Frankel on guitar, Sam Reed on banjo, David Thiessen on mandolin, and Tom Sours on bass fiddle.
Read more about Mission Blue.

title: Watercolor Fundamentals Part 1
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Anne Millett

Date: This is a 6-class series, meeting 6 Tuesdays September 15th, 22nd, 29th, October 6th, 13th & 20th.

Time: 10:30AM-1:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$270.00

There will be a materials fee of $20 plus tax for the series.

*optional 7th and 8th classes priced separately, October 27th & November 3rd.


Watercolor Fundamentals - Part 1

This class focuses on the simple delight of mixing color with water, brushing it on paper, and watching what happens as it moves and dries. You will learn easy ways to create paintings that are all about color and the sometimes unpredictable nature of water.

No drawing skills are needed.

In this class we will explore the basic principles of watercolor painting. Learn or refresh your understanding of brush handling, brush care and setting up, the benefits of “good paper”, watercolor lights and darks, flat and graded washes, wet-on-wet techniques such as charging, wet-on-dry techniques such as glazing, color wheel, color theory, color mixing, and more. Simple applications of these techniques invite you to experiment and play.

This class is designed for adults 18+ (exceptions made for very motivated teens, please email to discuss)

class sizes are limited to 8 people, please register early

$270 for 6 classes, 2.5 hours each class

There will be a materials fee of $20 plus tax for the series.

*optional 7th and 8th classes priced separately
Payable via check, cash, or Zelle.

*Brushes, palettes, set-ups, and paint will be provided.*

description:
Instructor: Anne Millett

Date: This is a 6-class series, meeting 6 Tuesdays September 15th, 22nd, 29th, October 6th, 13th & 20th.
Time: 2:00PM-4:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
Fee: $270.00

There will be a materials fee of $20 plus tax for the series.

*optional 7th and 8th classes priced separately, October 27th & November 3rd.


Watercolor Fundamentals - Part 2

This next series will build on what we learned in Part 1, quickly refreshing some techniques and then applying them in our paintings. We will create more complex landscape paintings, skies and seascapes; wet-into-wet and wet-into-dry nature studies in a few different ways, and we will venture further into painting from our imaginations. We will explore abstraction and non-representational styles, where we don't look at something and try to paint it, but instead work intuitively with colors and shapes and let the paintings emerge and evolve from there. You don't have to know where you're going, enjoy the journey and see where it takes you!

This class is designed for adults 18+

title: Upcycled Journal Workshop — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Upcycled Journal Workshop

  
    
      
        
          $70.00
        
      
    
  

Upcycled Journal WorkshopWednesday, October 21st, 6:00-9:00pmAges 13+ Attendance $60 + Materials $10 = $70.00 Registration Fee Join us for a fun and creative workshop turning recycled cereal/snack boxes into a unique handmade journal. Students will remove parts of the boxes until we have what we will use as our cover.  Then, using miscellaneous papers, we fold these into the pages of our journals. With simple book-binding skills using a needle and waxed thread, we will stitch the pages into our covers. We will also decorate the covers of our journals with collage papers and/or paint. Examples will be shown throughout the class, and step-by-step instruction with all materials being provided, this class is great for beginners looking to get started in upcycled crafting. Short exercises to boost your creativity and journal prompts are also included. Whether you are a beginning or seasoned artist/writer/crafter, or just looking to try something new, this is a great way to get inspired and create something meaningful to you. About the Instructor: Rendell Hourigan received a BBA in Marketing from Texas Tech University, and has pursued art for over 25 years focusing on sustainable mixed media. She has studied with artists including Chery Baird, Jenny London, and Teri Slot, exploring drawing, collage, and soft pastels. She’s exhibited work at the Sebastopol Center for the Arts, The Graton Gallery, and her SOFA district studio. Drawn to the beauty of discarded materials and passionate about recycling, she incorporates reclaimed materials into her work and now leads art workshops to inspire eco-conscious creativity in others.

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Beginning Watercolor Class

description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

title: Give 'Em the Axe! Ladies Night at the Range in Santa Rosa
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
Join us for an axe-throwing session to blow off some steam. I'm super excited to be able to offer a ladies' Axe-throwing night in Santa Rosa. If you've ever had a curiosity about this fun activity, this is your chance to find out more!

We have reserved a group spot with the indoor range on a Wednesday night. It will consist of an introductory lesson, and then we all get to practice taking turns. Everyone will get ample time to practice, as they have many lanes.

This event is focused on a less-competitive, relaxed, and entertaining atmosphere. All skill levels are encouraged. All equipment and targets are provided by them, and we will probably get about 1 to 2 hours to enjoy ourselves.

I encourage everyone to bring a bottle of wine or a snack to share with the rest of the group (We usually end up with a lovely charcuterie and wine spread for everyone to enjoy).

There are 10 spots available, guests welcome. The ladies' group lesson and event is $31 per person, with $6 prepaid via Paypal and $25 paid to the range.

Please only RSVP 'Yes' if you are able to make it, hostess Daima Phipps will be collecting a $6 fee via Paypal to hold your spot. Paypal/Meetup should lead you to make your payment after you RSVP 'Yes'.

Closed-toed shoes are recommended.

There is an attendance policy for all our events: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

Cheers, and hope to see you there!

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

You can also visit Eva's website at: http://evamautner.com http://evamautner.com evamautner.com

title: Take the art of Still Life to new places
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Fridays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series, meeting 6 consecutive Fridays. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 2:30pm - 4:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with instructor for details.



This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcomed.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: What We Can Know by Ian McEwan [OPTION 1]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
***What We Can Know* by Ian McEwan**

**Ed's description**: "It is 2119, and Thomas Metcalfe is a humanities academic expert on the 90 30 era - 1990 to 2030 - when the Derangement accelerated leading eventually to the Inundation which destroyed much of the civilized world with ephemeral archives preserved in mountainous libraries while Nigeria houses ALL digital records. Thomas embarks on a hero's journey to find the long lost but legendary 'Corona for Vivien' recited by the famed poet Francis Blundy for his wife's fiftieth birthday party at an 'immortal night' with literary luminaries in 2014. In this period the STEM colleges have all the best students and facilities while Humanities colleges have the lousiest students and facilities, and Thomas hopes his finding of the corona - a poetic structure usually of seven sonnets but 15 in this case - will spark some life in his dying field. He finds Vivien's memoirs, and the second part of the novel belongs to her."

**Lucinda**: "This book was a mind bender. I never quite knew what was going on until the very end. I believe that’s the whole point. I appreciated McEwan’s views on climate decline and what it might lead to. It was thought provoking (no spoilers). I also found the book a little hard to read as it was quite detailed, and the characters might be considered amoral. There is a lot here."

**Dave**: "Intriguing novel. Pondering the future not about technological change but what will do with the vast amount of saved data. How will we encounter our history and the place for humanities in the future."

**Nancy R**: "I've started on my second reading. There's so much in the book to discuss. One thing is 100 years in the future calling global warming 'the derangement.' brilliant, among others. The story is involving and well written, and is sure to generate lively discussions."

*•* "Sophisticated entertainment of a high order." —*The New York Times*
*• "*Brilliantly, and surprisingly, plotted."—*The Washington Post •* "A novelist of consummate skill."—*The Wall Street Journal*
*•* "Elegantly structured and provocative."—*Los Angeles Times*

title: Fresh Pressed Flower Card Workshop
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Jan Lochner
Date: Saturday, October 24th
Time: 2:00PM-5:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free: $40.00

This is a hands-on make and take class where you will make at least five items including a bookmark, a greeting card, a fridge magnet and an ornament. The class will use two different techniques and Jan will explain how to press flowers and which flowers hold their color best. It is a creative experience!


To register for this workshop, please contact Jan at: mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com mailto:freshpressedflowercards@yahoo.com

Creating note cards from pressed flowers has been Jan’s hobby for 25 years, though she has no formal art training. She utilizes color,
shape and texture on fine quality paper, each card uniquely handmade. Jan’s home in Sebastopol is her studio: the dining room table is her workshop, the kitchen cupboards storing boxes and trays of flowers. She buys card stock by the thousand and picks blooms from her garden and other public places. Her family is used to me saying, “could we stop for just a few minutes so I can gather some… ”

It is a wonderful way of life.

*A note to all students: Please park on in the East facing parking lot while attending classes. We greatly appreciate it. Thank you.

title: Patrick Ball: Celtic Harp & Story
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Step into the enchanting world of
Patrick Ball
, one of the premier Celtic harp players in the world and a captivating storyteller whose performances weave music, legend, wit, and wonder into an unforgettable experience.
With the crystalline beauty of the Celtic harp as his musical voice, Ball brings ancient Irish tales and timeless melodies vividly to life, transporting audiences to a world of heroes and dreamers, mystery and mischief, heartbreak and humor. His masterful playing and gift for storytelling create an evening that is at once intimate, magical, and deeply human.
Join us at Occidental Center for the Arts for a spellbinding journey through the music and stories of Ireland with a true master of the tradition.
Tickets are $35, $30 for OCA members. Doors open at 6:30 PM, refreshments available. Art gallery open during event.
Get Tickets
About Patrick Ball:
Whether in the stronghold of a Galway chieftain in the years before history began or yesterday in the snug corner of a pub in Dublin, the Irish have always delighted in storytelling. Their passion for eloquence and wordplay, their deep devotion to their mythical past, their ability to find joy and humor in a dark world, and their belief that the supernatural world could appear between one breath and the next made their stories and the telling of them unrivaled in the world of the oral tradition.
And always, amidst the storytelling, there was music. Jigs, reels and haunting airs graced the spaces between the tales. And first among Irish instruments, and the most honored, was the legendary Celtic harp. With its crystalline, bell-like voice and lavish resonance, it would soothe its listeners and lead them deeper into the realms of the imagination.
In
Celtic Harp and Story
Patrick Ball rekindles the fire and wonder of an evening of Irish storytelling. For in telling the marvelous old tales of wit and enchantment, and in playing the ancient, brass-strung harp of Ireland, he not only carries on two of the richest traditions of Celtic culture, but blends them in concert to create “a warm and magical performance.”
“An American master of the Irish instrument, a peripatetic modern day bard, combining tale-telling, history and music into a seamless compound that reaches all ages and types of listeners.”—San Francisco Chronicle
“It’s rare that we will feature a performer on our fine performances season for two consecutive years, but then Patrick is a rare artist ... The audience was entranced by his harp playing, amused by his storytelling. Patrick is a grand man who puts on a great show.”—APAP Report / Humboldt State University
“The SRO audience loved Mr. Ball's performance, asking when we will be bringing him back. Ball was a delight to work with, very professional, and he is superb at captivating an audience.”—APAP Report / Arizona State University
“Patrick Ball conjured some Druid magic ... weaving words and music into a spellbinding program.”—The Blade, Toledo, OH

title: Readers' Theatre
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
2nd & 4th Tuesdays, 2-4 pm in the OCA Lobby
Interested in learning, sharing and reading short plays? Readers Theatre is a fun opportunity to express yourself.
Readers Theatre participants read scripts adapted from literature, while the ‘audience’ pictures the action by hearing the script being read aloud. It requires no sets, costumes, props, or memorized lines. Instead of acting literature as in a play, the performer’s goal is to read a script aloud effectively, enabling the audience to visualize the action. Performers bring the text alive by using voice, facial expressions, and some gestures. $15 participation fee, $10 for OCA members.
Alternating READER’S CHOICE nights: Can be play, poetry, story, essay, your own writing, OR ??????
For more information, email
Joan Ambrosini,
coordinator .

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Beginning Watercolor Class

description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

title: Schnucks Wine Dinner with Jeff Bundschu
description:
Schnucks Wine Dinner with Jeff Bundschu
We invite you to join Jeff Bundschu at Schnucks Des Peres in St. Louis MO on Wednesday October 28th from 6-9pm for a special wine dinner. It will be a culinary experience you won’t want to miss, delicately paired with exceptional wines and their friendly staff.

FROM THE HOST
Join us for an exclusive five-course culinary journey featuring the exceptional cool-climate estate wines of Gundlach Bundschu, Sonoma’s oldest continuously family-owned winery. The evening features sixth-generation vintner and special guest Jeff Bundschu, who will share his personal stories, deep-rooted passion, and distinctively vibrant approach to California winemaking. As each meticulously paired course unfolds, you will gain firsthand insight into the unique terroir of their historic Rhinefarm estate, their sustainable wine-growing philosophies, and the meticulous crafting process that has defined the Bundschu family legacy for nearly 170 years.

MENU

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting March 2025, we ask that every attending member pay a $1 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!

location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Sandra Novia

Dates: Fridays, Ongoing. This is an ongoing 6-class series, meeting 6 consecutive Fridays. You can start your series anytime.

Time: 2:30pm - 4:30pm.

Location : Santa Rosa Store

Fee: $310 for 6 classes. Please check with instructor for details.



This class is for art explorers of all levels!

Creating a still life is about waking up your observational skills. Moving through different mediums, we will embark on a journey together, exploring how to apply many art forms and techniques to express what you see in life.

In this six week course, each class will explore a different art medium. We will draw and paint with graphite, watercolor pencils and acrylic. We will expand on those mediums as we move into printmaking, collage, and mosaic to bring your art to life. It's a great class to learn the fundamentals for beginners and for experienced artists that want to try their hand at a new art form you haven't done before.

All levels Welcomed.

Let's explore the beautiful art of expressing Art together.


To register for this series, please contact Sandra Novia at: (707) 433-ARTS (2787)

title: What We Can Know by Ian McEwan [OPTION 2]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
***What We Can Know* by Ian McEwan**

**Ed's description**: "It is 2119, and Thomas Metcalfe is a humanities academic expert on the 90 30 era - 1990 to 2030 - when the Derangement accelerated leading eventually to the Inundation which destroyed much of the civilized world with ephemeral archives preserved in mountainous libraries while Nigeria houses ALL digital records. Thomas embarks on a hero's journey to find the long lost but legendary 'Corona for Vivien' recited by the famed poet Francis Blundy for his wife's fiftieth birthday party at an 'immortal night' with literary luminaries in 2014. In this period the STEM colleges have all the best students and facilities while Humanities colleges have the lousiest students and facilities, and Thomas hopes his finding of the corona - a poetic structure usually of seven sonnets but 15 in this case - will spark some life in his dying field. He finds Vivien's memoirs, and the second part of the novel belongs to her."

**Lucinda**: "This book was a mind bender. I never quite knew what was going on until the very end. I believe that’s the whole point. I appreciated McEwan’s views on climate decline and what it might lead to. It was thought provoking (no spoilers). I also found the book a little hard to read as it was quite detailed, and the characters might be considered amoral. There is a lot here."

**Dave**: "Intriguing novel. Pondering the future not about technological change but what will do with the vast amount of saved data. How will we encounter our history and the place for humanities in the future."

**Nancy R**: "I've started on my second reading. There's so much in the book to discuss. One thing is 100 years in the future calling global warming 'the derangement.' brilliant, among others. The story is involving and well written, and is sure to generate lively discussions."

*•* "Sophisticated entertainment of a high order." —*The New York Times*
\*• "\*Brilliantly, and surprisingly, plotted."—*The Washington Post •* "A novelist of consummate skill."—*The Wall Street Journal*
*•* "Elegantly structured and provocative."—*Los Angeles Times*

title: The Art of Acrylics
description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson
Wednesday, Ongoing
10:00AM-12:00PM
Location: Santa Rosa Store
$30.00 per class

Suzanne will demo each week as students follow along with weekly projects, exploring techniques such as layering thick and thin paint, using gels and palette knife, and applying color theories. Students can work on their own projects as well.

Whether you're a beginner or looking to refine your skills, this class covers everything you need to know. You'll get informed instruction on how to begin a piece, from choosing the right materials to selecting the perfect color palette. We’ll dive into composition techniques to help you craft a balanced, captivating piece, and walk you through the finishing touches that bring your work to life.

Suzanne's artwork ranges from portraits, figurative genre, landscapes and caricatures. She has exhibited in juried shows including The Society of Illustrators in New York and for 10 years at the Southern California Laguna Beach Art Festival. She has taught classes and workshops for many years and led lecture-demos at art associations from California to Washington State.

For enrollment and supply list, please text or call Suzanne Carson at 707 888 2083

title: Beginning Watercolor Class
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,1138 4th St, San Rafael, CA 94901, USA
description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner
  * Fee: $60 per class or $220 for 4 classes
  * Days & Times: Wednesdays & Fridays, 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM
  * SAN RAFAEL LOCATION ONLY

Learning Objectives:

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work
  * Navigate the entire painting process, from choosing colors to building layers

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Selecting and using brushes
  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
  * Capturing shapes and light in your work
  * Creating solid underdrawings
  * Applying wet-on-wet techniques

Join us and experience the satisfaction of producing your own watercolor masterpieces. Register now and save with our early registration discount!

For more information or to register for this class, please contact Eva at: evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com mailto:evamautner@gmail.com

You can also visit Eva's website at: http://evamautner.com http://evamautner.com evamautner.com

Let's make beautiful art together!

title: Pilot Parallel Pen Demonstration: Doodles to Cadels
description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: Jizo Peace Project: Clay Gathering for Remembrance and Peace, November — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Jizo Peace Project: Clay Gathering for Remembrance and Peace, November

  
    
      
        
          $10.00
        
      
    
  

Friday, November 6, 2026; 1:30 – 4:00pmDue to limited capacity, we are asking for a suggested donation of $10 to the Sebastopol Center for the Arts to confirm your attendance. Bring a copy of your receipt at check-in to Painting/Drawing Studio adjacent to Ceramics Studio. Additional donations are welcome at the time of the class to cover rental and expenses for the peace project. Join us for a monthly, heart-centered gathering where we come together to create Jizo guardians out of clay—symbols of compassion, protection, and peace. Rooted in the Buddhist tradition and echoed across many cultures, Jizo figures traditionally honor children and all who have passed, those in transition, and those in distress.This ongoing project is dedicated to remembering those lost to war, with a special focus now on the approximately 19,000 children who have perished in Israel and Gaza in recent years. Through the simple, meditative act of working with clay, we create benevolent beings that will become part of public exhibits and peace sites, offering spaces for reflection, mourning, and hope. Our gatherings conclude with a gentle ritual to honor the lives of these children.Located in the Painting & Drawing Room. The gathering is open to ages 12 - adult, and no prior clay experience is necessary—all clay and basic materials are supplied. Registration is required to participate.Donations are welcome to help cover materials and expenses. More than a class, this is a shared space of warmth and care—an opportunity to tend to our own hearts while taking part in love in action.

description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner

  * Get acquainted with basic watercolor materials and tools
  * Master the ‘wet on wet’ watercolor technique
  * Learn the fundamentals of layering color and creating shadows
  * Build confidence and find joy in the creative process
  * Create and label a swatch of colors
  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them
  * Masking border edges for clean finishes
  * Develop tight underdrawings to guide your work

  * Layering and drying techniques
  * Building and placing colors effectively
  * Understanding complementary colors
